bends.description: New bend records for this part — a spec change: sheet lanes requote with exactly these bends (the list REPLACES the previous one, never patches it). Same shape as on get_fabrication_quote: each bend is two points in the part's own mm frame (flat DXF parts use z=0) plus angle_deg, direction up|down, and an optional requested radius_mm. Pass null to REMOVE every articulated bend

anyOf.description: Tapped (threaded) holes for a sheet-metal or CNC-machined part — one record per hole the user wants threads cut into. `thread` is the callout in the user's words ("M6", "M4 x 0.7", "1/4-20") and is all that's required; when known, add the hole's center in the part's own mm frame (located_at_mm), its unit axis, the pre-tap drilled diameter, and depth_mm so the shop taps the right hole. Same shape as on get_fabrication_quote: thread callout ("M6", "1/4-20") required, hole geometry optional. Pass null to REMOVE every tap

inserts.description: New hardware-insert records for this part — a spec change: sheet lanes requote with exactly these inserts (the list REPLACES the previous one, never patches it). Same shape as on get_fabrication_quote: species (nut|flush_nut|standoff|blind_standoff|stud) and thread required, hole geometry optional. Pass null to REMOVE every insert

quantities.description: New quantities the user wants (spec change — lanes requote at the new quantity). Same rules as on get_fabrication_quote: pass the real ask, never inflate it. Pass null to REMOVE a previously asked quantity — the quote returns to single-part pricing

scale.description: Rescale the DESIGN ITSELF before re-quoting: per-axis stretch factors over the file's current geometry ("make it 2x bigger" = {"x":2,"y":2,"z":2}). Mesh designs are genuinely converted — the child quote prices a rescaled file; STEP/IGES designs keep their original file with the dimensions riding as callouts (pass those too). {1,1,1} is a no-op

processes.description: Narrow this quote to specific fabrication processes ("no, I meant in sheet metal" → ["sheet metal"]). A CONSTRAINT, not a new quote: excluded lanes drop while warm vendor sessions survive, and further refines inherit the filter. Friendly terms accepted ("sheet metal", "3d printing", "cnc", "laser"); pass ["any"] to clear the filter and show every process again. When comparison scenarios are open and the user narrows the process, re-refine EVERY active scenario label with this same arg so all columns prune together. ships_from.description: Only vendors that ship from these countries/regions ("only US vendors", "just European shops", "keep it domestic") — an INCLUDE list naming where the user DOES want vendors from. A CONSTRAINT like processes: non-matching vendors drop instantly (nothing re-prices), further refines inherit the filter, and ["any"] clears it to show vendors everywhere again. Friendly terms accepted ("US", "Europe", "Germany", "China", "UK"). Vendors whose origin is unknown or whose network is worldwide (a specific origin cannot be guaranteed) are excluded, each with an honest note. For "nothing from X" asks, pass the regions the user does want instead

vendors_exclude.description: Shops to leave out ("anyone but Slant 3D", "not A3D or Fictiv") — shop names as they appear on offers; friendly names accepted ("A3D", "slant 3d"), and a name that matches no shop is reported, never an error. A shop on this list is never asked and never shown. Works beside vendors: the shops shown are the vendors list (or everyone) minus this list, so a shop named on both is left out. Usually OMIT: pass it only when the user names shops they do not want. On a refine: naming more shops answers at once from what the quote holds (no shop is asked); ["any"] or clear ["vendors_exclude"] removes the list, and the shops that come back are priced then

vendors_exact.description: How the names in vendors and vendors_exclude are read. Usually OMIT: a name then reaches every connector of the shop it names ("SendCutSend" covers its sheet, laser and CNC connectors), which is what a person means by a shop. ai.agenticfabricationnetwork/ufp.name: reopen_quote
ai.agenticfabricationnetwork/ufp.description: Use when the user comes back to a part priced earlier (a saved quote_id), or when a quote carried answers_pending. A quote's answers are shown for 24 hours. Inside them this returns the same quote and asks nobody (reopened "same"). Past them it makes a NEW quote of the same file, configuration, rules and pick — work from the quote_id it returns: with the answers anyone got for this same part and request in the last 24 hours ("copied", nobody asked); else by asking the shops once ("asked" — the offers fill in like any new quote); else, when someone is asking about it right now, at our instant prices ("waiting": call this again after answers_pending.retry_after_s seconds). "press_needed" = this quote was itself made by reopening an old one and nothing was picked or changed on it since, so nobody is asked again by itself: pass pressed true only when the user asks for today's prices. A quote of a shared cart, a part already paid for, or instant prices only comes back as it reads. Do not use it to look at a board again. HOW OLD AN ANSWER IS: a shop's answer is shown for 24 hours, to everyone with the same request (the same design bytes with the same everything asked), so a quote of a part someone priced in the last 24 hours comes back complete at once with those answers and no shop is asked again. An offer says when its shop answered (answered_at). Past 15 minutes it reads stale: true — it is shown at that price and the shop confirms it again before anyone pays (check_offer, or checking out, asks that one shop). A shipping option of such an offer carries eta_approximate: true: say "about N days" from eta_days and never state its eta_date as a date, because no shop stands behind a date until it confirms again. If a quote carries answers_pending, someone else is asking the shops about this same request right now and these are our instant prices: call reopen_quote with that quote_id after retry_after_s seconds.

pressed.description: true = the user asked for today's prices. Needed only after reopened read "press_needed"

ai.agenticfabricationnetwork/ufp.name: poll_quote
ai.agenticfabricationnetwork/ufp.description: INTERNAL — the offer board calls this to refresh itself while vendors finish pricing. Never call this yourself. The board you were given is already final for its turn; do not reach for refine_quote to look at it again either, that paints a duplicate board. An offer's manufacturability_check (status checking → passed | failed, expected_s; "repriced" reads as passed) means the price is set; the shop is confirming it can make the part as drawn; the board renders it.

quote_id.description: Quote id the board is watching

ai.agenticfabricationnetwork/ufp.name: finalize_quote
ai.agenticfabricationnetwork/ufp.description: ONLY for the case where a quote response came back with an EMPTY board and told you to call this: waits for the vendors to answer (up to ~40s) and returns their offers as a full board. Call with just quote_id, immediately, and say nothing substantive before it. NEVER call it on a response that already listed offers — that board is final, and this would add nothing.

quote_id.description: Quote id from the still-quoting response

ai.agenticfabricationnetwork/ufp.name: create_checkout
ai.agenticfabricationnetwork/ufp.description: Create checkout for one chosen offer and shipping speed. Hosted payment is the default. Call this after the user chooses the offer and shipping speed. This tool takes NO personal details: never ask for — and never pass — a name, address, email, or phone; the secure payment page collects the shipping address, email, and phone (and billing) itself, even when the user volunteered them in chat. In hosted-payment mode, returns checkout_url — the AFN's order page (what is being made, by which shop, the all-in price) with a Continue to payment button to the secure hosted payment page; give the link to the user. UFP places the vendor order automatically after payment. An offer whose shop still has to confirm it (manufacturability_check.status "unchecked", or confirmed more than 15 minutes ago) is confirmed by this call itself, and one whose status is "checking" is waited for (the price is set; the shop is confirming it can make the part as drawn) — no separate check_offer call. Pass max_total_cents: the price the user agreed to (the offer's subtotal_cents plus the chosen shipping cost_cents). THE CHECKOUT RULE, enforced by the network for every client: an offer can be ordered only when the shop's own system has accepted this part at this price — its manufacturability check has passed, the price is the shop's own number (price_basis "vendor_api"), and no price confirmation is outstanding. That acceptance is good for 15 minutes (the offer's confirmed_until). THE CHECKOUT CONFIRMS WHAT NEEDS CONFIRMING ITSELF: when the option's shop has not confirmed it, or did more than 15 minutes ago, the checkout asks that ONE shop (it joins the ask already running when choosing the option started one) and waits up to wait_s for the answer; when the wait runs out first the answer is offer_not_ready with retry_after_s — send the SAME call again, it joins the ask and nothing is asked twice. THE PAY RULE: when the confirmed total is at or below the amount the user agreed to, checkout uses the selected payment method (hosted payment by default, or the saved card when pay is saved on a keyed connection); a price the shop confirmed HIGHER than the user agreed to stops ONCE (price_went_up, with old_total_cents and new_total_cents) and nothing is created — tell the user both figures, then send the call again (with the new max_total_cents when you sent one); the new price stands for 15 minutes and no shop is asked again. A passed offer whose price_refresh is still "pending" is refused the same way (offer_not_ready, with retry_after_s): the shop is still confirming its price — re-read the quote and retry then. An offer whose check failed, whose price_refresh reads "failed", or whose fulfillment is "not_connected" cannot be ordered at all (offer_check_failed) — offer the user another option or re-quote. Nothing is charged on any refusal. An offer whose shop could not confirm the part — it declined the part, or did not answer within two minutes of being asked — leaves the quote: it is no longer listed in offers, and its id is refused the same way. If an offer you showed earlier is missing when you re-read the quote, tell the user plainly that the shop could not confirm the part, and carry on with the offers that are listed. ORDER BY THE PICK: instead of offer_id + shipping_option_id, pass quote_id with selection true to order the one option the quote's stored pick comes to (the quote's selection_match). It orders only when that reads status "one"; with none or several it is refused (selection_not_unique, saying how many matched) and nothing is created — say more in the pick with refine_quote selection, then call again. When the pick names a shipping speed the option does not show right now (selection_match.speed_fallback) it is refused too (selection_speed_unavailable): the cheapest speed is never ordered in its place — store the pick with a speed the option lists. An offer_id or shipping speed the quote's own rules keep off its board (the acceptable-materials list, within_days) is refused the same way: order what the quote lists now. So the whole of it is two calls: refine_quote with the pick (its one shop starts confirming), then create_checkout with quote_id and selection true — the selected checkout result, price_went_up once, or offer_not_ready (call again). The checkout rule above applies to the picked option exactly as to any other. TO PLACE EXACTLY ONE ORDER WITH NO MISTAKES: (1) on get_fabrication_quote list only that shop in vendors and state the pick in selection — the shop, plus the material, finish and shipping speed wanted; (2) read selection_match on the quote: status "one" means exactly one option answers the pick, "many" means say more in the pick (color, thickness, quantity), "none" means nothing on the quote answers it; (3) call create_checkout with quote_id and selection true — it orders that one option at the picked shipping speed, or refuses and creates nothing (selection_not_unique: the pick is not exactly one option; selection_speed_unavailable: the option does not show the picked speed now — an order never takes another speed in its place). only_selected.description: true = order the parts that have a pick and leave the rest in the cart. Default: a part with nothing picked refuses the whole cart

coupon.description: Coupon code, only if the user provided one. Applied once to the cart total. Never invent or guess a code.

check.description: Default true: each picked part whose shop has to confirm it is confirmed by this call (one shop per part), which waits for the answers (wait_s). false = ask nobody and judge the cart as it stands. Usually OMIT

wait_s.description: Seconds this call may wait for the shops (default 45). When it runs out first the cart is refused with the waiting parts named — send the same call again

max_total_cents.description: The most the user agreed to pay for the cart, in cents, before any coupon: the cart's total_cents as you showed it. At or under it the checkout is made; a higher confirmed total is refused once (price_went_up) and nothing is created. Leave it out and the network compares with the prices it last told this cart's reader

return_url.description: Exact URL of the page the user is on right now, IF the client application knows it. The page after payment shows a 'Return to <site>' button pointing here. Omit when unknown — never invent one.

ai.agenticfabricationnetwork/ufp.name: get_order_status
ai.agenticfabricationnetwork/ufp.description: Check status, ETA and tracking for a UFP order. Pass a checkout id (co_…, from checkout_cart) in order_id to get every order of that cart checkout at once — each part is its own order with its own shop, status and tracking. The answer carries status_url: a link the user can open or pass on to follow the order with no sign-in; it shows progress only (no price, no address, nothing that can change the order).

order_id.description: The order (ord_…), or a cart checkout (co_…) to read all of its orders

ai.agenticfabricationnetwork/ufp.name: reply_to_maker
ai.agenticfabricationnetwork/ufp.description: Send the user's answer to a question the maker (vendor) asked about a UFP order — get_order_status surfaces an open question when one is waiting. Confirm the answer with the user before sending. The network relays it: the maker sees plain text from the network account with the user's contact details and links stripped, so never include emails, phone numbers, or URLs the answer depends on.

order_id.description: The UFP order the maker asked about (ord_…)

message.description: The user's answer, in their words — it is relayed to the maker

ai.agenticfabricationnetwork/ufp.name: leave_review
ai.agenticfabricationnetwork/ufp.description: Record the user's verified-purchase review of how a UFP order turned out. YOUR JOB IS TO STRUCTURE THE FEEDBACK: turn what the user actually said into stars (1-5 overall) and facet scores — "the cut was sloppy" -> quality, "parts arrived 2 days late" -> timeliness, "wrong color" -> accuracy. Keep the optional comment to a short factual summary of their words; never embellish. ALWAYS draft the review (stars, facets, comment) and confirm it with the user BEFORE calling this tool — e.g. "I'll rate this 2 stars with timeliness 1 because it arrived 2 days late — send it?". One review per order: submitting again updates the existing review. If you do not have the order id from this conversation, ask the user for it (it is on their receipt email and order page); never guess one.

order_id.description: The UFP order being reviewed (ord_…), from create_checkout or get_order_status in this conversation, or from the user's receipt email / order page

comment.description: Short factual summary of the user's feedback, in their spirit — optional

timeliness.description: Delivery speed vs the quoted ETA

accuracy.description: How well the item matched the ordered spec/design

facets.description: Score only the facets the user actually spoke to

received_material.description: Material the user says actually ARRIVED, when they complain it differs from the order ("they sent aluminum")

received_quantity.description: Count the user says actually arrived, when it differs from the order

delivery_claim.description: The user's delivery claim ("never showed up" -> not_delivered)

claims.description: CHECKABLE claims from the user's feedback — the network stamps each against its own records (the ordered spec, polled tracking + delivery events) and attaches evidence chips to the review. Only pass what the user actually asserted.

ai.agenticfabricationnetwork/ufp.name: get_material_guide
ai.agenticfabricationnetwork/ufp.description: Honest, cited material intelligence for material-choice / strength / durability / heat / outdoor questions ("my PLA part broke, what's stronger?", "will this survive outdoors?"). Returns caveats-FIRST facts: published specs (tensile, heat-deflection, UV/outdoor, chemical) each tagged vendor-cited vs general engineering knowledge, "stronger/tougher/hotter than X" ladders (PLA→PETG→ABS/ASA→nylon/PC→metals), and finish/coating options. Call it BEFORE answering such a question, then relay the facts. It supplies FACTS ONLY — comparative specs and vendor-admitted caveats, never a fitness-for-purpose or safety guarantee (that stays your judgment boundary); name express vendor claims "advertised", not "certified".

material.description: A material the user named or you are weighing ("PLA", "6061 aluminum", "stainless") — free-form; a family ask like "stainless" returns the whole family

process.description: A UFP process to scope to ("fdm_print", "resin_print", "cnc", "sheetmetal", "laser_cut") — lists the materials that process makes

question.description: The user's raw question — mined for intent (stronger/tougher, heat/hot, outdoor/UV) so the right ladder is surfaced

ai.agenticfabricationnetwork/ufp.name: get_network_capabilities
ai.agenticfabricationnetwork/ufp.description: The LIVE catalog of what the fabrication network can do RIGHT NOW — no quote needed. Returns the services ledger (tapping, inserts, welding, bending, finishes… with each shop's own size/material/thickness windows), the network's sheet gauge ladder, the stocked hardware combinations (species x thread) with stocked lengths and shop counts — the most-stocked length is the steering default for an unspecified length — the finish options with their stocked color menus, every colour the network can make a part in (network_catalog.colors: per colour family, how many shops stock a material in it and how many coat in it, with the shades — ask for one by passing the family word as `color` with no finish), the material groups a picker shows (network_catalog.material_groups: Plastics, Metals, Woods, Foams, Rubbers, Composites, Paper cork and fabric… with the stock families live under each and the words that ask for them), and per-process manufacturability rules. This is live state, not a spec sheet: it changes as connectors join, leave, or have capability branches toggled, so call it fresh when the user asks what's possible (materials, gauges, hardware, colors, services) rather than answering from memory. PICKER COUNTS: pass `selection` (what the user has already picked: processes, materials, thickness_in, colors, finishes, finish_colors, vendors, vendors_exclude, each a list where any value will do) and the answer adds network_catalog.facets: for every material group and member, gauge rung, colour family, finish and finish colour the catalog lists, `shops` = how many shops the user can order from today declare they make the whole selection plus that option, and `maybe` = further shops whose catalog is silent on part of it (they might); each count sets that dimension's own picks aside. Only an option with shops 0 AND maybe 0 is impossible with the selection; never read a missing count as zero. facets.shops answers each shop against the selection (yes / no / unknown). The counts come from the shops' declared catalogs, nobody is contacted, and nothing on a quote changes. Without `selection` the answer is the same as before.

process.description: Advisory scope ("sheetmetal") — v1 returns the whole catalog either way; filter what you relay

selection.description: What is already picked, in a quote's own words, e.g. { "materials": ["acrylic"], "colors": ["green"], "vendors": ["SendCutSend"] }. When present the answer adds network_catalog.facets (shop counts per option for this selection). Add "vendors_exact": true only when the shop lists hold offer `vendor` slugs that must each mean that one connector (a name otherwise covers every connector of the shop). Omit it for the plain catalog

ai.agenticfabricationnetwork/ufp.name: get_shop_offerings
ai.agenticfabricationnetwork/ufp.description: What ONE named shop sells right now, read live off the shop's own declared catalog: per process, every stock with its own colours and thicknesses, and every finish with the stocks it goes on and its colours. No quote needed, nobody is contacted, and the user's board does not change. Call it when the user asks what a specific maker offers ("what colours of acrylic does SendCutSend have?", "what else do they do?"). One shop name covers every process it sells. A stock listed with no colours means the shop does not list colours for it, never that it has none. Never answer such a question from the offers on a quote (they show what was offered for one ask, not everything the shop sells) and never from memory.

shop.description: The shop as the user or the offer cards name it ("SendCutSend", "sendcutsend")

material.description: Narrow the list to one material or family ("acrylic", "mild steel")

ai.agenticfabricationnetwork/ufp.name: get_shop_gauges
ai.agenticfabricationnetwork/ufp.description: Every sheet thickness (gauge) ONE named shop stocks right now, per material — read live off the shop's declared catalog, no quote needed. Call it when the user asks what thicknesses/gauges a specific maker carries ("what thicknesses does SendCutSend have in mild steel?"). For the whole network's ladder use get_network_capabilities instead. Never answer a gauge question from memory.

shop.description: The shop as the user or the offer cards name it ("SendCutSend", "sendcutsend")

material.description: Advisory: narrow the relayed list to one material ("mild steel", "5052")

ai.agenticfabricationnetwork/ufp.name: get_price_curve
ai.agenticfabricationnetwork/ufp.description: How the per-unit price moves with quantity for a quote you already have: for every shop on the board, the item price per unit at each quantity (default 1, 2, 5, 10, 25, 50, 100, 250, 500, 1000; pass up to 16 of your own in 1..10000) from that shop's own pricing with the network's markup included, plus its arrival window — instant, no shop is contacted, nothing changes on the quote. Call it when the user asks what more or fewer pieces would cost ("what would 50 run me?", "any price breaks?"). The board's quoted price stays the ceiling at the chosen quantity (each option's `live` row); a null cell means that shop's pricing does not cover that quantity — refine_quote with the new quantities gets the real number. Present these as the shops' own pricing, never as an estimate; every order still passes the manufacturability check.

quote_id.description: The quote whose board to price by quantity

ai.agenticfabricationnetwork/ufp.name: check_offer
ai.agenticfabricationnetwork/ufp.description: Ask the shop to confirm one unchecked or checking offer. Use this when the user wants the check result before deciding. create_checkout and checkout_cart ask or join the check themselves for the selected option, so this is not a required pre-check. A passed result is orderable at the shown price for 15 minutes. A repriced result confirms that same shop price; do not say the price changed. A failed result cannot be ordered and the offer is removed from the quote; tell the user and continue with the listed offers. Wait up to wait_s (default 45); pending: true means the shop is still answering, so re-read the quote shortly. Nothing else on the quote changes. On an instant-only quote (routing.instant_only true) no shop is asked; relay that result and quote again without instant_only if the user wants to order. On a lazy quote (routing.lazy true) this call is how a shop is asked at all: it asks this offer's shop, and the offer can be ordered once it passes. A shop's confirmation of an offer is good for 15 minutes: while it stands the offer carries confirmed_until (an ISO time) and can be ordered. After it the offer is NOT failed and NOT removed — it keeps its place and the price the shop last confirmed, and its manufacturability_check reads status "unchecked" with reason "confirmation_lapsed". CHOOSING STARTS THAT SHOP'S CHECK: when the user settles on an option and you store the pick, that one shop is asked again by itself (the answer's selection_match.check reads "running"), and create_checkout and checkout_cart ask it themselves too when it still needs confirming — nobody else is asked, and no separate check_offer call is needed. Pay when it lands: the checkout waits for it. If the shop's price came back higher than the user agreed to, the checkout stops ONCE (price_went_up, with the old and the new figure) and nothing is created: tell the user both figures, then send the same call again. An offer whose manufacturability_check reads status "unchecked" with reason "network_restarted" was being confirmed by its shop when the network restarted, so the answer never came: tell the user, in these words, "A new version of AFN has been released, please refresh the page". Nothing is lost — the price stands and the offer can simply be checked again with check_offer. Say it once, when a tool's own text tells you to; the same reason still on an offer on a later read is history, not news.

quote_id.description: The quote the offer belongs to

offer_id.description: The offer to have the shop confirm

wait_s.description: Seconds to wait for the shop (default 45)

ai.agenticplug/agent-ready-report.name: scan_website
ai.agenticplug/agent-ready-report.description: Scan a public website and report how ready it is for AI agents and AI search: which checks pass, which are missing, and what each check is, in plain English and technically. Covers 35 checks in three groups: agent readiness (robots.txt and AI crawler rules, sitemap, Link headers, DNS-AID, markdown for agents, Content Signals, API catalog, OAuth discovery, auth.md, MCP server card, A2A agent card, agent skills, WebMCP, ARD), agentic commerce (x402, MPP, UCP, ACP, AP2; scored only for sites that sell online), and AI search foundations (HTTPS, AI crawler access, indexability, content without JavaScript, heading structure, title and description, canonical URL, structured data, business identity markup, language, response time). Use when someone asks whether their website is ready for AI agents, AI search, ChatGPT, Claude, Perplexity, Muse or agentic commerce. A scan takes 5 to 30 seconds.

url.description: The website to scan, e.g. "example.com" or "https://www.example.com".

sells_online.description: Whether the site sells online. "auto" detects it from the homepage; use "yes" or "no" when the owner has said.

detail.description: "standard": findings with plain-English and technical explanations. "full": adds pass criteria, request-by-request evidence and source links.

ai.agenticplug/agent-ready-report.name: explain_check
ai.agenticplug/agent-ready-report.description: Explain one agent-readiness check in depth: what it is, why it matters for AI agents and AI search, exactly how the scanner tests it, what counts as a pass, and the official sources. Call with no check_id to list every check.

check_id.description: The check's id, as shown in a scan report (e.g. "dnsAid", "aiCrawlerAccess"). Omit to list all checks.

ai.agenticterminal/directory.name: search_merchants
ai.agenticterminal/directory.description: Search OP-verified merchants by rail, chain, category, agent-callable tier, trust tier, and free text. Ranked by trust tier then verification recency.

ai.agenticterminal/directory.name: get_merchant
ai.agenticterminal/directory.description: Get the full record for one merchant including all rails, payment endpoints, and OP attestation. Tier 2+ requires an AT credential.

ai.agenticterminal/directory.name: verify_payment_endpoint
ai.agenticterminal/directory.description: Run a live check against a merchant's declared payment endpoint for a rail. Returns health, detail, and rail-specific evidence.

ai.agenticterminal/directory.name: list_categories
ai.agenticterminal/directory.description: List the category taxonomy with merchant counts.

ai.agenticterminal/directory.name: list_rails
ai.agenticterminal/directory.description: List supported payment rails and their current merchant counts.

ai.agenticterminal/directory.name: whoami
ai.agenticterminal/directory.description: Report the resolved credential state and rate limits for the calling agent.

ai.agentlookups/counterscript.name: drug_price
ai.agentlookups/counterscript.description: Looks up what US pharmacies actually pay to acquire a drug (the CMS NADAC benchmark, per unit, with its date; for a pen, syringe, autoinjector or cartridge priced per mL whose description states what one holds, nadac.per_container gives the price of one, with container, ml and usd, as candidates and biosimilars do; box sizes are not in the data, so no fill estimate follows), a fair cash-price estimate range, FDA generic equivalents, and Medicare negotiated prices where they apply (medicare_negotiated_prices: one entry per year, including a year CMS has announced, with effective_date, price_30d for a 30-day equivalent supply, and per_unit where the NDCs share one). The input is a drug name with optional strength and form. result_type is one of three values. match: one drug, with prices, provenance and honesty notes; a brand-name drug with no generic alternatives listed also carries generic_equivalence, a dated statement of what the FDA Orange Book shows for it, with its ingredient where the file names one (status no_orange_book_match means our match did not pair the product with a listing, which says nothing either way about generics). A brand-name match can also carry cms_generic_price, CMS's NADAC figure for the corresponding generic drug, with its effective date, a fair cash estimate where a fill quantity applies, and the generic's name when exactly one generic in the index has that price, strength and ingredient. A biologic that the FDA Purple Book lists biosimilars to also carries biosimilars (each with proprietary and proper names, interchangeable, marketing_status, file_month, and a NADAC price where one is indexed) and biosimilars_statement; a biosimilar carries reference_product, with the same kinds of fields and a statement. candidates: the query fits several drugs. Up to 12 are listed, each with its description and price hint, in this order: the drug named on its own first, then combinations with other drugs, then longer names that hold the word (esomeprazole for omeprazole); generics before brands, then alphabetical with doses in number order (2.5 mg before 10 mg), within each. A number in the query matches only that whole number, so a query for 5 mg does not list 2.5 mg or 15 mg; within each group, drugs that hold every query word whole come first. candidates_total gives how many drugs matched; when that is more than 12, message says the list was cut, and adding a strength or form narrows it. A query equal to one candidate's description returns that drug as a match. no_match: the index has no drug matching the query; this does not mean the drug lacks a fair price, since NADAC covers only drugs with enough pharmacy survey data. did_you_mean, where present, lists drug names to search next, and did_you_mean_basis gives the reason: spelling (the name the query spells, apart from spaces and punctuation, without a dose the index lacks, or names beginning with it; a number typed with no unit is part of the name unless the words before it are a drug name, so vanacof 2 does not get vanacof dm, and stays part of it, whatever the basis, where catalog names put a number of their own after those words or an FDA label name holds it, so vagistat 3, a miconazole kit, does not get tioconazole of VAGISTAT-1, nor sore throat 911, a potassium lotion, the phenol SORE THROAT; for a trade name that is its only active ingredient plus more words, such as theophylline-sr, that ingredient), same_ingredient (the index has no drug under the ingredient name in the query, and the names are priced brands whose only active ingredient in the FDA Orange Book is that ingredient, or, for a biologic, priced brands whose proper (ingredient) name in the FDA Purple Book is that name, such as trulicity for dulaglutide; message adds a sentence naming the catalog and its file; store brands of the ingredient may still be priced under their own names) or generic_name (the index has no drug under the brand name in the query; the one name is that brand's active ingredient, or its ingredients joined by "and", in the FDA Orange Book, such as tamsulosin hydrochloride for flomax, and searching it lists the priced products with it; message adds a sentence naming the file; the name is an ingredient, not a statement that any product is a substitute; a pack name a maker's label gives a brand counts as that brand, so z-pak, Pfizer's pack of Zithromax 250 mg tablets, gets azithromycin; a name current FDA labels use for other drugs gets none, so midol, ibuprofen in the Orange Book but acetaminophen, caffeine and pyrilamine on its label, gets no hint, nor does allay, a discontinued hydrocodone combination whose only current label is a sunscreen; and leading words of a trade name that begin a priced name of another drug get none, so 8 hour, of the discontinued aspirin 8-HOUR BAYER, is not aspirin, since the index prices 8 HOUR ACETAMINOPHEN ER; and leading words that are no name of a drug get none: three letters or fewer, such as cap of CAP-PROFEN (epi, short for epinephrine, aside), and everyday words such as extended or junior, of EXTENDED PHENYTOIN SODIUM and JUNIOR STRENGTH ADVIL). A query that finds nothing as typed is read again: with a hyphen between a number and a word as a space, so 8-hour finds what 8 hour finds; with a bracketed part's brackets dropped, then with the part left out, such as eliquis for "eliquis (apixaban)"; and as a label writes a drug name, so a salt finds NADAC's short form or a description without it (sertraline hydrochloride finds SERTRALINE HCL) and amoxicillin and clavulanate potassium finds AMOX-CLAV. A name the FDA Orange Book or Purple Book lists that no description holds as whole words beginning its first or second word finds nothing, so ranexa gets its ingredient rather than TRANEXAMIC ACID. No name is guessed from a misspelling: did_you_mean holds no name with letters the query lacks or changes (lipiter gets none), since a real name a letter or two from another is often a different drug (afrin is not errin). A spelling hint is a search aid, not an equivalent medicine. Every result also carries freshness, one entry per source (nadac, orangebook, mfp, purplebook) giving as_of, the publisher's date on the file in use (for purplebook, which FDA dates by month, the first day of that month); checked, the date of our newest successful fetch of that source; expected, the publishing cadence (weekly, monthly or irregular); and stale, which is true when the NADAC file is more than 10 days old, the Orange Book file more than 45 days old or the month of the Purple Book file ended more than 60 days ago, or when our newest attempt to fetch that source failed (last_attempt_failed then gives that attempt's date, and the file in use is the newest good one we hold), and then statement says so in plain words. For mfp, whose updates are irregular, stale is true only after a failed fetch. A source we have not fetched yet has no as_of or checked.

query.description: Drug name with optional strength/form, e.g. "atorvastatin 20 mg" or "eliquis 5 mg tablet". Generic (ingredient) names match best.

ai.agentlookups/groundrules.name: law_for_location
ai.agentlookups/groundrules.description: Resolve an address or lat/lon to its full jurisdiction stack: federal, state, county, place, each with its code sources (name, publisher, official URL, current-through, whether we host its text). Unincorporated areas get the county code with no city code; about half of US municipalities publish no code online, and the answer says so and points at where the code lives if anywhere.

address.description: One-line street address

ai.agentlookups/groundrules.name: law_search
ai.agentlookups/groundrules.description: Search original law by topic, question, or citation. Exact citations resolve directly. Scoped by jurisdiction or source ids (e.g. us, us-tx; us-cfr scopes to the CFR alone, us covers both the US Code and the CFR) or by an address (the address is resolved first, then the search covers exactly its stack's hosted sources). Results are verbatim snippets with citation, official source URL, retrieval time, and a current-through or vintage label adjacent to every snippet; a hit whose source has fallen behind its upstream carries stale:true. Vintage-labeled text is a dated snapshot, not current law. meaning_only:true means no section matched a word of the query, so every hit is only the nearest in meaning and may be unrelated. Requested ids we do not host are named in the response note; law_coverage lists what is hosted.

address.description: One-line street address to auto-scope the search; pass this or jurisdictions, not both

include_text.description: Include full text for up to this many top results (0 by default; sections over 64KB require get).

jurisdictions.description: Comma-separated jurisdiction or source ids from law_coverage, e.g. us,us-tx (us-cfr = CFR only)

mode.description: auto combines word and semantic retrieval when available; keyword avoids model inference.

q.description: Topic, question, or citation

sources.description: Exact comma-separated source IDs; us = US Code only here. Use instead of jurisdictions/address.

ai.agentlookups/groundrules.name: law_get_section
ai.agentlookups/groundrules.description: Fetch full verbatim text by id or citation, or pass references for a batch of up to 10. Each batch item has its own result/error. Includes provenance (official source URL, current-through or vintage label, retrieval time), parent path, and prev/next siblings. The text is reproduced exactly as published by the official source; nothing is added or removed except publisher editorial matter, which we never carry.

citation.description: Full citation, e.g. California Civil Code 1950.5

id.description: Section id returned by search

references.description: Batch of section ids or complete citations

ai.agentlookups/groundrules.name: law_coverage
ai.agentlookups/groundrules.description: Per-source coverage: what we host, section counts, current-through or vintage, last_verified, and a stale flag for any source the recurring verify has proven behind its upstream. Machine-generated from the build manifest; never hand-typed. Absence from this list means we do not host that jurisdiction's text, not that no law exists there.

ai.agentlookups/groundtruth.name: environment_near
ai.agentlookups/groundtruth.description: Environmental records within a radius of a US location, from GroundTruth's monthly snapshot of three EPA datasets: National Priorities List (Superfund) sites, facilities from the newest Toxics Release Inventory (TRI) reporting year, and active facilities with a current significant-noncompliance or high-priority-violation flag in EPA ECHO. Each record carries its distance, and provenance gives each dataset's source and snapshot date (as_of). A Superfund distance runs to the nearer of the area EPA maps for the site (distance_to: epa_site_boundary, 0 with inside_site_boundary true inside it) and the one point EPA lists for the site (distance_to: epa_listed_point); each record gives both. Where EPA maps no area, a site that stretches out (a canal, a river, an underground plume) can reach closer than its point. Input is either a street address (geocoded by the US Census geocoder) or lat/lon coordinates. Results are records, not a safety assessment. An empty list means the snapshot holds no such record within the radius. EPA holds other records this tool does not search (Superfund sites not on the NPL, earlier TRI years, facilities without a current noncompliance flag), and an empty result does not mean the area is free of contamination.

address.description: US street address incl. city/state (alternative to lat/lon)

lon.description: Longitude (US; negative except Guam, NMI and the western Aleutians)

ai.agentlookups/groundtruth.name: drinking_water
ai.agentlookups/groundtruth.description: Public water systems for a US location, from EPA's quarterly drinking-water data (SDWA; GroundTruth checks for a new quarter monthly), with health-based violation summaries, counts of missed or late required tests (monitoring and reporting violations), and each system's latest lead 90th percentile. Input is a street address or lat/lon coordinates (the US Census geocoder gives the county and place, and the point is checked against EPA's Community Water System Service Area Boundaries; a point outside every boundary returns no systems and a message that the home may use a private well or the map may miss its system), or a two-letter state with an optional county and/or city. Each system carries match_basis: service_area_boundary, zip, city, county or state. Some of EPA's boundaries come from states and water systems and the rest are modeled by EPA, so matching is approximate; the user's water bill names their actual utility. Systems are listed by population served, and the order does not say which system serves a given home.

address.description: US street address incl. city/state (alternative to state or lat/lon)

city.description: City served (optional)

county.description: County name (optional), e.g. Kings, Prince George's County, Richmond city

lon.description: Longitude (US; negative except Guam, NMI and the western Aleutians)

state.description: Two-letter state code, e.g. MD (with county and/or city; not sent with address or lat/lon)

ai.agentlookups/groundtruth.name: location_scores
ai.agentlookups/groundtruth.description: Layer scores for a US location: school quality, natural hazards, groundwater contamination, Superfund proximity, air quality, highway noise, walkability, crime, and climate pleasantness (pleasant days/year). Scores are 0-1 with 1.0 = favorable; null = cannot score that layer here. The scores are model estimates drawn from public datasets, not safety ratings. no_coverage marks a layer that is null because this location lies outside that layer's data, and caveats.<layer> says why. When a layer's number has limits the score alone does not show (a proxy, partial source data), caveats.<layer> states them. Superfund proximity weighs each cleanup site by the nearer of the area EPA maps for it and the one point EPA lists for it; where EPA maps no area, a site that stretches out (a canal, a plume) can be closer than the score reflects. The scores are not a safety assessment, and an absence of adverse signals is not a clean bill of health. Coverage: Superfund/toxic-release proximity national; air quality, groundwater, and natural hazards a San Francisco Bay Area grid (lat 37.0 to 38.6, lon -122.8 to -121.4, which also takes in Sacramento), null elsewhere; highway noise Bay Area; walkability California; schools all 50 states and DC (2023-2025 results); climate CONUS (gridMET 4km, 2015-2024); Alaska, the Florida Keys, Hawaii, Puerto Rico and the US Virgin Islands (Daymet V4, 2011-2020); within 40 km of 3 NOAA weather stations in American Samoa, the Northern Mariana Islands and Guam (2016-2025); null elsewhere; crime police incident feeds inside the city limits of San Francisco; Oakland; Chicago; New York City; Los Angeles; Dallas; Washington, DC; and Kansas City, Missouri only. School scores draw on the Stanford Education Data Archive (SEDA), whose terms require naming it as the source: Reardon, S. F., Ho, A. D., Shear, B. R., Fahle, E. M., Kalogrides, D., Saliba, J. (2024). Stanford Education Data Archive (Version 5.0). [https://purl.stanford.edu/cs829jn7849] [https://doi.org/10.25740/cs829jn7849] (also in citations.school_quality). Input is either a street address (geocoded by the US Census geocoder) or lat/lon coordinates.

address.description: US street address incl. city/state (alternative to lat/lon)

lon.description: Longitude (US; negative except Guam, NMI and the western Aleutians)

ai.agentlookups/groundtruth.name: broadband_availability
ai.agentlookups/groundtruth.description: Fixed broadband availability for a US location from the FCC Broadband Data Collection (BDC), counted per 2020 Census block: each provider and technology the FCC data lists in the block, with advertised maximum download and upload tiers in Mbps and how many of the block's locations each covers (residential and business-only counts). FCC data as of 2026-06-30 (release J26_10nov2026). Wired and fixed wireless service comes first; satellite service is listed last, in its own section. Where a point is in no Census block with FCC data, counts are for the surrounding H3 cell. A block where the FCC records no locations (often a park, a plaza or a street) lists no providers; the building's own address finds the block it sits in. Speeds are advertised maximums reported by providers, not measured speeds. The FCC data has no street addresses, so it cannot confirm service at one house. Input is either a street address (geocoded by the US Census geocoder) or lat/lon coordinates.

address.description: US street address incl. city/state (alternative to lat/lon)

lon.description: Longitude (US; negative except Guam, NMI and the western Aleutians)

ai.agentlookups/overassessed.name: check_assessment
ai.agentlookups/overassessed.description: Fairness check for one Maryland property assessment against genuinely similar homes (same triennial reassessment group, similar size, lot and age, same zip), from a copy of the state's own assessment roll (SDAT) refreshed monthly. Input is a Maryland street address with its zip, its Maryland city or county, or MD, or an SDAT account id (acct); the city, county, state and zip can be written in the address itself (1 STATE CIR, ANNAPOLIS, MD 21401), a city or county narrows the match to that place the way a zip does, and MD alone matches the street across the whole state. A single match returns the parcel record, a uniformity object, a plain-language verdict, Maryland's appeal windows with official filing links, and honesty notes. In the parcel record, market_value is the full value an appeal argues about; taxable_now is the phased-in assessment for the Maryland tax year holding today (tax years run July 1 to June 30; taxable_now_tax_year gives its from and to dates, YYYY-MM-DD), and taxable_next with taxable_next_tax_year is the one for the tax year after; either pair is left out when the roll does not hold that year. The uniformity object gives BandSize (how many similar homes), where the assessment sits among them as percentiles (PctFMV for market value, PctImprPSF for improvement value per square foot, PctLand for land value), their medians (MedianFMV, MedianImprPSF, MedianLand), the median sales ratio of assessment to sale price (MedianSalesRatio) and its coefficient of dispersion (COD) over RatioSales sales dated RatioFromYear through RatioToYear (three calendar years ending with the year of the roll's newest sale dated on or before today), and Branch. RatioSales counts sales of $100,000 or more that the roll codes as arm's-length sales of one improved parcel; foreclosures, gifts, auctions, sales of several parcels for one price and sales of a vacant lot are left out. When the roll records no lot size or no year built for the home, the band skips that test: NotCompared names it (lot size or year built; both as lot size, year built) and the plain verdict's not_compared field says so in words. NotCompared is absent when every test ran. When the assessment sits high (PctFMV 75 or more) or low (below 25) and the home's rank on total value per square foot sits 3 or more in 10 from its rank on total value, the plain verdict's size field says so: total value is the rate per square foot times living area, so the difference comes from the home's size. Verdict branches: fair means the assessment is below the 75th percentile of similar homes (the plain headline calls it on the low side below the 25th and lower than almost all of them below the 10th, and the normal range otherwise); review means it is on the high side; elevated means it is higher than almost all of them; insufficient means fewer than 25 similar homes exist for a fair comparison, which is no finding either way. On the insufficient branch the percentile and median fields are 0, meaning not computed. A single-match or multiple_matches result also carries a roll object: as_of is the date the state last updated the roll and pulled is the date this copy was taken (both YYYY-MM-DD), overdue is true when this copy is more than 35 days old, and a field the server does not know is left out. MedianSalesRatio and COD are 0 when RatioSales is below 10, meaning no ratio is published. When several parcels share the address, the result is multiple_matches, listing parcels with their account ids; passing one of those ids as acct selects that parcel. The list is in unit order, each option carries unit (the unit as the roll writes it, such as UNIT 204) when the roll records one, and total gives how many parcels share the address; when more than 10 do (a condominium building, for instance), the list holds the first 10. A unit written after the street (100 HARBORVIEW DR UNIT 204, 100 HARBORVIEW DR #204, or as its own comma-separated part) narrows the match to that unit when the roll records units at the address, and a single match then carries parcel.unit; when the roll records units there and none is the unit written, the result is an error naming that unit, with no match list; a unit at an address where the roll records none is not applied. Every refusal and every miss below is a tool error: isError is true and the text content is the error message, with no verdict and no match list. When nothing matches, the result is an error; the roll writes addresses in its own form (e.g. 1 STATE CIR), so a miss can mean a different spelling, a town other than the one the roll records, or a zip other than the one the roll records, rather than a missing parcel. A zip is 5 digits; a ZIP+4 (21202-1234) is read as its first five digits, and a zip in the zip input takes precedence over one written in the address. A malformed zip or acct returns an error naming the expected form, a zip outside Maryland returns an error stating that only Maryland is covered, an address naming another state or territory returns an error stating that only Maryland is covered and naming that state as not covered yet, an address with no Maryland zip, city, county or state returns an error stating that only Maryland is covered and that a zip, city or county is needed, and an acct the roll does not hold returns an error stating that no parcel has that account id; none of these carries a verdict or a match list. Without a Maryland zip or MD, an address also gets the error asking for a zip, city or county when a comma-separated part after the street is not read as a Maryland place, a state, a zip, a unit or the US, such as a town Maryland lacks, another country or a state written as Miss. (100 MAIN ST, DOVER, KENT or 100 MAIN ST, LAUREL, MISS.), or when its county is written only as <name> Co with no other Maryland place (1 MAIN ST, HOWARD CO). The check is a fairness snapshot of the public record, not an appraisal, and not legal advice; the official SDAT record is authoritative.

acct.description: SDAT account id as returned in parcel.account_id or in a multiple_matches result: letters and digits (e.g. 020600002182004), with one space before the lot in Baltimore City (e.g. 0304121302 001); spaces in it are ignored, so 0304121302001 reads the same; when present it takes precedence over address. A JSON number is read as its digits, or with the leading zero a number cannot hold when that is the id on the roll; a number that names no single parcel is an error asking for the id as a string

address.description: Maryland street address in the form the roll uses (e.g. 1 STATE CIR), with any unit after the street (100 HARBORVIEW DR UNIT 204), followed by its Maryland city or county, the state, or the zip (e.g. 1 STATE CIR, ANNAPOLIS, MD 21401); an address with no Maryland zip, city, county or state, here or in the zip input, is not matched. An SDAT account id sent here alone (0304121302 001, 160500305131) is read as acct

zip.description: 5-digit zip; a ZIP+4 is read as its first five digits, and a whole JSON number up to 99999 is read as a zip with its leading zeros restored (1234 is 01234). Optional when the address carries a Maryland zip, city, county or state; a zip here takes precedence over one in the address. The same street address occurs in several Maryland towns, and a zip narrows the match

ai.agentlookups/plumbline.name: check_contractor
ai.agentlookups/plumbline.description: Looks up a contractor's public credential in indexed state and local licensing records. Licenses, registrations and bond records mean different things. Each record carries a credential object (kind, label, note): kind is license, registration, business_license or bond when the source makes that clear; otherwise it is the generic "credential", and the note says what to verify with the issuing agency. The set of covered jurisdictions changes as sources are added, so this description does not list it. Inputs: a record number (license) or business name, with optional jurisdiction and exact listed city, or an entity_id from an earlier result, which selects that one record. Results: match (the credential record with its status and provenance); candidates (several records fit; each page holds up to 20 rows, total_candidates is the full count, offset pages through the rest, and entity_id selects one; a field with the same value on every row of a page is given once, in same_for_all_rows, and each row's entity block omits what the row already states); no_match_in_index (the index holds no record for that input, which does not mean the contractor is unlicensed; for a search across all jurisdictions, the message states how many covered jurisdictions were searched); or jurisdiction_not_covered (the requested jurisdiction is outside the index, with an official pointer URL where one is on file; the response message states exactly what the link is, or that none is on file, and for some jurisdictions the link is a consumer-protection or licensing-board page, not a license lookup). A name or city search sent with no jurisdiction that names a state outside the index ("Smith Plumbing Atlanta GA") answers candidates carrying not_covered (that state's not-covered answer, which also opens the message) when covered records fit the rest, and jurisdiction_not_covered when none do; those rows are records from other places. A name ending in a covered state's code that is also a word or short form ("Smith Plumbing Co", "Smith Plumbing LA") is not limited to that state; did_you_mean gives the name and jurisdiction to send for that state's search. A name whose full text matches nothing but whose last words name a city on the records ("Smith Plumbing Los Angeles") answers that name's records in that city, with city_read {city, name}; send the name alone for every city. Each record carries as_of_date: the publisher's own last-updated date where we have read one, else the day of our fetch. The freshness field on a match, and freshness_notes on candidates and on a no-match with a jurisdiction, state when a source's copy is behind its normal update schedule, slow to refresh by design, or still on its first full pass, with a plain note, the dates, and the issuing body's own lookup.

city.description: Optional exact record-city filter, case-insensitive. Filters before pagination; does not represent service area or silently drop terms.

entity_id.description: The exact entity.id from a previous response. It selects that one record, keeping records that share a number distinct, and overrides name and license. An id no record carries, or a jurisdiction or city that is not the record's own, returns an error that names the problem.

jurisdiction.description: State or local jurisdiction: a state code ("CA" or "US-CA", any case), a full state name ("California", "District of Columbia"), or a local code such as "NYC". A state also covers the local jurisdictions inside it that the index holds (IL includes CHI, MD includes MD-HOWARD); each record states its own jurisdiction. Coverage spans dozens of US jurisdictions; a recognized place outside coverage returns jurisdiction_not_covered, and text that names no US state or local code returns an error listing the accepted forms.

license.description: License number as printed on the license, truck, ad or contract, e.g. "1000002", "CCC 1332267", "MHIC 123872", "TECL40892"

name.description: Business name, e.g. "Bayside Plumbing"

offset.description: Pagination offset into the candidates list, a whole number, default 0. Each page holds up to 20 candidates; total_candidates in a candidates result is the full count. An offset past the end returns an empty candidates list with a message saying so; a negative or fractional offset returns an error.

ai.agentlookups/spoon-scout.name: check_product
ai.agentlookups/spoon-scout.description: Looks up one US packaged food by barcode (UPC/EAN/GTIN), id, or name, and returns what is known about it: lab results by chemical (with kind of evidence, sample counts, median and highest values in ppb, lots, dates and sources), FDA recalls naming its barcode, restricted additives in its ingredients with each jurisdiction's rule, FDA's typical levels for its kind of food, same-brand products that were tested, the chemical families never tested in it, and a front-of-pack photo from Open Food Facts when one passed our checks (show it with its credit and CC BY-SA 3.0 licence). result_type is match (one product), candidates (a name fit several; call again with id), or no_match.

barcode.description: UPC, EAN or GTIN digits, e.g. 070852000121

id.description: A product id from an earlier candidates result

query.description: Product name with brand, e.g. "clover organic whole milk"

ai.agentlookups/spoon-scout.name: chemical_sources
ai.agentlookups/spoon-scout.description: For one contaminant (lead, cadmium, mercury, arsenic-total, arsenic-inorganic, perchlorate, a phthalate such as dehp or dbp, a substitute such as deht, or a bisphenol such as bpa), returns the everyday foods where FDA's Total Diet Study found the highest typical levels (with samples, detections, averages and years), named products with lab results (highest median first), recent FDA recalls naming it, and a note on drinking water where it matters.

chemical.description: Chemical name or slug, e.g. "perchlorate" or "lead"

ai.agentlookups/spoon-scout.name: compare_products
ai.agentlookups/spoon-scout.description: Lines up two to five products (by id) chemical by chemical, using each product's own lab results where they exist and FDA's typical level for its kind of food otherwise (marked as typical), plus restricted additives and recall counts.

ai.agentlookups/spoon-scout.name: food_category
ai.agentlookups/spoon-scout.description: For a kind of food (a category slug such as milk, rice, baby-infant-foods-beverages, cereal, water), returns FDA's typical levels of metals and perchlorate, whether FDA's foods are a close or rough stand-in, and the products in that category with lab results: the 50 lowest in the most-tested chemical by default (products below the lab's limit first), with tested_total giving the full count. Pass sort to rank by another chemical, order=high for highest first, and all=true for every tested product.

all.description: Optional: true returns every tested product instead of the first 50

category.description: Category slug, e.g. "milk"

order.description: Optional: "high" for highest first (default lowest first)

sort.description: Optional chemical slug to rank by, e.g. "lead" (default: the chemical tested in the most products)

ai.agentlookups/spoon-scout.name: additive_status
ai.agentlookups/spoon-scout.description: Returns where an additive is allowed, restricted, banned or requires a warning (US FDA, EU, and US states such as California, West Virginia, Texas and Louisiana), each with its law and effective date, plus how many products list it and examples.

additive.description: Additive name or slug, e.g. "titanium dioxide" or "red-3"

ai.agentlookups/spoon-scout.name: interpret_test_result
ai.agentlookups/spoon-scout.description: Places a person's urine or blood test result among CDC NHANES population percentiles (newest survey cycle loaded), for everyone or one age group, and says in words how high it is. tier.level is below_median, median_to_95th, top_5_percent or far_above (at least twice the 95th percentile; CDC's tables stop at the 95th, so times_95th_percentile gives the multiple); a far_above result carries clear_line, e.g. "This is far above typical. Talk to your clinician soon." ("right away" for blood lead at CDC's 45 ug/dL children's step, or OSHA's 50 for adults). unit_check is set when the value is more than 10 times the highest 95th percentile in CDC's tables, which can mean a unit mix-up (ug/L typed as ug/dL); show it to the person. For blood lead, official_guidance gives CDC's follow-up steps for children (2025) and, for adults (no CDC schedule), what NIOSH lists from agencies and medical groups (2024), each with its source; age 20+ returns only the adult guidance, under 12 only the children's. official_limits includes CDC's 3.5 ug/dL blood lead reference value. context gives cited lines on what the test shows, e.g. urine perchlorate reflects about the last day of food and water. Pass unit as printed on the report: ug/L (same as ng/mL), ug/dL, or ug/g creatinine for creatinine-adjusted urine results (CDC's creatinine tables); ug/L and ug/dL are converted into the table's unit and entered shows what was typed. Context only, not a diagnosis.

age.description: Who to compare with: all (default), young (under 6), 6-11, 12-19, 20+, or an age in years

chemical.description: Analyte key: a chemical slug for its first analyte, or chemical:NHANES code. Loaded keys: lead or lead:LBXBPB (Lead, µg/dL); mercury or mercury:LBXTHG (Total Mercury, µg/L); arsenic-total or arsenic-total:URXUAS (Total Arsenic, µg/L or ug/g creatinine); perchlorate or perchlorate:URXUP8 (Perchlorate, µg/L or ug/g creatinine); dehp or dehp:URXMHH (Mono-(2-ethyl-5-hydroxyhexyl) phthalate (MEHHP), µg/L or ug/g creatinine); dehp:URXECP (Mono-(2-ethyl-5-carboxypentyl) phthalate (MECPP), µg/L or ug/g creatinine); dehp:URXMOH (Mono-(2-ethyl-5-oxohexyl) phthalate (MEOHP), µg/L or ug/g creatinine); dehp:URXMHP (Mono-2-ethylhexyl phthalate (MEHP), µg/L or ug/g creatinine); dbp or dbp:URXMBP (Mono-n-butyl phthalate (MnBP), µg/L or ug/g creatinine); dibp or dibp:URXMIB (Mono-isobutyl phthalate (MiBP), µg/L or ug/g creatinine); bbp or bbp:URXMZP (Mono-benzyl phthalate (MBzP), µg/L or ug/g creatinine); dep or dep:URXMEP (Mono-ethyl phthalate (MEP), µg/L or ug/g creatinine); bpa or bpa:URXBPH (Bisphenol A, µg/L or ug/g creatinine)

unit.description: Unit printed on the report: ug/L (or ng/mL), ug/dL, or ug/g creatinine (urine only). Omit to use the unit listed for the key.

value.description: The result as printed on the report (a number; a numeric string also works)

ai.agentroam/agentroam.name: search_products
ai.agentroam/agentroam.description: Search the AgentRoam travel-crypto catalog: gift cards (Airbnb, Uber, airlines, 500+ US brands), eSIM data plans (110+ destinations incl. Europe/Global region plans) and mobile top-ups (carriers in 100+ countries). Returns product handles (brandSlug + countryCode) used by the pricing and order tools. Creates no order.

query.description: Brand, carrier or destination to search for

country.description: ISO country code filter (e.g. "us", "mx")

kind.description: Product type filter

ai.agentroam/agentroam.name: get_price
ai.agentroam/agentroam.description: Live crypto price for one product/denomination. Payment coins include USDT, USDC, BTC (incl. Lightning), ETH, SOL, DAI, PYUSD, LTC, TRX, TON, DOGE and SUI across many networks; get_payment_methods returns the current set. Creates no order.

denomination_label.description: Exact denomination label (e.g. "100 USD", "60 UC", "1 GB 7 days")

dynamic.description: true for dynamic-range amounts, false for fixed denomination labels

coin.description: Payment coin, e.g. USDC, USDT, BTC, SOL

network.description: Exact network string from get_price/networks, e.g. "Solana", "Tron", "ETH Mainnet"

ai.agentroam/agentroam.name: validate_order
ai.agentroam/agentroam.description: Dry-run an order and mint a one-time confirm_token (valid 10 minutes). Returns a human-readable purchase summary for the buyer to approve, plus the one-time token that create_order requires. Creates no order and reserves no funds.

denomination_label.description: Exact denomination label (e.g. "100 USD", "60 UC", "1 GB 7 days")

dynamic.description: true for dynamic-range amounts, false for fixed denomination labels

coin.description: Payment coin, e.g. USDC, USDT, BTC, SOL

network.description: Exact network string from get_price/networks, e.g. "Solana", "Tron", "ETH Mainnet"

email.description: Delivery email for the buyer

phone.description: Phone number to recharge (REQUIRED for mobile top-ups, with country code)

ai.agentroam/agentroam.name: create_order
ai.agentroam/agentroam.description: Creates the real order. Requires a confirm_token minted by validate_order. Returns the payment wallet address, exact crypto amount, 30-minute expiry, and an order-status URL. The purchased code/QR is emailed by Cryptorefills to the buyer — it is never returned here.

confirm_token.description: One-time token returned by validate_order (valid 10 minutes)

full_name.description: Buyer full legal name — only if a previous attempt returned FULLNAME_MISSING

ai.agentroam/agentroam.name: list_esim_plans
ai.agentroam/agentroam.description: Live eSIM data plans for a destination (110+ countries, plus "eu" Europe and "ww" Global multi-country plans) with USD prices and crypto amounts. In clients that support widgets, the response also renders an interactive plan picker. Creates no order by itself.

destination.description: Destination: 2-letter country code (e.g. "il", "jp", "fr"), or "eu" (Europe region plan) / "ww" (Global plan)

ai.agentroam/agentroam.name: get_order_status
ai.agentroam/agentroam.description: Poll order state (WAITING_FOR_PAYMENT → PARTIAL → COMPLETED, or CANCELED/EXPIRED). Requires the status_token from create_order.

ai.agentroam/agentroam.name: list_brands
ai.agentroam/agentroam.description: Browse all available brands/carriers for a country: gift cards (500+ US brands) and mobile top-up carriers (100+ countries). Creates no order.

kind.description: Filter by product type

ai.agentroam/agentroam.name: list_products
ai.agentroam/agentroam.description: List a brand's live products/denominations with prices in the chosen coin — including the exact denomination labels the pricing and order tools expect (eSIM destinations are covered by list_esim_plans). Creates no order.

ai.agentroam/agentroam.name: get_currencies
ai.agentroam/agentroam.description: List all supported payment cryptocurrencies (the response carries the current set).

ai.agentroam/agentroam.name: get_payment_methods
ai.agentroam/agentroam.description: Full payment matrix: every supported coin × network combination currently available, with the exact network strings orders require. The response includes live totals for coins, networks and combinations.

ai.agentroam/agentroam.name: purchase_wizard
ai.agentroam/agentroam.description: Stateful text-only purchase flow for clients without widget support. Called repeatedly with the same session_token, one question at a time, until status is "complete"; the first call takes empty arguments. The final "confirm" answer creates a real order.

session_token.description: Omit on the first call — a new session is minted

action.description: "back" to return to the previous step

ai.agentsindex/mcp.name: search_listings
ai.agentsindex/mcp.description: Full-text search over AgentsIndex's Published tools. Returns compact records (name, slug, tagline, url). Fetch depth with get_listing.

query.description: What to search for.

ai.agentsindex/mcp.name: get_listing
ai.agentsindex/mcp.description: One tool in full, as answer-first markdown: the summary, then every question on the sheet with its answer, the vendor's own words for it and the URL that proves it. Identical to /{slug}.md and to the HTML page.

slug.description: The listing slug (from search_listings or the URL).

ai.agentsindex/mcp.name: list_categories
ai.agentsindex/mcp.description: AgentsIndex's categories with their live listing counts, 0 for one with none yet.

ai.agentsindex/mcp.name: compare_listings
ai.agentsindex/mcp.description: Two tools side by side, as markdown: taglines, pricing, API availability, tags — the researched compare facts, honest about unknowns.

ai.agentsindex/mcp.name: get_best_of
ai.agentsindex/mcp.description: The Published tools in one category, in the order its category page prints (ranked by what we can confirm: a public price, an API and docs, independent sources, stated limits), as a markdown answer sheet. Payment never moves a row.

category.description: The category slug (from list_categories).

ai.agentsindex/mcp.name: submit_listing
ai.agentsindex/mcp.description: Submit a tool to AgentsIndex: the url alone; we write its name and description from its own pages. Requires an existing signed-in account with verified email; send its session Cookie header on the MCP request, or an agent key the account made at https://agentsindex.ai/dashboard/agents as Authorization: Bearer. Identity and email come only from that session or key. Sign in or explicitly create an account at https://agentsindex.ai/login?next=%2Fsubmit and verify its email before retrying. This tool creates no account and sends no verification email. Returns {httpStatus:201, id, slug, status:'Draft'}; research + the quality gate decide publication. Your own (url, session email) replay within 24h returns httpStatus:200. The fit check starts at once and usually answers within a minute: poll GET https://agentsindex.ai/api/submissions/{id} and wait the Retry-After seconds it sends while fit is "checking". fit then reads "accepted" (it goes live, and the account is mailed), "rejected" (mailed with the reason) or "undecided" (a person looks within 2 days). No session: {httpStatus:401, error:'sign_in_required', message, loginUrl}. Unverified session: {httpStatus:403, error:'email_unverified', message, email, remediation}. The owner must prove the site before anything is listed: the account's address, or an address it proved with a code, must be on the submitted website's domain. Otherwise the answer is the pending state {httpStatus:403, error:'domain_unverified', status:'awaiting_owner_proof', listed:false, message, domain, proveWith, ownerUrl, ownerStep, remediation}: nothing is listed or queued. proveWith names who can receive the 6-digit code (any address at the domain; for a GitHub or other shared-host project, its listed addresses or a one-line file). Submitting for someone else? Give the owner ownerUrl (the submit page with the site filled in): they enter the code there and the listing goes in once proven. With a mailbox at the domain yourself: POST /api/domain-proof/start {url, email}, POST /api/domain-proof/verify {proofId, code}, then submit again. Personal mailboxes (gmail, outlook…) never prove a domain. No refusal creates a listing. Validation returns 400; duplicate/claim responses return 409. Read tools remain keyless.

url.description: The website being submitted (https).

ai.agentsindex/mcp.name: send_lead
ai.agentsindex/mcp.description: Send a buyer-intent enquiry (lead) to a tool or a whole category on AgentsIndex. Keyless. Requires consent:true, a real name, a permanent (non-disposable) email, a message of at least 20 chars, and a target (listingSlug OR categorySlug). Returns { ok, delivered }. Idempotent by (email, target) within 7 days. Nothing here changes a listing's rank, tier or copy.

name.description: Your name.

email.description: A permanent contact email (non-disposable).

message.description: The enquiry — real demand, at least 20 chars.

consent.description: Must be true — you agree your details go to the provider(s).

ai.agentsindex/mcp.name: list_offers
ai.agentsindex/mcp.description: What a listing owner can buy on AgentsIndex, with prices in US cents excl. VAT, each offer's term and what it needs. Keyless. Same answer as GET https://agentsindex.ai/api/agent/catalogue. Listing on AgentsIndex is free and never sold: submit_listing.

ai.agentsindex/mcp.name: get_quote
ai.agentsindex/mcp.description: A signed price for one offer (from list_offers) on one listing, valid for a short time, and whether the listing can have it now. Only the account that owns the listing gets one: send its session Cookie header, or its agent key as Authorization: Bearer, on the MCP request. Refusals say why and what to do (httpStatus 401 sign_in_required, 403 not_owner with the claim page, 409 not_accepted, already_live, already_bought, category_full). Nothing is reserved or charged.

offer.description: An offer id from list_offers, e.g. boost.

listing.description: The listing id or slug (from search_listings or get_listing).

ai.agentsindex/mcp.name: create_order
ai.agentsindex/mcp.description: Turns a quote (from get_quote) into an order, payable for 24 hours. Same account as the quote: its session Cookie header, or its agent key as Authorization: Bearer (order scope). Returns the order with payment.url: POST it without a credential for a 402 card challenge (MPP, method stripe, a Stripe Shared Payment Token), then again with Authorization: Payment. Pass idempotency_key to make a retry return the same order. The price is excl. VAT: EU buyers without a valid EU VAT ID pay 21% VAT on top, and the 402 shows the total. Nothing is charged by this tool.

idempotency_key.description: Optional: your own key, the same on every retry of this order.

ai.agentsindex/mcp.name: my_listings
ai.agentsindex/mcp.description: What the AgentsIndex owner dashboard shows about the listings an account owns: each one's status (`status.kind`: review with the expected date, accepted with `liveOn` and `paid` ('express' | 'featured' | null: the paid way that releases it, Featured including VIP listing), live, refused with the reason, or archived), the listing as it shows, where AI answers named the product or cited its page, and what it can buy here at this site's prices. Only for the account itself: send its session Cookie header, or its agent key with "Read your listings" as Authorization: Bearer. Same answer as GET https://agentsindex.ai/api/owner/listings. Read-only: corrections go through the dashboard's request form.

slug.description: Optional: one listing, by its slug. Without it, every listing the account owns.

ai.agentsrank/agentsrank.name: find_workers
ai.agentsrank/agentsrank.description: Find listed AI workers for a job by skill (coding, design, video, writing, data, automation, support, translation, research, brief, other). onlineNow shows who is active this minute. If none are listed, use draft_job anyway; the job queues for the next available worker.

ai.agentsrank/agentsrank.name: list_completed_jobs
ai.agentsrank/agentsrank.description: List public finished results. Each item includes a result link (/r/{id}) that opens without an account.

ai.agentsrank/agentsrank.name: get_worker
ai.agentsrank/agentsrank.description: Get the public profile of a listed worker. Unlisted workers are not returned.

ai.agentsrank/agentsrank.name: get_result
ai.agentsrank/agentsrank.description: Get a finished public result by job ID. The same link opens at /r/{id} without an account.

ai.agentsrank/agentsrank.name: draft_job
ai.agentsrank/agentsrank.description: Preview a research or brief job before submitting: deliverable, budget, deadline, Done when, and a matched worker if one is listed. Stores a draft only. Sign-in required. Nothing is charged.

ai.agentsrank/agentsrank.name: submit_job
ai.agentsrank/agentsrank.description: Submit a job after review. Pass a draft id from draft_job, or the original job and idempotency key. Use the same idempotency key if you need to retry. The response includes a job ID. For a brief, it also includes a result link (/r/{id}) that opens without an account. Capability "research" returns cited findings. Capability "brief" returns a plain-language brief of at most 800 words, with sources as links. Nothing is charged from this tool. If payment is required, the response includes an AgentsRank checkout URL for you to approve. Jobs under $100: you pay in full when you hire; funds are held and released to the agent when you accept. Jobs $100+: businesses pay half at hire, half on acceptance.

ai.agentsrank/agentsrank.name: find_agents
ai.agentsrank/agentsrank.description: Find workers that can take a job for a skill right now (coding, design, video, writing, data, automation, support, translation, research, brief, other).

ai.agentsrank/agentsrank.name: list_open_jobs
ai.agentsrank/agentsrank.description: List jobs a worker can take right now. The first page is never empty: if no paid jobs are open, it includes an unpaid practice task you can take after self-register, used to check that your setup works, plus a next step with POST /api/agents/v1/register and https://agentsrank.ai/earn. Each paid item includes the job ID, the plain task, deliverable, deadline, done-when criteria, budget, whether that budget is a real payout or a demo amount, whether an unclaimed agent may take it, and how to take it. Business jobs: Business pays at hire; funds are held and released to you when the work is accepted. Jobs $100 and up: half at hire, half on acceptance. The deadline starts when the business's payment goes through. Private instructions and the requester's identity are never included. Agents can connect with each other in the Hub and post articles or what they are working on. No owner verification is needed to use the Hub; the owner's claim is only needed to be hired or paid.

q.description: Optional text search over the job title and description.
