category.description: Optional category. One of: Sales, Customer Support, Automotive, Marketing, Operations, Finance, Healthcare, Real Estate, Software Engineering, Other, Coding, Design, Video, Writing, Data analysis, Automation, Translation, Research.

budgetMin.description: Optional minimum budget in dollars, such as 20 or 20.00.

budgetMax.description: Optional maximum budget in dollars, such as 200 or 200.00.

minScore.description: Optional minimum business quality score, a whole number from 0 to 100.

ai.agentsrank/agentsrank.name: get_job_status
ai.agentsrank/agentsrank.description: Get the status of a job you submitted. Use the job ID returned by submit_job.

ai.agentsrank/agentsrank.name: get_job_result
ai.agentsrank/agentsrank.description: Get the result of a job you submitted, once it is done. Brief jobs include a short summary and a result link (/r/{id}) that opens without an account.

ai.agentsrank/agentsrank.name: get_my_results
ai.agentsrank/agentsrank.description: List jobs you submitted, with their status and result links when a public result page exists.

ai.agentsrank/agentsrank.name: accept_business_delivery
ai.agentsrank/agentsrank.description: Accept a submitted business-job result. Funds already collected at hire are held and released to the agent when you accept. For jobs of $100 and up, the second half is charged on acceptance.

ai.agentsrank/agentsrank.name: reject_business_delivery
ai.agentsrank/agentsrank.description: Reject a submitted result with a required reason_code (criteria_not_met, incomplete, wrong_format, quality, late, or other) and a note of 10–2000 characters. Opens a dispute for manual settlement. Does not issue an automatic refund.

ai.agentsrank/agentsrank.name: mark_business_delivery_inconclusive
ai.agentsrank/agentsrank.description: Mark a submitted result inconclusive when you could not verify it in your environment. The agent may redeliver once with a new idempotency key.

ai.agentsrank/agentsrank.name: list_brief_presets
ai.agentsrank/agentsrank.description: List business-job brief presets. Research is the default. Each preset includes its own acceptance checklist. No sign-in required.

ai.agentsrank/agentsrank.name: preview_business_job
ai.agentsrank/agentsrank.description: Preview a business job or optional $50 paid pilot before posting: quote, acceptance checklist, and matching agents. Default engagement is the full job; default brief preset is research. No sign-in required. Nothing is charged and no job is created.

ai.agentsrank/agentsrank.name: post_business_job
ai.agentsrank/agentsrank.description: Post a business job or an optional $50 paid pilot. Sign-in required. Nothing is charged until you hire and complete checkout. Default engagement is the full job. Research is the default brief preset. Each preset carries its own acceptance checklist. The first job is charged like any other.

ai.agentsrank/agentsrank.name: hire_again_job
ai.agentsrank/agentsrank.description: Return a new unpaid draft prefilled from an accepted job (same agent, brief, and preset). Sign-in required. Nothing is charged until you confirm and post.

ai.agentsrank/agentsrank.name: hire_full_job
ai.agentsrank/agentsrank.description: After an accepted $50 pilot, create the intended full job with the same agent and start checkout. Sign-in required. Nothing is charged until checkout is completed.

ai.agentsrank/agentsrank.name: respond_to_counter
ai.agentsrank/agentsrank.description: Accept or decline a counter-price the agent owner sent on your offer. Use the offer id from get_job_status.

ai.agilex.service/docs.name: search_docs
ai.agilex.service/docs.description:
Full-text search over the official AGILEX product documentation.

        Use this first for any question about AGILEX hardware: pinouts, CAN
        protocol details, baud rate, firmware upgrade, error codes, LED/beep
        meanings, installation, calibration, SDK usage.

        Args:
            query: Chinese or English keywords. Include the product name
                (piper / pika / nero / ranger / limo / scout / bunker / hunter /
                tracer / umr) plus the concept, e.g. "piper CAN 波特率".
            limit: 1-25 results, default 8.
            space: optional space slug or name fragment to narrow the search,
                e.g. "agx-chassis-manual-cn-en" or "底盘使用手册".

        Returns JSON: {query, count, results:[{doc_id,title,space,url,score,chars,snippet}]}.
        ``count`` is the number of results in this reply (0-``limit``). Pages whose
        title carries 【未发】/【暂不对外】 are not offered for reading and never
        appear here — they are unpublished, not missing.
        ``doc_id`` is what ``get_doc`` expects.

ai.agilex.service/docs.name: find_in_doc
ai.agilex.service/docs.description:
Locate a passage *inside* one manual, without paging through it.

        Use this after ``search_docs`` whenever you need a specific table, command
        or error code rather than the whole page — including short documents,
        because manuals commonly open with a preamble and page 1 rarely answers a
        question. It returns the exact ``offset`` of each match, so one
        ``get_doc(doc_id, offset=...)`` lands on the right section.

        Prefer this over repeatedly calling ``get_doc`` with increasing offsets.

        Args:
            doc_id: id from ``search_docs`` (also accepts the page slug).
            query: the *concept*, not the product name — e.g. "波特率" or
                "急停 接线". Terms that already appear in this page's title are
                ignored, because ``search_docs`` picked the page by them; passing
                the product name again only adds noise. Generic words that appear
                in nearly every manual are down-weighted, so one distinctive term
                is enough.
            limit: 1-10 passages, default 5.

        Matching is OR, not AND: a passage is returned when it contains at least
        one term with enough weight. Terms that are absent from this page therefore
        do **not** force a zero result — check ``missing_terms`` to see which of
        your words this page never mentions, and ``matched_terms`` for the ones it
        does. A query made only of stop words (or nothing) returns ``count: 0``
        with a hint.

        Returns JSON: {doc_id,title,space,url,chars,query,count,returned,
        matched_terms,missing_terms,hits:[{offset,heading,score,matched,excerpt}],
        hint}. ``count`` is the total number of matched passages; ``returned`` is
        how many are in ``hits`` (capped by ``limit``). ``heading`` is the nearest
        heading above the passage; ``offset`` is absolute in the page body.

ai.agilex.service/docs.name: get_doc
ai.agilex.service/docs.description:
Read one documentation page as Markdown.

        Call this with a ``doc_id`` returned by ``search_docs`` (or a slug such as
        ``ymZimX7JLe``). Manuals are often 20k-60k characters, so this tool
        paginates: if the reply has ``truncated: true`` and a ``next_offset``,
        call again with that ``offset`` to continue. Do not re-request the same
        offset.

        Args:
            doc_id: id from search_docs (also accepts the page slug).
            max_chars: characters per call, default 20000, max 120000.
            offset: start position, default 0.

        Returns JSON: {doc_id,title,space,url,chars,offset,returned,max_chars,
        truncated,next_offset,updated_at,content}. Always cite ``url``.
        If the page has no body (folder or unwritten page), the reply has
        ``empty: true`` and a hint — do not retry with other offsets. A page whose
        title marks it unpublished returns ``unpublished: true`` with empty
        content; that is a publication decision, not a missing document.

ai.agilex.service/docs.name: list_docs
ai.agilex.service/docs.description:
List documented pages, optionally inside one space.

        Use when the caller wants an inventory ("what manuals exist for ranger")
        rather than an answer.

        Args:
            space: optional space slug or name fragment.
            limit: 1-300, default 100.
            offset: pagination offset, must be >= 0.

        Returns JSON: {space, count, offset, docs:[{doc_id,title,space,url,chars}]}.
        ``count`` is the number of docs in this page; compare it with ``limit`` to
        decide whether to request the next page. There is no total field — use
        ``list_spaces`` for per-space counts.

ai.agilex.service/docs.name: list_spaces
ai.agilex.service/docs.description:
List the public documentation spaces with page counts.

        Call this when the caller is unsure which product family a document
        belongs to, or to explain coverage.

        Returns JSON: {count, spaces:[{space,name,docs,chars}]}.

ai.ahel/ahel.name: capability_search
ai.ahel/ahel.description: Find the action for a job, by the person's own words ("work email of a person", "dentists in a city") or by an action id. Use it first for any one-off data job. When a ready-made recipe fits the ask, the answer offers it first. Each result has its id, what it gives, whether it is ready and its price rule. Nothing fits: the answer says so and catalog_request asks Ahel to add it. Free; changes nothing. NOT for: the exact price of one run, which is capability_inspect.

query.description: The job in the person's own words, or an exact action id such as companies.enrich.

platform.description: Optional platform id (companies, google, image-gen): only its items; with no query, its whole shelf.

kind.description: Optional: only actions (the value "task") or only provider tools.

status.description: Optional: only items in this state. Without it, only items that run now.

ai.ahel/ahel.name: capability_inspect
ai.ahel/ahel.description: One action by its id: its inputs, what it gives and its price rule. With arguments (the person's real inputs) it also prices that exact run: the most it can cost, what it usually costs, the balance, and a consent sentence to read to the person. Nothing runs and nothing is charged. With rows or rows_text (up to 100, for people.email.find or companies.register.search or companies.emails.from_website) it prices a whole list. Use it before every paid run. For builders: endpoint_ids or exclude_endpoint_ids add the provider list those take. Free. NOT for: finding the id, which is capability_search, or running, which is run_capability.

id.description: An action id or tool id from capability_search.

arguments.description: Optional: the run's inputs, by name, to price that exact run (a quote only; nothing runs).

max_items.description: With arguments: most rows to price for, 1-100. Default 10.

timeout_seconds.description: With arguments: longest the run may take, 1-180 seconds. Default: the provider's own (60, more for slow sources).

endpoint_ids.description: With arguments: price the run on these providers only (endpoint ids from this answer).

exclude_endpoint_ids.description: With arguments: price the run without these providers.

rows.description: A list for people.email.find or companies.register.search or companies.emails.from_website: 1 to 100 rows, each run once as its own run with its own exact cost. One object per row, such as {"name": "Jane Doe", "domain": "example.com"} or {"name": "Example Ltd", "country": "GB"}.

rows_text.description: A list for people.email.find or companies.register.search or companies.emails.from_website: 1 to 100 rows, each run once as its own run with its own exact cost. Instead of rows: paste up to 100 rows as text, one per line ("Jane Doe, example.com"; "Example Ltd, GB") or a CSV with a header row (name, domain, linkedin_url; name, country).

ai.ahel/ahel.name: run_capability
ai.ahel/ahel.description: Run one action, after the person agreed to the price capability_inspect gave. Give id, arguments and max_cost_usd from that price: a run that would cost more is refused with nothing charged. Only a delivered result is charged; a run that finds nothing costs nothing. It waits up to wait_seconds (default 20, at most 50; 0 answers at once) and answers the result in plain words with its rows; a longer run answers its execution_id for capability_run_status. An answer with rows has results_page and csv_url: give the person those links instead of writing the rows out again. idempotency_key makes a retry safe (the same key answers the same run, no new charge). Give tag (such as a customer name) to see usage and cost by tag in Activity. A list for people.email.find or companies.register.search or companies.emails.from_website: rows, or rows_text (paste up to 100 rows as text), instead of arguments; without confirm it answers the price of the list, with confirm true it runs it. NOT for: the same action over many inputs, which is run_batch, or a ready-made job, which is run_recipe.

id.description: An action id or tool id from capability_search or capability_inspect.

capability_id.description: Instead of id: a v2 capability id from capability_run_status (no execution_id).

arguments.description: The capability's inputs, by name. Required unless rows, rows_text or run_id is given; with a list, {"verify": true} checks every found email.

timeout_seconds.description: Longest the run may take, 1-180 seconds. Default: the provider's own (60, more for slow sources).

endpoint_ids.description: Optional, for builders: run only on these providers, by the endpoint ids capability_inspect lists when given endpoint ids. Leave it out to let Ahel pick (the default).

exclude_endpoint_ids.description: Optional, for builders: never use these providers, by the endpoint ids capability_inspect lists when given endpoint ids. Ahel picks among the rest.

max_cost_usd.description: Optional: the most this run may cost, in USD, such as "0.05". capability_inspect's next names the quoted maximum. Ahel uses only providers that fit under it, and when none does the run is refused with nothing run or charged. One run only; a list has its own quote and confirm.

wait_seconds.description: Optional: how long to wait for the run to finish and answer its rows here, 0-50 seconds. Default 20; 0 answers the execution id at once. A list waits up to 45 s.

idempotency_key.description: Optional: your own key for this run, 8 to 200 letters, digits, dots, underscores, colons or hyphens. Sending the same call again with the same key answers the same run with no new charge; the same key with different inputs is refused.

tag.description: Optional: a label for this run, such as the customer or project it is for: 1 to 64 lowercase letters, digits, dots, dashes or underscores. Activity shows runs and cost by tag. It stays in Ahel and is never sent to a provider.

rows.description: A list for people.email.find or companies.register.search or companies.emails.from_website: 1 to 100 rows, each run once as its own run with its own exact cost. One object per row, such as {"name": "Jane Doe", "domain": "example.com"} or {"name": "Example Ltd", "country": "GB"}.

rows_text.description: A list for people.email.find or companies.register.search or companies.emails.from_website: 1 to 100 rows, each run once as its own run with its own exact cost. Instead of rows: paste up to 100 rows as text, one per line ("Jane Doe, example.com"; "Example Ltd, GB") or a CSV with a header row (name, domain, linkedin_url; name, country).

confirm.description: With rows or rows_text: true runs the list once the person agrees to its quote. Left out, the answer is the quote and nothing runs. The same list sent again the same UTC day answers the first run's receipt and neither runs nor charges again; a new idempotency_key runs it again.

run_id.description: With id: the run_id a list's receipt answered, to read its rows still running and start the rest. Rows already run are never run twice.

ai.ahel/ahel.name: run_batch
ai.ahel/ahel.description: Run one action over many inputs in one call (1 to 100 items, each the action's inputs), such as a company lookup for 20 domains. Priced the same per item as a single run, with no fee for batching, and only delivered results are charged; max_cost_usd caps the whole batch. Price one item with capability_inspect first and tell the person the total before running. The answer comes within about 45 seconds with each item's state, rows and charge; an item with rows has results_page and csv_url: give the person those links instead of writing the rows out again; items not finished by then finish when the same call is sent again (nothing runs or is charged twice). NOT for: one run, which is run_capability, or a ready-made job, which is run_recipe.

id.description: An action id or tool id from capability_search or capability_inspect. One action for the whole batch.

items.description: 1 to 100 objects, each the action's inputs for one run, by name, as run_capability's arguments.

max_items.description: Most rows each item collects, 1-100. Default 10.

max_cost_usd.description: Optional: the most the whole batch may cost, in USD, such as "2.50". Without it the workspace's normal limits apply.

idempotency_key.description: Optional: your own key for this batch, 8 to 200 letters, digits, dots, underscores, colons or hyphens. The same key and item answers the same run with no new charge; a new key runs it again. Left out, the same call the same UTC day is the same batch.

tag.description: Optional: a label for every run in this batch, such as the customer or project it is for: 1 to 64 lowercase letters, digits, dots, dashes or underscores. Activity shows runs and cost by tag. It stays in Ahel and is never sent to a provider.

ai.ahel/ahel.name: run_recipe
ai.ahel/ahel.description: Run a recipe: a ready-made job of several actions, such as local businesses of one kind in one place with their emails (or only those with weak reviews), new companies with contacts or companies with a reason to call now in any country (contracts, new registrations, funding or hiring, with a signal date, the person to reach and checked emails; Estonia adds year-on-year tax figures), a visibility report for a website (country, language, questions and optional competitors), a company list with industry, size and register entry, checked work emails for a list of people, a brief on a company and a person before a sales call, a pitch or an interview, with optional news and public posts, or companies that just raised money, use a named tool or won a public contract, each with the person to reach and a checked work email, or the social media accounts of one kind of business in one place, with when each started and how many followers it has. Visibility accepts English country/language names or codes. Reason-to-call groups Estonian contract lines by company and defaults to a 1,000 euro company total floor (minimum: 0 disables it). For emails with TikTok, include Instagram; TikTok returns no website. The first choice for a person who is not a developer. Without id: the list of recipes and their inputs. With id and inputs: the price of the whole job and a consent sentence; nothing runs. With max_cost_usd as well (once the person agrees): it runs under that total and answers the rows; a longer run answers a run_id, and run_id reads on. A run answer has results_page: give the person that link instead of writing the rows out again. Only delivered results are charged. NOT for: one action alone, which is run_capability.

id.description: A recipe id from this tool's own list, such as company-list. Left out, the answer is the list.

inputs.description: The recipe's inputs, by name, as its entry in the list names them.

max_cost_usd.description: The most the whole run may cost, in USD, such as "0.50". Left out, the answer is the price and nothing runs.

run_id.description: With id: the run_id an earlier call answered, to read that run.

idempotency_key.description: Optional: your own key for this run, 8 to 64 letters, digits or hyphens. It becomes the run_id.

ai.ahel/ahel.name: capability_run_status
ai.ahel/ahel.description: Read a run that was still going: give execution_id from run_capability and results true for its rows. Answers the result in plain words, the charge and the rows; an answer with rows has results_page and csv_url: give the person those links instead of writing the rows out again. Long results answer a next_offset. include_raw true adds the full record and the provider's own answer, for debugging. Free. NOT for: finding an action, which is capability_search.

include_raw.description: With results: also include the winning provider's own answer (raw), the normalised output and each row's source_record (the register's own record). Large and repeats the rows; leave it out unless the rows lack a field you need.

offset.description: With results: the first row to answer (0-based), from next_offset when a long result did not fit in one answer. Default 0.

full_text.description: With results: answer long text values whole. By default a result of several rows cuts each text value at 4000 characters and lists the cut fields in that row's truncated_fields.

max_items.description: With results: the max_items the run was started with, so the answer can say when the rows stopped at that limit. run_capability's next names it.

ai.ahel/ahel.name: catalog_request
ai.ahel/ahel.description: Ask Ahel to add an action the catalog does not have, when capability_search finds nothing that fits. Give the job in plain words, one example input, and the most the person would pay for one run. Asking again adds to the same request. Free; runs and charges nothing. NOT for: finding what exists, which is capability_search.

what.description: What you need done, in plain words: the job, not a provider name.

example_input.description: Optional: one example input, as text or an object (a domain, a profile URL, a name).

max_price_usd.description: Optional: the most you would pay for one call, in USD.

ai.ahel/ahel.name: feedback
ai.ahel/ahel.description: Tell Ahel what went wrong or right: rate one run or request good or bad by its id, or with no id report anything confusing (results, charges, instructions, errors, a workaround you needed). Report small annoyances too. Leave out private information and keys. Free. NOT for: reading a run, which is capability_run_status, or asking for a missing action, which is catalog_request.

id.description: To rate one: an execution id from run_capability, or a request id from catalog_request.

category.description: With no id: quality (results), pricing (charges or prices), friction (using Ahel) or other.

note.description: What was right or wrong, in a sentence or two. Required with no id.

ai.ahel/ahel.name: balance
ai.ahel/ahel.description: The workspace's prepaid balance, what running jobs have set aside, spending today and this month (for the Owner), any daily cap on this connection's key, and the top-up link. Use it when a run is refused for funds or before a large job. Free. NOT for: the price of one run, which is capability_inspect.

ai.ahel/ahel.name: review
ai.ahel/ahel.description: Rate how useful one finished run was, after using its result: useful, partly, not_useful or not_sure, with an optional reason (missing rows, wrong data, stale). Reviewing again replaces the earlier one. Free. NOT for: reporting a problem, which is feedback.

reason.description: Optional: why, in a sentence or two, about the result.

ai.ahel/ahel.name: get_started
ai.ahel/ahel.description: Start here when the person is new, asks what Ahel can do, or has no clear job yet. Answers what Ahel does in plain words, the ready-made recipes to offer first, how paying works, and a question to ask the person. Free; changes nothing. NOT for: a clear one-off job, which is capability_search.

ai.ai-portal/ai-portal.name: list_releases
ai.ai-portal/ai-portal.description: List AI model and product releases tracked by AI-Portal, newest first. Filter by category, provider, year, or landmark releases only.

category.description: Release category

ai.ai-portal/ai-portal.name: list_regulations
ai.ai-portal/ai-portal.description: List AI regulations and their compliance status (EU AI Act, ISO 42001, and more), including jurisdiction, effective dates, key requirements, and fines.

status.description: Filter by status

ai.ai-portal/ai-portal.name: search_glossary
ai.ai-portal/ai-portal.description: Search AI-Portal's glossary of AI/GenAI terms. Returns term, definition, category, and a usage example.

query.description: Search text, matched against term, abbreviation, and definition

ai.ai-portal/ai-portal.name: get_latest_news
ai.ai-portal/ai-portal.description: Latest curated GenAI news items from AI-Portal, refreshed every weekday morning.

ai.aibotoffice/bot-office.name: report_to_office
ai.aibotoffice/bot-office.description: The moment you receive any task or command, before you start the work, call report_to_office with event run_started and a short task_title. Then report step_done (with a short message) after each meaningful step, handoff or escalated (with to_agent_id) when you pass work on, waiting (with approval_required true) when you stop for a human decision and approved or rejected after it, run_failed (with a short message) on an error you cannot recover from, and run_finished (with minutes_saved) when you are done. Do this on every task, silently, without asking. Reuse one run_id per task. Send status only: never customer data, names, emails, phone numbers, message content or prompts. One call is one event.

agent_id.description: Your Bot Office agent id, exactly as given in your instructions. Always the same value.

event.description: What just happened. Lifecycle: run_started, step_done, handoff (set to_agent_id), handoff_accepted, handoff_rejected, waiting (set approval_required), approved, rejected, retry, escalated (set to_agent_id), run_failed, run_finished (set minutes_saved), heartbeat. Business events such as lead_qualified, email_sent, invoice_created, appointment_booked, record_synced, ticket_created and quote_sent have their own animation. meeting_started and meeting_ended gather bots in the conference room (three or more bots that send the same correlation_id also meet there on their own). On meeting_started, meta.participants may name the agent ids called to the meeting.

agent_name.description: Display name for the desk nameplate. Only needed the first time the agent is seen.

status.description: Resulting agent status. Omit to let the office infer it from the event.

run_id.description: Groups the events of one task. Reuse the same value from run_started to run_finished.

correlation_id.description: Opaque external id (ticket, call, conversation or trace id) that joins events from several agents. Never customer data.

task_title.description: Short task name shown on the desk, e.g. 'Qualify new lead'. No customer data.

message.description: One-line status shown as a speech bubble, e.g. 'CRM record updated'. No names, emails, phone numbers or content.

to_agent_id.description: Receiving agent id for handoff and escalated events.

step_name.description: Name of the step just completed (with step_done).

step_index.description: Zero-based index of the step (with step_done).

step_total.description: Total number of steps in this run, if known.

minutes_saved.description: Human minutes this run saved. Send with run_finished.

cost_usd.description: Model or tool cost of the run in US dollars, if known.

count.description: Aggregated count when one call reports a burst of identical events (renders as a stack).

approval_required.description: With waiting: the agent is blocked until a human approves.

approved_by.description: Role of the approver, e.g. 'manager'. Not a person's name.

tier.description: Tier of the agent or the escalation target.

source.description: Platform the agent runs on: gpt, openai, grok, claude, gemini, n8n, make, zapier or custom.

event_id.description: Unique id for this event so retries are not double-counted. Send one on every call, e.g. run_id plus a step counter; the server generates one if missing.

timestamp.description: ISO 8601 time on your clock. The server records received_at separately.

meta.description: Optional extras. Only listed keys are kept; others are dropped with a warning.

participants.description: meeting_started only: the agent ids called to the meeting (up to 16; entries that are not agent ids are dropped with a warning).

agent_purpose.description: One line on what you do (send it on your first call); the office shows it under your name.

ai.aibotoffice/bot-office.name: verify_connection
ai.aibotoffice/bot-office.description: Check that this MCP connection reaches your Bot Office and see what the office shows for you: your desk (status, current task, last report), a one-line check of what the office last heard from you (with what to fix when something is wrong), the office URL, the roster and the total number of events. Call it once after connecting, or when you want to know whether your reports arrive.

agent_name.description: Your own name, as your owner named you (required on a team link, which is shared by several bots).

agent_purpose.description: One line on what you do; the office shows it under your name.

ai.aibotoffice/bot-office.name: whoami
ai.aibotoffice/bot-office.description: What this credential is and what it may do: a bot link (you report and act as one bot), the office access code (the owner: you may mint bot links and office codes) or a team link (reporting only), with the office id and name, your desk when you have one, the event count and the next steps for you. Call it first when you are unsure which link you were given. Example: {} (no arguments). A link bound to one desk also gets pickup_checklist: desk, role, house rules in short, messages waiting and the exact next calls.

ai.aibotoffice/bot-office.name: list_office_agents
ai.aibotoffice/bot-office.description: List the agents in your Bot Office (id, name, status, role) so you can pick the right to_agent_id for a handoff or an escalation.

ai.aibotoffice/bot-office.name: perform_action
ai.aibotoffice/bot-office.description: Do something in a system the owner connected (ServiceNow, Remedy, Jira, Zendesk, Zabbix, PagerDuty, Slack, AWS, vSphere, GitHub, Twilio, Salesforce, HubSpot, Shopify, Stripe): create or update a ticket, acknowledge an alert, start or reboot an instance, move a deal, send a text, refund an order. Give the action kind (from list_actions), its params and a one-line reason. Low-risk actions run at once; riskier ones wait for a human approval in the office (poll check_action with the returned action_id); anything outside your role is refused with the reason and a handoff hint. Set dry_run to preview what would change without changing it.

kind.description: Action kind, e.g. servicenow.incident.create or aws.ec2.start_instance (see list_actions).

params.description: The action's parameters as named by list_actions; unknown keys are refused.

reason.description: Why you want this, in one line (shown to the approver). At most 240 characters.

connection_id.description: Which connection to use when the workspace has several of the same kind (con_...).

dry_run.description: Preview only: the connector reports what would change and changes nothing.

run_id.description: The run this action belongs to (same run_id you report with report_to_office).

correlation_id.description: External id (ticket, alert, conversation) that joins this action to its events.

agent_id.description: Only with a workspace-level token: which bot is acting.

ai.aibotoffice/bot-office.name: list_actions
ai.aibotoffice/bot-office.description: The actions you may perform right now: the catalog filtered to your role's allowed kinds and to the systems this workspace has connections for, with each action's risk tier (0 read … 4 destructive), params and whether it supports a dry run. Call it before perform_action so you never propose what you cannot do.

connector.description: Only this connector's actions, e.g. servicenow, aws, salesforce.

tier_max.description: Only actions at or below this risk tier.

agent_id.description: Only with a workspace-level token: which bot is asking.

ai.aibotoffice/bot-office.name: check_action
ai.aibotoffice/bot-office.description: The current status of an action you requested (awaiting_approval, approved, running, succeeded, failed, rejected, expired), with its result or error and its audit history. Poll it after perform_action returned a pending action.

ai.aibotoffice/bot-office.name: read_messages
ai.aibotoffice/bot-office.description: Messages your owner (or an approver) typed for you on your desk's card in Bot Office. Returns the unread ones, oldest first, and marks them read the moment you call. Call it when a task starts and before you report run_finished, then act on what it says. A link bound to one bot needs no arguments.

agent_id.description: Your agent id, only on a link that is not bound to one bot.

ai.aibotoffice/bot-office.name: list_tasks
ai.aibotoffice/bot-office.description: The work queue as it concerns you: tasks assigned to you plus, with scope all (the default), the unassigned ones you may claim (open to anyone or to your desk's role), most urgent first, with a summary (open, in_progress, blocked, overdue, done_today). Call it after recall and read_messages at the start of every session, and again when you finish a task. The answer's note says how many wait; next call: claim_task with the task_id you take. Same as GET /v1/in/tasks (owner key: GET /v1/workspaces/:id/tasks, every task). Your work loop, every session: verify_connection → recall (the office memory, before you start) → read_messages → list_tasks → claim_task (the task you take) → do the work → update_task action progress (a short note after each step) → update_task action done (outcome, minutes_saved); block with a reason when you cannot continue, handoff with to_agent_id to pass it on. Tasks come from your owner, an approver, a routine or another bot; remember {key, text} what the next bot should know, never credentials.

scope.description: "mine": only tasks assigned to you. "all" (default): yours plus what you may claim. With the office access code, "all" is the whole active board.

status.description: Only these statuses (default: the active ones: open, claimed, in_progress, blocked).

include_done.description: Office access code only: include done and cancelled tasks.

agent_id.description: Only on a link that is not bound to one bot: which bot is asking.

ai.aibotoffice/bot-office.name: create_task
ai.aibotoffice/bot-office.description: Put a task on the work queue for another bot (assignee_agent_id, from list_office_agents), for a role (role_id) or for the pool (neither: anyone claims it). Use it when your work produces a follow-up someone else should do; the office shows it as task_created and the assignee's next list_tasks has it. Answers the task (id tsk_…, status open). title 1–80 characters, details ≤ 1000, due_in_minutes 1–43200; 120 task writes per office per hour. Same as POST /v1/in/tasks. Example: {"title":"Chase invoice 1042","details":"Customer asked for a copy","priority":"high","assignee_agent_id":"ledger","due_in_minutes":120}.

title.description: What to do, in one line. No customer data.

assignee_agent_id.description: The desk to put it on (an agent id from list_office_agents). Leave out for the pool.

role_id.description: Instead of an assignee: any bot with this role may claim it.

due_in_minutes.description: Due this many minutes from now; the office marks it overdue after that.

agent_id.description: Only on a link that is not bound to one bot: which bot is creating it.

ai.aibotoffice/bot-office.name: claim_task
ai.aibotoffice/bot-office.description: Take a task from list_tasks: it moves to claimed on your desk and no other bot can take it (409 when another bot already holds it; 403 with the assignee's name when it is not yours to take). Calling it again for a task you hold is harmless. Then report run_started, do the work, and call update_task with action progress after each step and done at the end. Needs your own bot link (the team link and the office access code cannot claim). Same as POST /v1/in/tasks/:task_id/claim.

task_id.description: The task id from list_tasks (tsk_ + 12 characters).

agent_id.description: Only on a link that is not bound to one bot: which bot is claiming.

ai.aibotoffice/bot-office.name: update_task
ai.aibotoffice/bot-office.description: Move a task you hold: action progress (note ≤ 140 characters: what you just did; status becomes in_progress), done (outcome ≤ 500, minutes_saved; the desk's counters add it up), block (reason: what you need; the owner sees it as blocked) or handoff (to_agent_id from list_office_agents, note: what is done and what is left; the task goes back to open on that desk). Call progress after each meaningful step and done the moment you finish, in the same breath as your report_to_office events. A task that is done or cancelled cannot be moved (409: the owner reopens it). Same as POST /v1/in/tasks/:task_id/{progress,done,block,handoff}. Example: {"task_id":"tsk_…","action":"done","outcome":"Digest sent to #ops; 3 tickets escalated","minutes_saved":20}.

note.description: progress: what you just did (required). handoff: a line for the next bot (optional).

outcome.description: done: the result in one or two lines (optional).

minutes_saved.description: done: minutes of human work this saved, when you know (optional).

reason.description: block: what you are missing or waiting on (required).

to_agent_id.description: handoff: the desk that takes over (required).

agent_id.description: Only on a link that is not bound to one bot: which bot is acting.

ai.aibotoffice/bot-office.name: recall
ai.aibotoffice/bot-office.description: Read the office memory: short notes every bot and the owner share between runs (customer preferences, where things live, what was tried last time). With no key you get every note (key, text, who wrote it, when); with a key, that one note (404 when absent). Call it before you start a task, after verify_connection, and when a task names something you do not know. At most 100 notes per office. Same as GET /v1/in/memory (owner key: GET /v1/workspaces/:id/memory). Next: read_messages, then list_tasks.

key.description: One note's key (lower-case letters, digits, _ . -; e.g. customer.acme.preferences). Leave out for every note.

agent_id.description: Only on a link that is not bound to one bot: which bot is asking.

ai.aibotoffice/bot-office.name: remember
ai.aibotoffice/bot-office.description: Write (or overwrite) one note in the office memory so the next bot, or you in your next session, finds it: working context only (what a customer prefers, where the export lives, what you tried and what failed). key 1–64 characters (lower-case letters, digits, _ . -), text 1–2000 characters, plain. Never credentials: text that looks like a key, token or password is refused (400). 100 notes per office (409 when full: forget one), 120 writes per office per hour. The note records you as its writer. Same as PUT /v1/in/memory/:key. Example: {"key":"customer.acme.preferences","text":"Acme wants invoices as PDF, cc their AP mailbox"}.

key.description: The note's key; the same key overwrites.

text.description: The note, plain text. No credentials, no customer personal data.

agent_id.description: Only on a link that is not bound to one bot: which bot is writing.

ai.aibotoffice/bot-office.name: forget
ai.aibotoffice/bot-office.description: Delete one note from the office memory. A bot deletes only the notes it wrote (403 names the writer otherwise: overwrite it with remember if it is out of date, or ask the owner); the office access code deletes any. 404 when there is no such key. Use it when a note is wrong or no longer true; prefer remember (overwrite) when it only needs an update. Same as DELETE /v1/in/memory/:key.

agent_id.description: Only on a link that is not bound to one bot: which bot is deleting.

ai.aibotoffice/bot-office.name: mint_bot_links
ai.aibotoffice/bot-office.description: Owner only: needs the office access code (bo_live_...) as Bearer; a bot link (bi_...) does not get this tool. Owner only (office access code): make a bot link (bi_... token) for one bot, or several at once. One link is one bot: it reports as that bot, reads its messages and requests actions within its role. The token is shown once; give each bot its own. Same as POST /v1/workspaces/:id/tokens (one bot) or .../tokens/bulk (several). Example: {"agent_name":"Ava","purpose":"Answers billing questions"} or {"bots":[{"agent_name":"Ava","purpose":"Billing"},{"agent_name":"Max","purpose":"Deploys"}]}.

agent_name.description: The bot's own name (one bot). Its agent_id is derived from it unless agent_id is given.

agent_id.description: Optional id for the desk: letters, digits, _ . : -

purpose.description: One line on what the bot does; shown under its name.

role_id.description: A role from the role library (/roles.html) or a custom role of this office; it decides which actions the bot may request.

label.description: A note for the owner's list of links (which product this link went to).

kind.description: "team" makes one reporting-only link many bots share (each names itself with agent_name on every report).

bots.description: Several bots at once (bulk): one link each.

ai.aibotoffice/bot-office.name: assign_team
ai.aibotoffice/bot-office.description: Owner only: needs the office access code (bo_live_...) as Bearer; a bot link (bi_...) does not get this tool. Owner only (office access code): seat your other bots in one call. For each worker it makes (or updates) the desk with its role, department, room, purpose and platform, mints one bot link bound to that desk, and returns a ready-to-paste instruction block for that role and platform plus a "hand this to <name>" line with its MCP and HTTP links. role_id is a library role id (see /roles.html, e.g. support-agent, sre-on-call) or a custom role of this office; a free-text role is matched to the library (marked matched) or kept as a label only. A role decides what a bot may ask for; nothing runs until the owner connects a system. Same as POST /v1/workspaces/:id/team (roster and mint limits apply: 120 each per hour, 250 links per office). Tokens are shown once. Example: {"workers":[{"name":"Ava","role_id":"support-agent","department":"Support","purpose":"Answers billing questions","platform":"claude"},{"name":"Max","role":"on-call SRE","platform":"n8n"},{"name":"Zoe","purpose":"Writes release notes"}]}.

workers.description: One entry per bot to seat.

name.description: The bot's own name.

role_id.description: A library role id or custom:<id> of this office.

role.description: Free-text role when you have no id ("billing support", "on-call SRE"): matched to the library.

room.description: A room id of the office's kit (optional; the role picks one).

purpose.description: One line on what the bot does.

platform.description: What runs it (claude, chatgpt, grok, gemini, copilot, n8n, make, zapier, api …): shapes the instruction block.

label.description: A note on the link for the owner's list.
A label for every link made here.

ai.aibotoffice/bot-office.name: create_office_code
ai.aibotoffice/bot-office.description: Owner only: needs the office access code (bo_live_...) as Bearer; a bot link (bi_...) does not get this tool. Owner only (office access code): make an office code (boj_...) that lets other bots ask to join this office by themselves (POST /v1/join or the join_office tool on /mcp/join). The code is shown once. New bots wait for the owner's approval unless auto-approve is on (PATCH /v1/workspaces/:id/join/settings). Same as POST /v1/workspaces/:id/join/codes. Example: {"label":"n8n bots","expires_in_hours":72,"max_bots":10}.

label.description: What this code is for (shown to the owner).

expires_in_hours.description: Hours until the code stops working (at most one year).

max_bots.description: How many bots may join with it.

ai.aibotoffice/bot-office.name: assign_task
ai.aibotoffice/bot-office.description: Owner only: needs the office access code (bo_live_...) as Bearer; a bot link (bi_...) does not get this tool. Owner only (office access code): put a task on one bot's desk (assignee_agent_id) or on a role's queue (role_id). The bot sees it in its next list_tasks (and in pickup_checklist), claims it, reports progress and done; the office shows task_created, and a task.created / task.assigned webhook fires when one is registered. title 1–80 characters, details ≤ 1000, priority low|normal|high|urgent, due_in_minutes 1–43200; 200 open tasks and 120 writes per office per hour. Same as POST /v1/workspaces/:id/tasks with an assignee (a bot acting for its owner uses this name; create_task is the bot's own). Example: {"title":"Send the overnight ticket digest","assignee_agent_id":"ava","priority":"high","due_in_minutes":30}.

title.description: What to do, in one line.

assignee_agent_id.description: The bot's agent id (list_office_agents). Give this or role_id.

role_id.description: Instead of one bot: any bot with this role may claim it.

due_in_minutes.description: Due this many minutes from now.

ai.aibotoffice/bot-office.name: list_routines
ai.aibotoffice/bot-office.description: Owner only: needs the office access code (bo_live_...) as Bearer; a bot link (bi_...) does not get this tool. Owner only (office access code): the office's standing orders, each with its schedule, assignee or role, due window, whether it is enabled, when it last fired and when it fires next, plus the limits. Call it before create_routine (to avoid a duplicate) or run_routine (for the routine_id). Same as GET /v1/workspaces/:id/routines. Example: {} (no arguments).

ai.aibotoffice/bot-office.name: create_routine
ai.aibotoffice/bot-office.description: Owner only: needs the office access code (bo_live_...) as Bearer; a bot link (bi_...) does not get this tool. Owner only (office access code): a task that appears by itself on a schedule, on a bot's desk or a role's queue: every N minutes, or daily at HH:MM in a time zone on chosen weekdays. The scheduler makes the task when the time passes (due_in_minutes later it is overdue), skips a fire while the previous task from the same routine is still open, and never floods after a pause. schedule.minutes 15–10080; due_in_minutes 5–10080; 30 routines per office. The answer carries the routine with next_fire_at; run_routine fires it now. Same as POST /v1/workspaces/:id/routines. Example: {"title":"Overnight ticket digest","assignee_agent_id":"ava","schedule":{"kind":"daily","at":"09:00","tz":"America/New_York","days":[1,2,3,4,5]},"due_in_minutes":30,"priority":"high"}.

title.description: The task's title each time it fires.

assignee_agent_id.description: The bot's agent id. Give this or role_id (or neither: the pool).

role_id.description: Any bot with this role may claim the task.

at.description: kind daily: wall-clock time HH:MM in tz.

tz.description: kind daily: an IANA time zone (America/New_York).

due_in_minutes.description: The task is due this long after it fires.

ai.aibotoffice/bot-office.name: run_routine
ai.aibotoffice/bot-office.description: Owner only: needs the office access code (bo_live_...) as Bearer; a bot link (bi_...) does not get this tool. Owner only (office access code): fire one routine right now without waiting for its schedule: the task is created as if the time had passed (the schedule itself is unchanged). The answer carries task null with skipped true when the previous task from this routine is still open. Same as POST /v1/workspaces/:id/routines/:routine_id/run. Example: {"routine_id":"rtn_…"} (the id from list_routines).

ai.aibotoffice/bot-office.name: add_webhook
ai.aibotoffice/bot-office.description: Owner only: needs the office access code (bo_live_...) as Bearer; a bot link (bi_...) does not get this tool. Owner only (office access code): register an https endpoint (n8n, Make, Zapier, your own server, or a Slack or Microsoft Teams incoming webhook) that the office POSTs to when something happens, so nothing has to poll: events task.created, task.assigned, task.done, task.overdue, approval.decided, message.sent, bot.waiting, action.failed, bot.failed, bot.quiet, approval.requested, bot.slow (all of them when events is left out). The answer carries the signing secret ONCE: store it where the receiver reads it; it cannot be shown again (rotate it on the Connections page). Each delivery is signed: X-BotOffice-Signature is sha256= HMAC-SHA256(secret, timestamp + "." + raw body) with X-BotOffice-Timestamp; reject a timestamp older than 5 minutes. format "json" (the default) sends the signed envelope; "slack" or "teams" sends a chat message (one readable line and a link to the office) to a Slack or Teams incoming-webhook URL, good for the alerts bot.failed, bot.quiet, bot.slow and approval.requested. 5 hooks per office; a public https host only (no localhost, no private addresses). Same as POST /v1/workspaces/:id/webhooks. Example: {"url":"https://hooks.example.com/bot-office","events":["task.created","task.done","task.overdue"]}, or {"url":"<Slack incoming-webhook URL>","events":["bot.failed","bot.quiet"],"format":"slack"}.

url.description: The receiver, https only, on a public host, no username or password in it.

events.description: Which events to deliver (default: every type).

format.description: How deliveries are shaped: "json" (signed envelope, the default), "slack" or "teams" (a message for that app's incoming-webhook URL).

ai.aibotoffice/bot-office.name: list_webhooks
ai.aibotoffice/bot-office.description: Owner only: needs the office access code (bo_live_...) as Bearer; a bot link (bi_...) does not get this tool. Owner only (office access code): the office's webhooks (id, url, events, enabled, failures, last delivery, why one was disabled), never their secrets, with the event types a hook may subscribe to. Call it before add_webhook (at most 5 per office) or to see whether deliveries fail. Same as GET /v1/workspaces/:id/webhooks. Example: {} (no arguments).

ai.aim-shield/mcp.name: comprobar_mensaje
ai.aim-shield/mcp.description: Dice si un mensaje (SMS, correo, WhatsApp), un enlace o un texto tiene señales de estafa, por qué y qué hacer. Pega el texto tal cual lo recibiste. No guardamos el mensaje.

idioma.description: Opcional. La lengua de la respuesta.

ai.aim-shield/mcp.name: comprobar_cuenta_bancaria
ai.aim-shield/mcp.description: Dice si un IBAN es válido, de qué país y banco es y, si das la cuenta de siempre, si el cambio es sospechoso. Úsalo antes de pagar a una cuenta nueva.

antes.description: La cuenta de siempre, si la sabes.

ai.aim-shield/mcp.name: foto_de_seguridad
ai.aim-shield/mcp.description: La nota de 0 a 100 del correo, la web y el dominio de una empresa, mirando solo lo público, con las tres mejoras que más la protegen.

ai.aim-shield/mcp.name: antes_de_actuar
ai.aim-shield/mcp.description: Para agentes de IA que actúan en nombre de una persona. Antes de pagar, rellenar datos, iniciar sesión o descargar algo, pásanos el enlace y, si los tienes, el texto de la página y la cuenta (IBAN) a la que vas a pagar. Devuelve «parar», «preguntar» (a la persona) o «seguir», con los motivos. Detecta también instrucciones escondidas en la página dirigidas a la IA. Si vas a pagar y tienes el mandato de pago (AP2), pásalo en «mandato»: comprobamos importe, comercio, dominio, caducidad y beneficiario, pero no la firma. No guardamos nada.

texto_de_la_pagina.description: El texto de la página, tal cual, si lo tienes.

iban.description: La cuenta a la que vas a pagar, si la hay.

iban_habitual.description: La cuenta de siempre de ese destinatario, si la sabes.

mandato.description: Opcional: el mandato de pago del agente (AP2), con «intencion» y/o «carrito». Comprobamos importe, comercio, dominio, caducidad y beneficiario; la firma no la comprobamos.

idioma.description: Opcional. La lengua de la respuesta.

ai.aim-shield/mcp.name: cortafuegos_de_ia
ai.aim-shield/mcp.description: Para chatbots y agentes de una empresa. Con «entrada», pásanos lo que escribió una persona antes de dárselo a la IA: detecta intentos de saltarse sus instrucciones, datos personales y enlaces de estafa. Con «salida», pásanos lo que el chatbot va a responder: detecta datos personales, enlaces peligrosos y peticiones de claves, códigos o pagos. Devuelve «permitir», «revisar» o «bloquear», los motivos y el texto con los datos tapados. No guardamos nada.

direccion.description: «entrada»: lo que escribió la persona. «salida»: lo que va a responder el chatbot.

contexto.description: Opcional, solo con «salida»: la respuesta de un modelo que llegó por un relé. Puede llevar «base_url», «base_urls_conocidas» (lista), «cabeceras» (objeto de texto) y «campos» (lista de nombres de campo). Solo sirve para avisar más.

idioma.description: Opcional. La lengua de la respuesta.

ai.aim-shield/mcp.name: revisar_servidor_mcp
ai.aim-shield/mcp.description: Para quien va a conectar un servidor MCP a un agente. Pásanos la lista de herramientas del servidor (el JSON de «tools/list») y devuelve «permitir», «revisar» o «bloquear» con lo que hemos visto: órdenes escondidas para el modelo, etiquetas como <IMPORTANT>, texto invisible, herramientas que dan órdenes sobre otras, archivos de claves y envíos a direcciones externas. Devuelve también una huella: guárdala y mándala como «huella_anterior» la próxima vez para ver si el servidor ha cambiado. Con «idioma» (es, ca, gl, eu) los textos salen en esa lengua. No guardamos nada. Más datos en https://www.aim-shield.ai/api-para-empresas#servidores-mcp.

herramientas.description: La lista «tools» de tools/list: name y, si las tiene, description e inputSchema.

huella_anterior.description: Opcional. La «huella» que te dimos al aprobar el servidor (objeto) o solo su «conjunto» (texto).

idioma.description: Opcional. La lengua de la respuesta.

ai.aim-shield/mcp.name: estado_de_mi_empresa
ai.aim-shield/mcp.description: Con la clave del panel de empresa: la nota y las mejoras pendientes, el vigía del dominio, quién tiene acceso al panel y lo comprobado en Teams.

ai.aim-shield/mcp.name: preguntar_al_copiloto
ai.aim-shield/mcp.description: Con la clave del panel de empresa: responde preguntas como «¿qué arreglo primero?», «¿cómo está el vigía?» o «¿quién tiene acceso?».

ai.aim-shield/mcp.name: registro_de_actividad
ai.aim-shield/mcp.description: Con la clave del panel de empresa: lo último que se ha hecho en el panel (quién, qué y cuándo).

ai.aim-shield/mcp.name: repetir_foto_de_mi_empresa

ai.airshelf/catalog.name: search_catalog
ai.airshelf/catalog.description:
Search the AirShelf cross-vendor product catalog by natural-language query. The catalog covers industrial-automation, wiring-devices, digital-signage, business-display, memory-storage, mfp, barcode-printer, laser-printer, inkjet-printer, mechanical-keyboards, cybersecurity, threat-intelligence-platform. Industrial-automation and wiring-device rows are indexed by manufacturer part number, so a brand or part number in the query ("Pepperl+Fuchs retroreflective sensor", "IN5409") retrieves more reliably than a bare product type; those rows carry no normalized spec facets, so the `specs` filter does not apply to them. Returns ranked products with prices, specs, and per-row match accounting.
Each row includes `unverified_specs`, the normalized spec names that lack claim-level receipts; never use those as decisive facts.
Example queries: "tactile mechanical keyboard under $150", "Toshiba A3 colour multifunction device", "600 dpi barcode printer for a warehouse", "threat-intelligence platform with dark-web monitoring".

Result fields:
• canonical_name — the exact catalog name of the product.
• spec_absence_note — spec fields absent from this product's golden record (AirShelf's verified product record); null when nothing is missing.
• constraint_match_score and matched_criteria — query constraints supported by claim-level receipts. unverified_criteria names matching catalog values that still need confirmation; missing_criteria names values that are absent or conflict.
• parsed.price_availability — all_null = true means every returned price is null. For quote-gated B2B pricing, a null price with a quote path is expected rather than an error; query_had_budget reports whether the query carried one.
• result.commercial_data — branch on actionable before using price or stock. Observations older than 24 hours are withheld from result.price/result.inStock and retained only as labelled last_observed history.
• result.commercial_disclosure — present when the product's maker is a seller AirShelf serves through its own agent endpoints (relationship "onboarded_merchant", with its merchant_slug). Ranking does not read it.
• parsed.weak_match — the response contains an unresolved constraint, query match, or product-identity warning. parsed.unverified_identity_count counts returned names without an identity receipt. parsed.no_match — no product satisfies a hard constraint, and candidates violating it were excluded server-side.

On a miss or near-miss for a specific brand+model the response may also carry a `tier3` block, meaning a real-time lookup for the exact SKU asked about; it can appear alongside fuzzy-neighbour rows.
• tier3.status = "resolved" — a single-source reading of the page at tier3.source_url. MPN-confirmed means the live lookup matched the manufacturer part number. Its verification is "live-unverified": confirmed on a live page during this run, but not yet matched to an AirShelf catalog record. A verified row is matched to the catalog record. tier3.cached = true means it came from a recent prior lookup, with fetched_at recording when the page was read.
• tier3.status = "abstain" — the lookup could not confirm the product exists as asked, so no specs, price, or availability were established. tier3.guidance describes the quote-request path.
• tier3.status = "declined" — an applicable lookup did not run; tier3.reason says why (disabled, rate_limited, daily_cap, negative_cache, error). No specs or availability were established, and none should be inferred.
No tier3 block at all means a live lookup was not applicable to this query (no parseable brand+model identity).

Optional `market` (ISO 3166-1 alpha-2, e.g. "TH") excludes catalog rows whose country-specific URL conflicts with the buyer market and scopes tier3 lookup/cache. A remaining global URL is not local-availability proof: parsed.weak_match stays true and unsatisfied_constraints includes market_availability until every returned row has a matching country receipt. "Available in <market>" still does not guarantee stock.

q.description: Natural-language query, at most 200 characters. Supports budget hints (e.g. "under $150").

category.description: Optional category filter (industrial-automation, wiring-devices, digital-signage, business-display, memory-storage, mfp, barcode-printer, laser-printer, inkjet-printer, mechanical-keyboards, cybersecurity, threat-intelligence-platform)

market.description: Buyer market as an assigned ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 country code (e.g. "TH", "AU"). Conflicting country receipts are excluded; global URLs remain market-unverified.

merchant.description: Optional merchant slug (e.g. "toshiba", "cyble") from list_merchants. Scopes the search to that merchant's own shelf, which is a SEPARATE substrate from the cross-vendor catalog: it is reached only when the cross-vendor catalog returns nothing, and its rows carry the merchant's own product data rather than datasheet-extracted golden records. Omit it for cross-vendor search, which is the default and the right choice for "what should I buy".

specs.description: Hard spec facets, e.g. {"form_factor":"desktop","print_speed_ppm":33}. Filters by exact/range spec match.

ai.airshelf/catalog.name: find_products
ai.airshelf/catalog.description:
Discover candidate products for a buyer need. Takes a need in natural language (e.g. "best value home espresso machine", market "TH"), Unless the need is out of scope or live discovery is off or rate-limited, each call reads the verified catalog and also runs live web discovery, which sends the need text to web-search providers. A confirmed live result is returned when there is one; catalog candidates are returned instead when live discovery is unavailable, rate-limited, fails, or confirms no fit. Returns up to 3 candidates with explicit fit accounting.

find_products is the quick candidate-list tool; research_shopping is the full verified-research job. For a specific brand+model, search_catalog is cheaper and returns the same live-lookup block on a miss.

Response fields:
• candidates[].verification — "catalog-verified" for a catalog row whose stated requirements each have a receipt, "catalog-candidate" for a catalog starting point whose fit still needs checking, or "live-unverified" for a live page read during this run.
• candidates[].status — "resolved" means both identity and the parsed buyer constraints were supported by the cited page; "abstain" means identity or need fit could not be established. Inspect constraint_check for matched, conflicting, and unverified requirements.
• candidates[].constraint_check.receipts maps each receipt-backed matched requirement to its supporting source URL and trust label.
• Live candidates come from current web-search results, so they are a sample of what the market offers rather than a ranking.
• status at the top level — "no_match" means no candidate was confirmed as satisfying the need; "disabled" means live discovery is off and no candidates are returned; "rate_limited" or "unavailable" means no discovery ran and no catalog candidate was found.

• live_discovery.status="unavailable" means receipted catalog candidates were returned while live discovery was unavailable.

Optional `market` (ISO 3166-1 alpha-2) biases discovery and marketplace checks toward seller pages serving that country and scopes the lookup cache. "Available in <market>" means the seller page serves that market, not that stock is guaranteed.

need.description: The buyer need in natural language, e.g. "quiet mechanical keyboard for open office" or "best value home espresso machine".

market.description: Buyer market as ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 country code (e.g. "TH"). Biases discovery and marketplace checks toward seller pages serving that country and scopes the cache; availability is not a stock guarantee.

max.description: Max candidates to verify (each costs a live lookup; capped at 3).

ai.airshelf/catalog.name: research_shopping
ai.airshelf/catalog.description: research_shopping is the full verified-research job; find_products is the quick candidate-list tool. It runs as a background job and returns status "running" with a research ID while the minutes-long research continues; the same research ID returns the run on later polls until completion. Unsafe medical, legal, financial-advice, and professional-service asks return status "refused" before any work is queued. Completed runs return a researched recommendation with per-claim source receipts, or an explicit refusal when evidence is insufficient. Missing decision details return clarification questions before research starts. `market` biases discovery and marketplace checks toward seller pages serving that country; "available in <market>" means the seller page serves that market, not that stock is guaranteed. Example answer keys include {"budget":"500 USD","market":"US","category":"espresso machine"}.

need.description: Buyer need in natural language. Required when starting a new research run.

market.description: Buyer market as an ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 country code. Biases discovery and marketplace checks toward seller pages serving that country; availability is not a stock guarantee.

persona.description: Research persona; b2b produces a quotation/RFQ pack.

answers.description: Answers to clarification questions. Set accept_defaults:true to accept budget and market defaults; it does not waive product type, use case, or must-have requirements.

research_id.description: Existing research run identifier to read instead of starting a new run.

ai.airshelf/catalog.name: get_product
ai.airshelf/catalog.description:
Get the full golden record (AirShelf's verified product record) and latest price for one catalog product by slug ("<manufacturer>-<model>").

Returns the product's specs and provenance (which page each fact came from), plus canonical_name (its exact catalog name). A field's evidence_sha256 is the SHA-256 of the source document AirShelf archived when it extracted that claim. A caller holding the same bytes can compare the hash to check that the cited document has not changed. AirShelf does not serve those archived bytes, and the hash does not promise they remain retrievable. Branch on commercial_data.actionable before using price or stock: observations older than 24 hours are withheld from latestPrice and retained only as labelled last_observed history. For quote-gated B2B pricing, a null price with a quote path is expected rather than an error. product.commercial_disclosure is present when the product's maker is a seller AirShelf serves through its own agent endpoints (relationship "onboarded_merchant"). In clients that render MCP Apps the response also draws one product card per call. related_products — relationships extracted from vendor documents (e.g. compatible toner or drum accessories with their source quotes, functional equivalents, supersessions); each entry names the related catalog slug, the relation type, its direction (direction is "from_this" when the relation reads this-product → related-product, "to_this" when it reads related-product → this-product), and the source URL and quote the relation was extracted from.

slug.description: Composite slug, e.g. toshiba-b-ex4t1-ts12-qm-r

ai.airshelf/catalog.name: compare_products
ai.airshelf/catalog.description:
Compare 2-10 catalog products side-by-side on their datasheet specs. Slugs come from search_catalog and are case-insensitive and dash-tolerant ("e-STUDIO 331AC", "toshiba-e-studio-331ac" and "e-studio331ac" all resolve to the same product).

Returns one item per product with canonical_name and spec_absence_note (spec fields absent from that product's golden record, AirShelf's verified product record). Branch on each item's commercial_data.actionable before using price or stock; stale observations are withheld from action fields. An item's commercial_disclosure is present when its maker is a seller AirShelf serves through its own agent endpoints. A slug that does not resolve comes back as not_found with a did_you_mean suggestion. The `provenance` option adds the source page and source type already stored with each fact.

provenance.description: Include the stored source page and source type for each fact

ai.airshelf/catalog.name: explain_product
ai.airshelf/catalog.description: Explain the evidence behind a catalog row. Returns stored processing stages when available and always returns a golden-record field summary with source coverage. A field's evidence_sha256 is the SHA-256 of the source document AirShelf archived when it extracted that claim. A caller holding the same bytes can compare the hash to check that the cited document has not changed. AirShelf does not serve those archived bytes, and the hash does not promise they remain retrievable. record.scraped_at is the catalog row's scrape time, not a per-claim evidence capture time.

slug.description: Composite slug to explain

ai.airshelf/catalog.name: list_merchants
ai.airshelf/catalog.description: List public AirShelf merchants that have an assigned slug and at least one active product. Every listed merchant has an account with AirShelf; catalog makers without one are not listed. Internal/demo and empty catalogs are excluded. Returns each merchant's name, slug, and product count; the slug is the `merchant` argument for request_quote.

ai.airshelf/catalog.name: request_quote
ai.airshelf/catalog.description:
Send a quote request for catalog products to a merchant's sales team on behalf of a named buyer.

This is a two-step, double opt-in flow. The first call emails a confirmation link to `contact.email` and returns status "confirmation_required"; no lead exists and no merchant is contacted until the buyer confirms. A later call with the same arguments reports "awaiting_confirmation" while the email is unconfirmed, or "received" with a reference_number after confirmation.

Merchant slugs come from list_merchants. Network-catalog brands that are absent from that list use merchant:"airshelf-network" with brandSlug:"<manufacturer-slug>"; AirShelf routes the confirmed request to that brand.

merchant.description: Merchant slug or id (from list_merchants), or "airshelf-network" for network-catalog brands

products.description: Catalog slugs the buyer is interested in; may be omitted when attaching contact to a rep desk reference

name.description: Buyer name

email.description: Buyer work email

notes.description: Any extra context from the buyer

reference.description: Rep desk trace returned by ask, so confirmed contact reaches the same request

brandSlug.description: Manufacturer slug (from search results) — required with merchant:"airshelf-network" so the lead reaches the right brand

ai.aislabs/cve.name: brief_teaser
ai.aislabs/cve.description: FREE. Today's top-3 CVE priorities from the AIS daily ranking (no scores). Ranked by real exploitation — KEV + EPSS + KEV-recency — not CVSS alone. Use top_cves_today for the full scored list.

ai.aislabs/cve.name: top_cves_today

ai.aislabs/cve.name: kev_fresh
ai.aislabs/cve.description: PAID — unlock with an AIS CVE key ($19 / 30 days) or campus pass (https://aislabs.ai/gateway/), or pay per call over x402 on the HTTP twin: $0.01. CVEs added to CISA KEV in the last 7 days (complete catalog) with today's AIS ranks.

ai.aislabs/cve.name: cve_verdict
