ai.arcangel/trademark-search.name: update_company
ai.arcangel/trademark-search.description: Change fields on a saved company (id from list_companies). Only the fields passed change. A draft already linked to the company picks up the change when company_id is passed again or the draft is opened on arcangel.ai. Requires Sign in with Arcangel.

id.description: Company id from list_companies.

legal_name.description: Registered legal name, e.g. "Lumora Labs LLC".

entity_type.description: c_corp, s_corp, llc, llp, lp (limited partnership), general_partnership, sole_proprietorship, nonprofit or other.

registered_state.description: US state where the company is registered (formed), e.g. Delaware. Can differ from the address.

address_line2.description: Suite or unit. null clears it.

city.description: City.

state_province.description: State or province of the address.

country.description: Country of the address, e.g. United States.

ai.arclan/registry.name: query_registry
ai.arclan/registry.description: Search the Arclan registry for MCP servers. By default returns only connectable servers (active, mcp_partial, auth_gated). Use status=stdio to browse local-only servers available for installation. Use status=all to query the full index. Use production_safe=true to restrict to servers with uptime > 97% and handshake success > 95%. Use read_only=true to restrict to servers with no write or exec tools. Use this before connecting to an MCP server to check its validation status and score. After using a server, call report_server to contribute reliability data.

capability.description: Filter by tool name or keyword (searches name, description, tools)

status.description: Filter by state. Default (omit): connectable states only (active + mcp_partial + auth_gated). Use "stdio" for local-install catalog. Use "all" for the full index.

production_safe.description: Only return servers with uptime_7d > 97% and handshake_success_rate > 95%. Use when reliability matters.

read_only.description: Only return servers with no write or exec tools — safe for read-only agent workflows.

ai.arclan/registry.name: get_server
ai.arclan/registry.description: Get full details for a specific MCP server. Pass the server name (e.g. "GitHub", "Brave Search"), registry ID slug, or endpoint URL. Returns score, state, tools list, latency, and recent test history.

url.description: The MCP server endpoint URL (e.g. "https://mcp.example.com/mcp")

id.description: Server name, registry ID slug, or any identifier (e.g. "github", "brave-search", "gateway-pipeworx-io-rpc-mcp")

ai.arclan/registry.name: recommend_server
ai.arclan/registry.description: Get ranked MCP server recommendations for a task. Returns servers scored by production safety, keyword relevance, registry score, latency, and freshness. Each result includes a reason code array explaining why it was ranked. Use this instead of query_registry when you want an opinionated ranked list rather than a filtered search.

q.description: Task or capability query — e.g. "search the web" or "read files"

auth.description: Include servers that require authentication (default: true)

read_only.description: Only return servers with no write-classified tools

ai.arclan/registry.name: report_server
ai.arclan/registry.description: Submit an agent usage report for an MCP server. Reports are aggregated and influence registry trust scores. Call this after using an MCP server so the registry can track real-world reliability. Supports both a simple outcome report and a structured scoring report (criterion + component_score).

serverUrl.description: The MCP server endpoint URL that was used

toolsUsed.description: List of tool names that were called

turnsRequired.description: Number of turns to complete the task

taskDescription.description: Brief description of what the task was

errors.description: Array of error strings encountered during tool use

criterion.description: Specific reliability criterion being scored (enables structured component scoring)

severity.description: Severity of the worst issue encountered

environment.description: Environment the server was used in

evidenceRef.description: Trace ID, log URL, or other reference supporting this report

ai.arclan/registry.name: sign_in
ai.arclan/registry.description: Start GitHub sign-in to get an Arclan API key, without leaving MCP (OAuth device flow). Returns a verification URL and a short user_code — show both to the user and ask them to authorize in a browser. Then call complete_sign_in with the returned device_code to mint the key. A key raises your MCP rate limit above the keyless tier and tracks your usage.

ai.arclan/registry.name: complete_sign_in
ai.arclan/registry.description: Finish the GitHub sign-in started by sign_in and return a new Arclan API key. Pass the device_code from sign_in. If the user has not authorized in the browser yet, this returns status "pending" — wait poll_interval_seconds and call again. The api_key is shown ONCE; store it and send it as "Authorization: Bearer <key>".

ai.arcreport/ask.name: before_checkout
ai.arcreport/ask.description: Call this right before your agent tries to check out at a store, or when a user asks "can my agent check out at <store>?". Not for an attempt that already happened (log it with report_outcome), the reason an agent keeps failing (why_blocked_and_fix), or choosing between 2 or more stores (compare). Returns a one-line answer, reaches_checkout (true only when a checkout link came back or a shopper reached checkout; false when a route was measured and did not reach checkout; null when not shown either way: no agent catalog found and no browser test is null, and so is a product added to the cart with no shopper reaching checkout; null is not a no), protocol_route, browser_route, standard_shoppers when ARC's standard shoppers tried the store (a dated label, "ARC's standard shoppers: N of M reached checkout, <date>": a lower bound, not a verdict; ARC stops before payment and never places an order), best_route (the best saved way in), payment_methods_declared (the payment handler ids the store declares to agents in its own UCP profile, with source "ucp_profile", checked_at and a note; the store's own declaration, not a test of any agent paying there; null with payment_methods_note when ARC has no UCP profile reading, which is not a no), up to 3 blockers, checked_at, the Agent Readiness Grade (grade, with expired when over 30 days old; grade_note when not graded, which is not a mark against the store), alternatives_hint when the grade is D or F or expired (a find_stores call with min_grade B in the same category), and a full_record link (the precheck answer, which also carries product_markup). Example: before_checkout({"url":"https://allbirds.com"}) → {"answer":"A saved check got a checkout link back at allbirds.com via storefront_mcp (6 hours ago).","reaches_checkout":true,…}. The answer leads with the dated fact; once the record is not current it starts "Last known on <date>.". reaches_checkout false or unknown is not a no. Saved checks only: no store fetch, no scan, no login. Advisory; ARC stops before payment. Every answer carries checked_at (the saved check it rests on; for a list, the oldest) and stale (true when that check is 24 hours old or older, or has no time). Errors: {error:{code, message, next_step}}.

url.description: Store or product URL, such as https://allbirds.com or allbirds.com.

ai.arcreport/ask.name: find_stores
ai.arcreport/ask.description: Call this when you need to pick a store for a product need and want one where a saved check shows an agent reached checkout. Filters: category or q (shopper words), min_grade (optional, default none), payment_method (optional: a payment handler id such as com.google.pay, or "google pay" or "shop pay"; keeps stores whose saved UCP profile declares it), limit (default 5). Returns total, the store hosts with checked_at and grade, and a full_list link; with payment_method, also payment_method (id, name, declared_by: how many listed stores declare it, and a note: a declaration is the store's own statement, not a test of any agent paying there). Each store carries its Agent Readiness Grade (grade, null when not graded). Stores whose saved checkout evidence is from the last 30 days come first (fresh_success: true), then older evidence. Within each, best current grade first (A, then B…); an expired grade ranks after current ones of the same letter; newest checked_at first within a grade. Results are ordered only by published grade and freshness, never by anything else. Pass min_grade to keep only stores with a current grade of that letter or better. Example: find_stores({"category":"running shoes","limit":3}) → {"total":12,"stores":[{"host":"…","checked_at":"…","grade":{"grade":"A",…}}],…}. Example: "Which stores declare Google Pay to agents?" → find_stores({"payment_method":"google pay"}) → {"payment_method":{"id":"com.google.pay","declared_by":…},"stores":[…],…}. An unknown payment_method is error code unknown_payment_method with handler_ids (the ids ARC has seen); not_available means retry in a minute. A store missing from the list is not a no. Saved checks only: no store fetch, no scan, no login. Advisory; ARC stops before payment. Every answer carries checked_at (the saved check it rests on; for a list, the oldest) and stale (true when that check is 24 hours old or older, or has no time). Errors: {error:{code, message, next_step}}.

category.description: Category or shopper words, such as footwear or running shoes.

q.description: Product need, such as skincare or camping gear.

limit.description: How many stores to return. Default 5.

min_grade.description: Optional: keep only stores whose current (not expired) Agent Readiness Grade is this letter or better (A, B, C or D; F is accepted and means any graded store, since method v2 gives no F). Default none: every store is listed. Expired and not-graded stores are left out when this is set.

payment_method.description: Optional. A payment handler id as stores declare it in their UCP profile, such as com.google.pay or dev.shopify.shop_pay, or the plain name google pay or shop pay (any case).

ai.arcreport/ask.name: why_blocked_and_fix
ai.arcreport/ask.description: Call this after before_checkout says reaches_checkout is false or null, or when an agent got stuck at a store and you want the reason and the fix. Returns why (the saved blockers), fix (the store page's recorded fix, or "not recorded"), next_step and links to the full record. Example: why_blocked_and_fix({"store":"gymshark.com"}) → {"why":["…"],"fix":"…","next_step":"…"}. Saved checks only: no store fetch, no scan, no login. Advisory; ARC stops before payment. Every answer carries checked_at (the saved check it rests on; for a list, the oldest) and stale (true when that check is 24 hours old or older, or has no time). Errors: {error:{code, message, next_step}}.

store.description: Store domain or URL, such as gymshark.com.

ai.arcreport/ask.name: report_outcome
ai.arcreport/ask.description: Call this right after your agent tried to check out at a store, to log, record or report what happened: it reached checkout, a captcha stopped it, it got as far as shipping, anything. Use it for any attempt that already happened, so the next agent knows; before_checkout is only for before an attempt. Free, no login. Omit contributor_key and ARC issues one; send it on later reports. No personal data: emails, phones, addresses, card numbers and IPs are rejected or stripped. Example: report_outcome({"store_domain":"allbirds.com","agent_family":"browser","agent_name":"my-agent","timestamp":"2026-11-05T10:00:00Z","furthest_step":"checkout","blocker":"none"}) → {"ok":true,"status":"unverified",…}. A report stays private until 3 independent contributors agree. Same as POST /api/outcomes and report_checkout on /api/mcp. checked_at and stale are null on this answer: a report is not one of ARC's checks. Errors: {error:{code, message, next_step}}.

agent_family.description: Agent family, such as browser or a model family. No personal name.

agent_name.description: Optional. Name of the agent that tried the checkout. No personal name. Omit it and ARC records "not recorded".

contributor_key.description: Optional. Omit it and ARC returns a free key. Send that key on later reports.

timestamp.description: Optional. ISO 8601 time of the attempt, within the last 14 days. Omit it and ARC uses the time it received the report.

blocker.description: What stopped the agent, or none.

store_error_text.description: Optional store error text. Personal data is stripped.

ai.arcreport/ask.name: store_record
ai.arcreport/ask.description: Call this when a user asks what ARC recorded for a store, or you need the citable store page. Returns the store page's verdict, checked_at (the day of the check), stale, category, tried (ARC's standard shoppers' newest dated run, or "Not measured"), the recorded fix, payment_methods_declared (as on before_checkout; null with payment_methods_note when ARC has no UCP profile reading, which is not a no), record_url (claimed, served, date, method and product_markup as JSON) and links to the page, its JSON and Markdown. Example: store_record({"store":"allbirds.com"}) → {"verdict":"…","page_url":"https://www.arcreport.ai/stores/allbirds.com",…}. Reads the published snapshot behind /stores/<host>. Saved checks only: no store fetch, no scan, no login. Advisory; ARC stops before payment. Every answer carries checked_at (the saved check it rests on; for a list, the oldest) and stale (true when that check is 24 hours old or older, or has no time). Errors: {error:{code, message, next_step}}.

store.description: Store domain or URL, such as allbirds.com.

ai.arcreport/ask.name: compare
ai.arcreport/ask.description: Call this when a user names 2 or more stores for the same item and asks which one to use, or when you must choose between a few stores and want the one where an agent is most likely to reach checkout. Use it instead of calling before_checkout once per store. Pass 2 to 10 store domains or URLs. Returns one short row per store (reaches_checkout, best_route, checked_at, grade, payment_methods_declared as on before_checkout), and pick: among stores whose saved check reached checkout in the last 30 days, the one with the best current Agent Readiness Grade (expired after current of the same letter, not graded last); null when no store has such evidence. A row with stale: true is more than 24 hours old: re-check right before the attempt. Rows are ordered only by saved checkout evidence, its freshness and published grade, never by anything else. Example: compare({"stores":["allbirds.com","gymshark.com"]}) → {"pick":"allbirds.com","stores":[…]}. Each store counts as one precheck read. Saved checks only: no store fetch, no scan, no login. Advisory; ARC stops before payment. Every answer carries checked_at (the saved check it rests on; for a list, the oldest) and stale (true when that check is 24 hours old or older, or has no time). Errors: {error:{code, message, next_step}}.

ai.arcreport/ask.name: guide
ai.arcreport/ask.description: Call this when a person at a store (a CEO, a marketing or e-commerce manager, or a developer) asks where their store is on the journey to AI assistants, what to do next on their platform, or how stores in their category compare. Not for an agent about to check out: use before_checkout for that. Returns the store's place on ARC's journey map (arc-journey/v1: 5 stages, each met, not met or "Not measured" with its date; not measured is not a no, and there is no score or grade), the next 3 steps for its platform at the chosen depth with source links and an as-of date (a platform fact ARC has not sourced says "Not yet documented by ARC"), how many stores ARC checked in its category and on its platform and how many meet each stage (counts with denominators and the snapshot date), and up to 5 named stores that meet the furthest stage (ordered only by stage reached, then the newest reading). role: ceo, manager or developer sets depth (basics, detail or implement) unless depth is given. Send platform alone for the platform guide with no store. Example: guide({"store":"gymshark.com","role":"manager"}) → {"answer":"gymshark.com: Meets stages 1, 2, 3 and 4. Not met: stage 5. Saved check 16 Oct 2026.","stages":[…],"next_steps":[…],"comparison":{…},"examples":{…}}. Saved checks only: no store fetch, no scan, no login. Advisory; ARC stops before payment. Every answer carries checked_at (the saved check it rests on; for a list, the oldest) and stale (true when that check is 24 hours old or older, or has no time). Errors: {error:{code, message, next_step}}.

store.description: Store domain or URL, such as gymshark.com. Leave out and send platform for the platform guide alone.

role.description: Who is asking. Sets depth: ceo basics, manager detail, developer implement.

depth.description: How much detail. Default from role, else basics.

platform.description: shopify, magento, salesforce, woocommerce, bigcommerce, wix, squarespace or other. Overrides the platform ARC detected.

category.description: Category for a platform-only call, such as footwear or apparel. A store uses its own category.

ai.arcreport/mcp.name: check_store
ai.arcreport/mcp.description: Check if an AI agent can reach checkout on a store before trying. Call this with a store domain, such as allbirds.com. Returns the saved checkout evidence, or not checked yet when ARC has no saved check. The poppy field is what the saved check read at /.well-known/poppy.json (Personal Agent Protocol): file_present, the protocol_version the file states, and the check time. "Not measured" there is not a no. Free, no login, no new scan, and no fetch of the store. A missing field says "not recorded" and is not a zero. Results are advisory. ARC stops before payment.

ai.arcreport/mcp.name: find_stores
ai.arcreport/mcp.description: Find stores where a saved check shows an AI agent can reach checkout. Filter by platform, protocol, category, or min_grade (optional, default none). With no filters, returns those stores and labels the result default: no filters given. Each store carries its Agent Readiness Grade (grade, null when not graded). Stores whose saved checkout evidence is from the last 30 days come first (fresh_success: true), then older evidence. Within each, best current grade first (A, then B…); an expired grade ranks after current ones of the same letter; newest checked_at first within a grade. Results are ordered only by published grade and freshness, never by anything else. Pass min_grade to keep only stores with a current grade of that letter or better. A missing result is not counted against a store. No login and no new scan. Results are advisory. ARC stops before payment.

platform.description: Commerce platform id, such as shopify or woocommerce.

protocol.description: ucp, webmcp, or mcp. ACP, PAP, and payments are not filters here.

category.description: Category or shopper words, such as footwear or running shoes.

limit.description: How many stores to return. Default 10. Maximum 25.

min_grade.description: Optional: keep only stores whose current (not expired) Agent Readiness Grade is this letter or better (A, B, C or D; F is accepted and means any graded store, since method v2 gives no F). Default none: every store is listed. Expired and not-graded stores are left out when this is set.

ai.arcreport/mcp.name: report_checkout
ai.arcreport/mcp.description: Report how far one agent got at one store. Free, no login. Omit contributor_key and ARC issues one. Emails, phones, street addresses, card numbers, IP addresses, and private hosts are rejected. The report stays private until 3 independent contributors with a day-old key, or enough reputation, agree within 14 days. A blocked outcome also waits for ARC's free HTTP recheck. Same as POST /api/outcomes.

agent_family.description: Agent family, such as browser or a model family. No personal name.

agent_name.description: Optional. Name of the agent that tried the checkout. No personal name. Omit it and ARC records "not recorded".

contributor_key.description: Optional. Omit it and ARC returns a free key. Send that key on later reports.

timestamp.description: Optional. ISO 8601 time of the attempt, within the last 14 days. Omit it and ARC uses the time it received the report.

blocker.description: What stopped the agent, or none.

store_error_text.description: Optional store error text. Personal data is stripped.

ai.arcreport/mcp.name: get_store_hub
ai.arcreport/mcp.description: [Requires sign-in] Look up a free ARC store card by host. Includes saved measurements and brand_claim ownership metadata. Brand statements are not measured by ARC; claims never change measured scores.

ai.arcreport/mcp.name: google_checkout_readiness
ai.arcreport/mcp.description: [Requires sign-in] Read saved public Google agentic checkout readiness checks for a store. Free; no new scan or paid calls. Merchant Center feed eligibility cannot be checked from outside. Not Google approval or certification.

ai.arcreport/mcp.name: product_data_check
ai.arcreport/mcp.description: Free latest saved product data and return/shipping policy check from the store's pages and structured data. Reads history only; no store fetch or model call. A missing result is not a zero.

ai.arcreport/mcp.name: can_agent_checkout
ai.arcreport/mcp.description: [Requires sign-in] Call when you need a saved checkout-link check for any public store URL, not only Index brands. Use it for 'what stops an agent at <store> checkout?' or 'which checkout route works on <store>?' when you also want the one fix. Saved HTTP checkout check for a public homepage or product URL: catalog, product, checkout link, UCP profile, blocks, and one fix. No model call, payment, or browser scan. Uses ARC's last check (cached up to 24 hours). A missing result is unknown, not a no. A checkout link means reach checkout, not a completed order. Results are advisory. ARC stops before payment.

url.description: Public store homepage or product URL

ai.arcreport/mcp.name: check_agent_readiness
ai.arcreport/mcp.description: [Requires sign-in] Check whether personal AI agents can reach a product URL, understand it, and reach checkout. Runs ARC's readiness check: crawler access, whether an agent can answer a shopper's questions from the page, and personal shopping agents trying to add to cart or reach checkout. Returns a check id — poll get_readiness_result (about 30–60 seconds). This does not ask what agents think of the brand; use ask_agents_about_brand for that.

url.description: The product or store URL to test, e.g. https://store.com/products/best-seller

task.description: Optional goal, e.g. 'add to cart' (default) or 'reach checkout'.

ai.arcreport/mcp.name: get_readiness_result
ai.arcreport/mcp.description: [Requires sign-in] Get a readiness check by id. While running, reports progress. When complete, reports whether personal agents could reach the page, understand it, and reach checkout, plus the wall, concrete next steps, a directional score, a per-agent breakdown, and screenshots. Calling this again with the same id redisplays the result and does not start a new check. Never re-run check_agent_readiness just to see the screenshots again.

id.description: The check id returned by check_agent_readiness.

ai.arcreport/mcp.name: list_readiness_checks
ai.arcreport/mcp.description: [Requires sign-in] List this workspace's recent readiness checks (newest first) — each store, its score, status, and id. Use an id with get_readiness_result to reopen a check.

ai.arcreport/mcp.name: ask_agents_about_brand
ai.arcreport/mcp.description: [Requires sign-in] Ask benchmark personal-agent personas what they think of a brand and whether they would recommend it for a category. Personas A to E are ARC benchmark personas named by how they shop: A always-on errands, B errands by text, C researches on its own computer, D works toward a goal, E self-hosted. None of them is a consumer AI product or a live consumer-product session. Persona C runs on a Grok model via API. It is not the real Grok read-back on a scan and it is not the agent-rails HTTP check. What Grok tells shoppers on a scan is a real model call via API, checked against the store's pages, not the consumer Grok app. All five cart attempts, Grok included, are ARC browser cart tests. Returns, per persona: mentioned, recommended, which competitors were recommended instead, sentiment, and short quotes, plus next steps. Limited to 8 runs per workspace per day and 12 per network. Free workspaces also share a site-wide daily cap so unpaid runs cannot drain the model budget.

category.description: Product category a shopper would ask about, e.g. running shoes.

competitors.description: Optional competitor brand names to watch for in the answers.

ai.arcreport/mcp.name: get_fixes
ai.arcreport/mcp.description: [Requires sign-in] Concrete next steps to get recommended by personal agents and to become reachable, understandable, and buyable. Pass a readiness check id and/or the brand, category, store URL, and competitors that were recommended instead. Uses the check's evidence when an id is given. Does not start a new check.

scan_id.description: Optional readiness check id from check_agent_readiness.

brand.description: Brand name, if you want recommendation steps.

category.description: Product category, e.g. running shoes.

mentioned.description: Whether any benchmark persona mentioned the brand.

recommended.description: Whether any benchmark persona recommended the brand for the category.

ai.arcreport/mcp.name: bulk_create_monitors
ai.arcreport/mcp.description: [Requires sign-in] Set up scheduled monitoring for one or more store URLs (the 'set up monitoring' flow). Validates each URL and rejects invalid/private/internal ones. GUIDED FLOW: first ask the user for the URLs (paste a list or a CSV), then the frequency (daily/weekly/monthly, default weekly). Every monitor runs the core panel of personal shopping agents — no picking needed. Call once without confirmed=true to preview the exact setup and how many scans it will run, read that summary to the user, and only after the user explicitly says yes call again with confirmed=true to create the monitors. Each scheduled run is one scan. Every run emails who reached the cart, who stopped or started, the stuck step, and the fix. Weekly fits every workspace's monthly scan limit; daily only fits when the limit covers it.

urls.description: Store/product URLs to monitor (a list or pasted CSV lines).

frequency.description: How often to re-test. Default: weekly.

depth.description: How far each scan goes. Default: cart.

confirmed.description: Must be true only after the user has confirmed the summarized setup. If missing or false, ARC returns a preview and creates nothing.

ai.arcreport/mcp.name: list_monitors
ai.arcreport/mcp.description: [Requires sign-in] List the workspace's monitors — each store re-checked on a schedule for whether personal agents can still reach it and its checkout. Includes cadence, status, last score, next run, and the monitor id.

ai.arcreport/mcp.name: monitor_summary

ai.arcreport/mcp.name: update_monitor

ai.arcreport/mcp.name: pause_monitor

ai.arcreport/mcp.name: run_monitor_now

ai.artemisgtm/gtm-engineer.name: describe_firm
ai.artemisgtm/gtm-engineer.description: What Artemis GTM is: an AI GTM engineering firm for seed to Series C B2B startups, who founded it, what it builds, how it builds (its proprietary agent architecture, never sold or installed), what clients keep, how an engagement starts, how it is priced (two options, Single system build and Embedded GTM Engineering, with prices for both published at https://artemisgtm.ai/pricing/) and the booking link.

ai.artemisgtm/gtm-engineer.name: recommend_engagement

ai.artemisgtm/gtm-engineer.name: book_evaluation

ai.artidrop/artidrop.name: publish
ai.artidrop/artidrop.description: Publish HTML or Markdown content as a shareable URL. Pass `content` byte-for-byte from the source — do not retype, reformat, minify, summarize, or 'clean up' the input; even one stray character can break inline scripts on the published page. If the content is too large to copy verbatim through the model, use the REST endpoint `POST /v1/artifacts` (or `/v1/artifacts/upload` for ZIPs) instead. For Markdown, optionally include images as base64-encoded data.

content.description: The HTML or Markdown content to publish. Copy this verbatim from the source file or buffer — do not modify, reformat, or regenerate it. Whitespace, emojis, comments, and exact character sequences inside <script> and <style> blocks all matter. If you cannot fit the full content unmodified in one tool call, fall back to POST /v1/artifacts via curl.

format.description: Content format

title.description: Artifact title (default: Untitled)

images.description: Images referenced in the markdown content. Only used when format is 'markdown'.

path.description: Relative path as referenced in the markdown (e.g., 'images/demo.png')

ai.artidrop/artidrop.name: publish_site
ai.artidrop/artidrop.description: Publish a multi-file HTML site from a base64-encoded ZIP file. The ZIP must contain an index.html at its root. For sites larger than ~10MB — or whenever you have the file on disk — prefer the REST API /v1/artifacts/upload endpoint to avoid base64 overhead and to guarantee byte-faithful upload.

zip_base64.description: Base64-encoded ZIP file containing the site files

title.description: Site title (default: Untitled)

ai.artidrop/artidrop.name: get

email.description: Ties the record to this pair. Never stored, never sent to an AI model.

teamSize.description: People on the account, counting the user.

scores.description: Only results from a personality assessment the person agreed to. At least 5 of the 9 traits, each 1 to 10. Never results collected for a hiring decision, and never clinical tests. Leave this out to have the person read from their emails.

email.description: Ties the record to this pair. Never stored, never sent to an AI model.

country.description: ARVX reads people in the United States only. US switches on U.S. holidays.

city.description: With state, switches on severe weather warnings.

state.description: Two-letter code, such as MI.

scores.description: Only results from a personality assessment the person agreed to. At least 5 of the 9 traits, each 1 to 10. Never results collected for a hiring decision, and never clinical tests. Leave this out to have the person read from their emails.

other.description: The person the user works with.

sentAt.description: Date and time sent, such as 2026-10-01T14:30:00Z.

ai.arvx/arvx.name: arvx_record_summary
ai.arvx/arvx.description: When someone asks what is held about them: returns every item in a saved record in plain words. Needs the record and both people's emails. Never uses up a Reading; 10 a month per account.

ai.askmiles/catalog.name: search_card_catalog
ai.askmiles/catalog.description: Find credit cards open to new applicants by issuer, annual fee, network, rewards currency, or a benefit they carry. Returns a short row per card; call get_card_facts for one card's full record. Card facts only: no earning rates, welcome-offer amounts, transfer ratios, or bonus sizes.

no_foreign_transaction_fee.description: Only cards with no foreign transaction fee.

rewards_currency.description: Loyalty currency the card earns, e.g. 'Chase Ultimate Rewards'. Matched loosely.

benefit.description: Words to look for in a card's statement credits, lounge networks, or purchase/travel protections, e.g. 'Global Entry', 'Priority Pass', 'trip delay'.

has_lounge_access.description: Only cards carrying at least one lounge network.

has_free_night_certificate.description: Only cards granting a free night certificate.

ai.askmiles/catalog.name: get_card_facts
ai.askmiles/catalog.description: Everything the public catalog holds on one card: issuer, annual fee, network, foreign transaction fee, rewards currency, and the names of its statement credits, lounge networks and protections. Card name is matched loosely. Card facts only: no earning rates, welcome-offer amounts, transfer ratios, or bonus sizes.

card_name.description: Card name, e.g. 'Amex Platinum' or 'Venture X'.

ai.askmiles/catalog.name: compare_card_facts
ai.askmiles/catalog.description: The same catalog record for 2-5 cards at once, for comparing fees, networks and which benefits each carries. Card facts only: no earning rates, welcome-offer amounts, transfer ratios, or bonus sizes.

ai.askmiles/catalog.name: find_transfer_routes
ai.askmiles/catalog.description: Which loyalty programs a currency transfers to, or which currencies reach a destination, and whether a transfer bonus is running. This is the route graph only. It does not carry transfer ratios, bonus sizes, expiry dates, or which route is worth taking. Card facts only: no earning rates, welcome-offer amounts, transfer ratios, or bonus sizes.

to_program.description: Destination program, e.g. 'World of Hyatt'. Matched loosely; call with neither argument to list every source.

only_with_bonus.description: Only routes with a transfer bonus running.

include_inactive.description: Include routes that have been discontinued.

ai.askmiles/catalog.name: estimate_point_value
ai.askmiles/catalog.description: Miles' own estimate of a loyalty point's value in cents, optionally multiplied by a balance. A cash balance such as Uber Cash is valued as a share of face value (0.9 is 90%). Call with no arguments to list every program Miles values, with the exact spelling to use. These are Miles' estimates, not market prices. Attribute them. Card facts only: no earning rates, welcome-offer amounts, transfer ratios, or bonus sizes.

program.description: Loyalty program, e.g. 'World of Hyatt'. Matched loosely. Omit to list all.

points.description: A balance to value, in points, or in dollars for a cash balance such as Uber Cash.

ai.asms/asms.name: get_balance
ai.asms/asms.description: Get the current wallet balance for the authenticated account.

service.description: Service slug to receive the OTP for (e.g. "google", "telegram", "whatsapp").

ai.asms/asms.name: get_inventory

service.description: Service slug to receive the OTP for (e.g. "google", "telegram", "whatsapp").

ai.asms/asms.name: create_otp_order
ai.asms/asms.description: Buy a number to receive an OTP: allocates a number, debits the wallet, and returns an orderId + phoneNumber. Then poll with poll_sms. If no code arrives, do NOT cancel to retry: simply call create_otp_order again for a fresh number and keep polling that one. Unfilled orders auto-refund within 10 minutes, so you only pay for codes that actually land and there is no penalty for ordering repeatedly. When a service keeps rejecting codes, order on the "us1" (Non-VoIP AT&T) pool, which has the highest delivery rate. WARNING: this spends real wallet balance.

country.description: Number pool to order from: "us1" = Non-VoIP AT&T (real carrier line, for strict services like WhatsApp/Telegram/Google), "us" = VoIP High Quality (lowest price, works for most signups), "uk" = United Kingdom (+44), "au" = Australia (+61).

service.description: Service slug to receive the OTP for (e.g. "google", "telegram", "whatsapp").

ai.asms/asms.name: poll_sms
ai.asms/asms.description: Check for the SMS / OTP code on an order. Returns the code once it has arrived, otherwise an empty result: poll again after a few seconds. If nothing lands after a minute or two, the fastest path is to order a fresh number with create_otp_order (prefer the "us1" Non-VoIP pool) and leave the original: it auto-refunds within 10 minutes. Never cancel just to retry, and there is no charge for ordering again, you only pay for codes that arrive.

ai.asms/asms.name: list_active_orders
ai.asms/asms.description: List recent OTP orders for the account (awaiting a code or already received).

ai.asms/asms.name: cancel_order
ai.asms/asms.description: Rarely needed. To retry a verification do NOT cancel: just call create_otp_order again, because every unfilled order auto-refunds within 10 minutes on its own, and cancel is blocked for the first 10 minutes anyway. Only use this to release an order you are certain you no longer need once its 10-minute hold has passed.

ai.asms/asms.name: get_rental_offers

ai.asms/asms.name: rent_number
ai.asms/asms.description: Rent a phone number in a country for a period (get the periods and prices from get_rental_offers first). Debits the wallet and returns the number and when the rental ends. Read its SMS with read_rental_sms. WARNING: this spends real wallet balance; confirm the country, period and price with the user first.

country.description: Country to rent a number in: "us" (United States), "uk" (United Kingdom), "ca" (Canada), "au" (Australia), "es" (Spain), "se" (Sweden), "de" (Germany), "nl" (Netherlands), "it" (Italy), "pl" (Poland), "fi" (Finland), "pt" (Portugal), "be" (Belgium), "at" (Austria), "ch" (Switzerland), "cz" (Czechia), "si" (Slovenia), "lt" (Lithuania), "mx" (Mexico), "hk" (Hong Kong), "il" (Israel), "za" (South Africa).

ai.asms/asms.name: list_rentals
ai.asms/asms.description: List the account's rented numbers with their country, period, end date and whether auto-renew is on. Ended rentals are left out unless `includeEnded` is true.

ai.asms/asms.name: read_rental_sms

ai.asms/asms.name: cancel_rental
ai.asms/asms.description: Cancel a rented number and refund it. Only possible between 5 and 120 minutes after renting, and only if the number has received no SMS; after that the rental runs to its end date.

number.description: The rented number, as rent_number or list_rentals gave it ("+", spaces and dashes are ignored).

ai.asms/asms.name: renew_rental
ai.asms/asms.description: Keep a rented number for another period: the period is added to its current end, at today's price for that period in its country (see get_rental_offers). Possible from 2 hours after renting until 20 minutes before the end. Debits the wallet only if the renewal goes through. WARNING: this spends real wallet balance; confirm the number, period and price with the user first.

number.description: The rented number, as rent_number or list_rentals gave it ("+", spaces and dashes are ignored).

period.description: Rental period: "oneDay" (1 day), "oneWeek" (1 week), "oneMonth" (1 month), "threeMonths" (3 months), "sixMonths" (6 months), "twelveMonths" (12 months). Not every period is on sale in every country: check get_rental_offers.

ai.asms/asms.name: set_rental_auto_renew
ai.asms/asms.description: With auto-renew on, the number is renewed for its rental period from the wallet a day before it ends (6 hours before for a one-day rental); if the balance is short then, the account is emailed and nothing is charged. number.description: The rented number, as rent_number or list_rentals gave it ("+", spaces and dashes are ignored).

autoRenew.description: true to turn auto-renew on, false to turn it off.

ai.atdev/supershopping.name: search_products
ai.atdev/supershopping.description:
자연어로 신품·중고 통합 상품 검색 (슈퍼쇼핑의 기본 진입점).

언제: 사용자가 특정 상품을 찾을 때. 예) "남성 패딩 20만원 이하", "중고 RTX 4070", "27인치 게이밍 모니터".
자동 처리: 도메인(패션/전자)·성별·가격대·속성을 질의에서 추출해 필터링.
반환: {items: [{title, min_price, key_specs, thumbnail, buy_url, source, condition, ...}], total}.
  → 결과 제시 시 각 buy_url을 링크로 함께 보여줘라. 사진은 get_product_image로 렌더.
추천만 원하거나 검색어가 모호하면 recommend_products를 써라.

ai.atdev/supershopping.name: get_product_detail
ai.atdev/supershopping.description:
슈퍼쇼핑 상품의 전체 상세 — 스펙·쇼핑몰별 가격(offers)·신품/중고 교차비교.

언제: 사용자가 한 상품을 깊이 보거나 구매 직전일 때. (product_id는 search/recommend 결과에서 얻는다)
반환: 전체 속성 + offers(쇼핑몰별 buy_url) + comparison_url + other_sources(같은 모델의 다른 소스
  신품↔중고 가격 스프레드) + affiliate_disclosure(있으면 고지).
  → other_sources로 "같은 모델 중고는 얼마" 같은 가격차를 안내하면 좋다.

ai.atdev/supershopping.name: get_product_image
ai.atdev/supershopping.description:
슈퍼쇼핑 상품의 대표 이미지를 실제 이미지(렌더 가능)로 반환.

언제: 사용자가 상품 사진을 보고 싶어할 때("이 코트 보여줘"). 검색/추천 결과의 thumbnail은
URL(텍스트)이라 화면에 안 뜨므로, 시각 확인이 필요하면 이 툴로 이미지 자체를 가져온다.
반환: 이미지 콘텐츠(여러 개를 한 번에 보여주지 말고 관심 상품 위주로 호출).

ai.atdev/supershopping.name: compare_products
ai.atdev/supershopping.description:
슈퍼쇼핑 상품 여러 개(2~5개)의 스펙·가격 비교 매트릭스 + 한 줄 결론.

언제: 사용자가 후보 여러 개를 견주려 할 때("이 중에 뭐가 나아?"). product_ids는 search 결과에서.
반환: {attributes: 공통 키, matrix: 상품별 값/가격, verdict: 한국어 결론}.

ai.atdev/supershopping.name: recommend_products
ai.atdev/supershopping.description:
슈퍼쇼핑에서 의도·예산 기반 상품 추천 + 추천 근거.

언제: 사용자가 구체적 검색어 없이 용도/취향/예산만 말할 때("겨울 데이트룩 추천", "50만원대 가성비 노트북").
인자: intent(용도/취향), budget(예산 상한), must_have(필수 조건).
반환: {recommendations: [{title, min_price, reason, buy_url, thumbnail, source}], affiliate_disclosure?}.
  → 각 추천을 buy_url 링크와 함께 제시하고, 사진은 get_product_image로 보여줘라.

ai.atdev/supershopping.name: recommend_outfit
ai.atdev/supershopping.description:
슈퍼쇼핑에서 어울리는 코디를 추천 (씨앗 상품 또는 의도 기반).

언제: "이 코트에 어울리는 코디", "가을 데이트룩 코디" 처럼 한 벌 구성을 원할 때.
인자: product_id(씨앗 아이템, 선택), intent(의도/무드, 선택), budget(전체 예산 상한, 선택). 둘 중 하나는 필요.
반환: {seed, items:[{slot, title, min_price, reason, buy_url, thumbnail, source}], styling_reason, affiliate_disclosure?}.
  → 각 아이템을 buy_url 링크와 함께 제시하고, 사진은 get_product_image로 보여줘라.

ai.atdev/supershopping.name: analyze_market
ai.atdev/supershopping.description:
슈퍼쇼핑 카테고리 시세 분석 — 가격 분포·최저가몰·대안.

언제: 사용자가 시세/적정가를 물을 때("그래픽카드 요즘 얼마", "노트북 가격대"). category는 이름(예: '노트북') 또는 ID.
반환: 가격 통계(최저/중앙/최고·분포)·최저가 쇼핑몰·대안 상품.

ai.atdev/supershopping.name: initiate_checkout
ai.atdev/supershopping.description:
슈퍼쇼핑에서 선택한 상품의 구매로 연결 — 최저가 쇼핑몰의 구매 링크와 가격·고지를 반환.

언제: 사용자가 구매 의사를 보일 때("이거 살래", "구매하기"). 실제 결제는 판매처 페이지에서 일어난다.
반환: {payload: {merchant, buy_url(제휴 변환됨), price, ...}, affiliate_disclosure?, next_actions}.
  → buy_url을 명확한 구매 링크로 제시하고, affiliate_disclosure가 있으면 반드시 고지하라.
  중고(used)는 개인 직거래이므로 안전결제/실물확인을 안내하라.

ai.athenahq/mcp.name: open_ai_access
ai.athenahq/mcp.description: Open the AthenaHQ AI crawler access panel. Enter a public HTTPS domain to inspect crawler responses and robots.txt permissions without an AthenaHQ account.

ai.athenahq/mcp.name: check_public_ai_access
ai.athenahq/mcp.description: Check HTTP responses to AI crawler user agents and robots.txt permissions for a public website. No AthenaHQ account required. Search, retrieval and training are separate. Use nullable evidence and diagnostics.

ai.athenahq/mcp.name: get_prompt_schedules
ai.athenahq/mcp.description: List the Default, custom and archived streaming schedules for a website. Use each row's selection value when filtering analytics or responses. Default includes all pre-cutover history and ad hoc runs; archived schedules retain results. To combine schedules, pass several selection values as an array in the schedule field of query_metrics and query_rows, or use a saved view that stores several schedules. Partner REST filters take one schedule. starts_on and ends_on bound a custom schedule's active period as UTC days (null means no bound); an active schedule outside its period does not run.

ai.athenahq/mcp.name: get_ai_search_value
ai.athenahq/mcp.description: AI Search Value for a website: topic-market value, captured value range, headroom, coverage, value-weighted AI share of voice, per-topic detail, and modeled attributed contribution.

ai.athenahq/mcp.name: get_competitors

ai.athenahq/mcp.name: get_content_hub_sheets

Use to discover available tabs (e.g. 1st-party content, 3rd-party placements, Reddit) before calling get_tracked_content with a specific sheet_id (metrics; excludes in-flight pipeline items) or list_content (every item including unpublished drafts).

ai.athenahq/mcp.name: get_tracked_content
ai.athenahq/mcp.description: List tracked content (1st-party drafts, imported pages, 3rd-party placements) with citation, mention, and impression metrics for the supplied date range and filters. Supports pagination via page_num / page_size and optional filtering by Content Hub sheet_id or content_type. A sheet_id of a view-type tab (see get_content_hub_sheets sheet_type) lists the shared main pool: content not filed in any sheet. In-flight pipeline items (drafts, briefs, running generations) never appear here; enumerate those with list_content. A returned item can still lack a url (pipeline finished but not published anywhere yet).

sheet_id.description: Content Hub tab to list (get_content_hub_sheets). A sheet-type tab lists its own content; a view-type tab, the default tab included, lists the shared main pool (content not filed in any sheet), without the view's saved filters. Omit to list content on every tab.

ai.athenahq/mcp.name: list_content
ai.athenahq/mcp.description: Enumerate every content item in a website's Content Hub, published or not: in-flight drafts, briefs, snipes, optimize and slice runs, scheduled and failed items, plus tracked pages. Returns identity fields only (id, title, type, stage, sheet, URL, timestamps, target prompt ids), no metrics. Uncached and Postgres-backed, so an item created by create_content is listable immediately. Filter by sheet_id, content_type, stage, or prompt_id. stage is the raw pipeline workflow state, not a publication flag: null = no pipeline record (most tracked external / imported pages), and manual editor items carry 'generated'. Treat an item as published only when its stage is done (or it is an external / imported page) AND it has a url; done without a url is an unpublished orphan. A sheet_id of a view-type tab (see get_content_hub_sheets sheet_type) lists the shared main pool without the view's saved filters. Use get_tracked_content for citation and impression metrics on published content; use this tool to discover what exists. Each row carries prompt_ids: the prompts that item was WRITTEN FOR (what create_content was given), capped at 25 with the true size in prompt_count — resolve the ids to text with get_prompts rather than calling get_content_detail per row, and drill in with get_content_detail where prompt_count exceeds the ids returned (that read carries up to 100; associations past 100 are not currently readable). prompt_ids includes soft-deleted prompts, which get_prompts does NOT list — an id that fails to resolve there is a deleted prompt, and get_content_detail returns its text and status: "deleted". Empty prompt_ids means no targeting was recorded, which is normal for imported or externally tracked pages. This is not the same as being cited for a prompt — see get_content_citation_prompts for that. Filter by prompt_id for the reverse question: which content already targets a given prompt (coverage gaps).

ai.athenahq/mcp.name: get_content_detail
ai.athenahq/mcp.description: Fetch the full detail of a single tracked content item — its brief and body text (drafts, optimize rewrites, snipes, authored and scraped pages), plus status, cited source URLs, and links. Use after get_tracked_content to read the actual text behind a content_id. A status of generated_brief means the brief is ready while the article is still being written. Pages registered via track_content_urls return a null body and null status until their page text is fetched from the app — a null body on an external page means not fetched yet, not missing content; citation tracking does not need the body. `prompts` lists the prompts this page was WRITTEN FOR (the same ids create_content takes), newest-linked last, capped at 100 with the true size in `prompts_total`. When prompts_total exceeds 100 the rest are not currently readable through any tool — report the total, do not imply the list is complete. Entries carry status active, paused or deleted: a deleted prompt is still part of what the page was written for and still shows in the Content Hub, but get_prompts will not list it, so use the text returned here. An empty array means the page has no prompt targeting, which is normal for imported or externally tracked pages. That is a different question from get_content_citation_prompts, which lists prompts whose AI responses CITED the page. For an optimize item, source_url is the live page it is based on, available as soon as the item exists; url stays null until publish_content records the published page and marks the item done, so read source_url to link a request in review to its page. source_url is null for other content types and for optimize items based on pasted text or a file. To see the reworded variants actually asked of the models for these prompts, pass their ids to get_responses (each row carries base_prompt plus the variation as prompt) or query the responses cube via query_rows on the prompt_variation dimension.

ai.athenahq/mcp.name: get_content_citation_prompts
ai.athenahq/mcp.description: For a single tracked content item, list every prompt whose AI responses cited it — with citations, citation %, and estimated impressions. Use after get_tracked_content to drill into which prompts a given URL is appearing for. This is CITED-BY, measured over the requested date range, not the targeting the page was written for: an empty prompts array means no AI response cited this URL in that window, which is expected for new or never-cited pages and is not missing data. For the prompts a page was written to target, read `prompts` on get_content_detail (or prompt_ids on list_content) — those come from the content record itself and do not depend on any citation having happened.

ai.athenahq/mcp.description: Get LLM responses for a website. Shows how AI models answer queries, with sources, sentiment, and ranking data. For a variation-level export at volume, pair filters.variation_filter with include_response: false and compact_sources: true. ai.athenahq/mcp.name: query_metrics
ai.athenahq/mcp.description:
Query aggregated metrics for brand performance, competitors, sources, citations, and response trends. Use query_rows for individual records.

Mentions: from "response_mentions". Citations: from "citations". On either, where { is_website: true } selects the brand; { is_competitor: true } selects competitors; { entity_id: { eq: "<uuid>" } } selects one entity.
Filter/group models by model_category (display names like "ChatGPT", "Claude"), never "model". Dimensions vary by cube; source_mentions has no prompt/model dimensions.
Group by week (Monday start) or month wherever date groups. prompt_status is the paused flag (true = paused).

Measures: count, count_distinct, avg, sum, min, max; per-measure where enables conditional aggregation. Use compare for two date ranges.
When grouping by IDs, use alsoSelect for names: entity_id/entity_name, prompt_id/prompt_text, prompt_topic_id/topic_name (prompts uses topic_id).

Cited pages mentioning competitors but not the brand: from "sources", where { source_mentions_entity: { hasSome: [competitorIds], hasNone: [brandId] } }. Also works on "source_mentions". Checks all stored page mentions per URL/website. Date/model on sources scope AI responses; extracted page content may be older than the live page.

Content-hub attribution: on "sources", where { is_attributed_content: true }; by: ["content_id"], alsoSelect: ["content_title"]. Add content_type to by for type, or group by content_type alone. Read articles from "contents" via query_rows.

Schedule: select one "default" or custom/archived UUID from the catalog, or an array of them to combine schedules. Omit for caller default (current page in Ask Athena); explicit schedule overrides it. Top-level prompt_schedule_kind/id equality filters remain supported but must not conflict with schedule. Historical provenance is independent of current prompt membership; website-level cubes are unaffected.

from.description:
Dataset to query. Cubes and their contracts:

schedule.description: One schedule from the catalog ("default" or a custom/archived UUID), or an array of them to combine their data. Omit to use the caller default. The retired "manual" token is accepted as a deprecated alias of "default". Website-level cubes are unaffected.

of.description: Dimension to aggregate. Required for all functions except count. Bare `count` (no `of`) counts distinct facts (responses, mentions, citations...) on fact cubes. It throws on pre-aggregated tables (MVs) where rows are groups, not facts — use `{ fn: 'count_distinct', of: '<id-dim>' }` instead (e.g. `of: 'response_id'` on mentions/citations) to hit the MV's pre-computed aggregate.

where.description: Per-measure conditional filter (compiles to countIf, avgIf, etc.).

anyOf.description: Aggregate expression.
Derived measure — an s-expression computed over other measures. Refs resolve to other measure aliases in the same query. Example: { expr: ["/", "brand", ["nullIf", "total", 0]] }

measures.description: Aggregate expressions keyed by output column name. Example: { total: { fn: 'count_distinct', of: 'response_id' } }

by.description: GROUP BY dimensions. Omit for scalar result.

alsoSelect.description: Label dimensions carried via any(). Must be determined by a by dim (cube's dependentDims). Example: entity_name when entity_id is in by.

having.description: HAVING filter (after grouping). References measure aliases and by dims.

orderBy.description: ORDER BY. Measure aliases and by dims allowed.

anyOf.description: Dim or measure name, ascending.

compare.description: Compare the same measures across two slices. Each base measure `m` expands to `m_<baseline.label>` and `m_<current.label>`; the result also gets `m_delta` (= current − baseline) and `m_pct_change` (= (current − baseline) / baseline, null when baseline = 0). For a min/max of `date`, `m_delta` is in days and `m_pct_change` is null. Default labels are 'baseline' and 'current'; override per side for non-temporal compares (e.g. brand vs competitors). One scan; orderBy on `m_delta` works push-down.

website_id.description: The website to query. Must be a website your credentials can access.

Filter.description: Prisma-style filter. A bare scalar value on a dim is shorthand for `eq` (e.g. `{ is_website: true }`); bare arrays and op-less objects throw — use `{ in: [...] }` / `{ hasSome: [...] }` explicitly. Operators: eq, neq, in, notIn, gt, gte, lt, lte, isNull, like, ilike, startsWith, hasSome, hasEvery, hasNone. Combinators: AND, OR, NOT. On semi-join dims (e.g. `response_mentions_entity`, `prompt_tag_ids`), `hasSome`/`in` emit `IN (SELECT …)` and `hasNone`/`notIn` emit `NOT IN (SELECT …)`; combine both on one dim to express "includes any of A but none of B". Empty `AND: []` / `OR: []` throw (the math identities are asymmetric — drop the clause before passing). Empty list operators (`hasSome: []` / `hasNone: []` / `hasEvery: []`) also throw — drop the predicate or supply at least one value. NOT accepts a single Filter only — for arrays use `NOT: { AND: [...] }` (`not all`) or `NOT: { OR: [...] }` (`none`). NOT keeps rows whose value is NULL: `NOT { sentiment: { eq: "positive" } }` returns unanalyzed responses as well as negative and neutral ones, because "not positive" is true of a row with no sentiment. Exclude them explicitly with `AND: [{ NOT: {...} }, { sentiment: { isNull: false } }]`.

Expr.description: S-expression. Strings are refs (to a measure alias or by-dim). Numbers/booleans/null are literals. Arrays are [op, ...args] where op is a binary operator (+ - * / % = != < <= > >= AND OR) or one of the allowed scalar functions: nullIf, coalesce, ifNull, if, multiIf, abs, round, floor, ceil, sqrt, pow, least, greatest, log, exp, sign. Examples: ["-", "n_current", "n_baseline"], ["/", "num", ["nullIf", "denom", 0]], ["coalesce", "value", 0].

CompareSlice.description: One side of a compare. `where` is the filter that scopes this slice (non-empty — empty means 'all rows', which trivializes the comparison). `label` defaults to 'baseline' / 'current' and forms the suffix on expanded column names; override for non-temporal compares.

ai.athenahq/mcp.name: query_rows
ai.athenahq/mcp.description:
Query individual analytics rows. Use for qualitative data like response text, specific identifiers, or individual mentions.

Schedule selection: pass schedule: "default" or a custom/archived UUID from the schedule catalog, or an array of them to combine schedules. Omit to use the caller default (Ask Athena uses the current page selection). Explicit selection overrides that default. Existing top-level equality predicates on prompt_schedule_kind/id remain supported, but cannot conflict with schedule. Historical provenance does not change with current prompt membership. Website-level cubes are unaffected.

Cubes (same set as query_metrics): attributes, citations, competitors, contents, prompts, response_mentions, responses, source_mentions, sources, topics, websites.
Returns { rows, nextCursor, hasMore }. Pass nextCursor back as "after" to paginate.
prompt_status is the prompt's paused flag (boolean, true = paused), not a status string.
On the responses cube, content is hydrated from Postgres and can only be selected. Do not filter or sort by content. Use search_terms_in_responses for text frequency analysis.
Use query_metrics for aggregates instead.

start_date.description: Start of the date range. Required. Accepts YYYY-MM-DD, ISO 8601 timestamps (timezone omitted means UTC), English month names with a four-digit year, and unambiguous numeric dates separated by /, -, or .; ambiguous dates are rejected.

end_date.description: End of the date range, inclusive. Date-only values include the UTC day through 23:59:59.999; timestamps keep their exact instant. ai.athenahq/mcp.name: get_attribute_metrics

It is NOT every response for the website — responses that never mention the brand are excluded, and Athena samples which responses get extraction, so un-analyzed ones are excluded too. Compute rates from the returned `percentage` / `total_responses` rather than against a response count from another endpoint. Attributes nobody mentioned come back with response_count 0. Use get_competitor_attribute_metrics for the same breakdown per competitor.

ai.athenahq/mcp.name: get_attribute_observations
ai.athenahq/mcp.description: Get individual brand trait (attribute) observations: each row is one AI response describing one entity (the brand or a competitor) with one brand trait, including the response excerpt as `text_span`. `score` runs from -1 to 1 and its sign always matches `positive`; its magnitude (0.1 to 1.0) is how strongly the wording praises or criticizes. `score` is null when the observation was not scored (extracted before scoring existed, or no valid value was recorded); for direction only, use `score ?? (positive ? 1 : -1)`. Omit `positive` for both directions. `sort: "intensity"` (the default) returns the strongest observations first with unscored ones last; `sort: "recent"` returns the newest first. Narrow with entity_ids and attribute_ids (from get_attributes). Paginate with page_num and page_size; a page can hold fewer than page_size rows when an excerpt is no longer available, so use `has_more` to decide whether to fetch the next page. Use get_attribute_metrics for how often each trait is mentioned.

ai.athenahq/mcp.name: get_user_by_email
ai.athenahq/mcp.description: Look up a user by email address, scoped to the caller's organization. Returns 404 when the email does not belong to a member of the organization or of one of its websites.

ai.athenahq/mcp.name: get_oracle_findings
ai.athenahq/mcp.description: When grounding is present, use its complete team-confirmed statement and all supporting facts as joint evidence; the legacy fact ID/text are only a compatibility anchor. List Oracle accuracy findings for a website: places where an AI response contradicted a verified brand fact (type 'inaccuracy' or 'kb_issue', with quote, claim, and reason) or where two knowledge-base facts conflict ('kb_duplicate' / 'kb_contradiction', pairing fact_text with related_fact_text). Findings from every status are included by default (pending, acknowledged, ignored, ...), each row carrying its status — pass the status filter for pending items only. Filters (run_id, fact_id, lineage_id, response_id, prompt_id, source_url, type, kind, severity, status) AND-compose; source_url matches evidence URLs exactly after normalization (protocol and trailing slash ignored). 'total' is the pre-limit count. 'latest_run' is the newest scan of any kind and is null only when the website has never been scanned, so latest_run plus empty findings means it scanned clean, while latest_run null means never scanned, not clean. Archived findings from before the current scanner ARE included: their run carries 'is_imported': true and keeps its original started_at, so an import can be the newest run — say the history is archived rather than calling it a current scan. 'has_imported_history' is true when any such archived run exists, and every finding row carries 'run_is_imported' so archival and current rows stay distinguishable in one list. Returns status 'no_access' if the brand does not have Oracle v2; that response carries the status alone, with no counts or findings.

model.description: Filter to one AI model by product name (ChatGPT, Claude, Gemini, Perplexity, Copilot, Muse Spark); raw identifiers also match exactly

ai.athenahq/mcp.name: get_oracle_finding
ai.athenahq/mcp.description: When grounding is present, use its complete team-confirmed statement and all supporting facts as joint evidence; the legacy fact ID/text are only a compatibility anchor. Load one Oracle finding in full: the flagged claim with its verified fact and prompt text, the run it came from, a ~2000-character response excerpt centered on the quoted claim, the cited-page evidence captured during the run (url, quote, snippet, scrape_hash), and its lineage: sibling findings sharing its lineage_id across runs, newest first. Use after get_oracle_findings to interrogate a specific finding. Returns a not-found error for an unknown finding id, and status 'no_access' if the brand does not have Oracle v2.

ai.athenahq/mcp.name: list_api_keys
ai.athenahq/mcp.description: List the organization's API key metadata, including creator and creation date, oldest first. Includes revoked keys so polling can detect keys revoked between checks. Never returns secrets or hashes. Requires a global API key or an organization admin's MCP connection. For polling, keep since/until fixed while paging, overlap successive windows and deduplicate by id. This is an inventory, not a durable event log; deleted creator accounts remove their keys.

since.description: Include keys created at or after this ISO 8601 timestamp.

until.description: Include keys created at or before this ISO 8601 timestamp. Keep fixed while paging.

ai.athenahq/mcp.name: add_brand_facts
ai.athenahq/mcp.description: Add brand facts to a website's Knowledge Base in bulk (1-50 per call). Each fact runs the full ingestion pipeline (deduplication, approval gates, pillar routing); there is no way to force-approve. Returns one outcome per fact (approved | pending | duplicate; extensible) with the created fact id and the pillar it was filed under. Facts without a pillar_id are routed automatically and may land unfiled. A fact similar to facts already in the Knowledge Base is not added: its outcome is duplicate and lists them under matches, and the response carries a match_token. To resolve, call again with those facts, the match_token, one decision per listed match (approve, optionally with new text, or delete) and save_submitted (true adds the facts as written, false only applies the decisions).

ai.athenahq/mcp.name: add_competitors
ai.athenahq/mcp.description: Start tracking competitors on a website, 1 to 25 per call, under the same rules as the Competitors page. Each competitor needs a name and its website url, or no_website: true for a brand with no website of its own; identifiers and additional_urls are optional. Returns one result per competitor, in order: added, already_tracked (the website already tracks that url; nothing changes), or rejected with the reason (a url on the website's own domains, an invalid url, or the limit of 500 competitors per website). New AI responses count mentions of an added competitor right away. Past responses are reanalyzed only when someone runs the backfill on the Competitors page, which costs credits; this tool never starts it and costs no credits.

url.description: The competitor's website, e.g. acme.com. Required unless no_website is true.

no_website.description: Pass true only for a brand that has no website of its own. Mentions still match on the name and identifiers.

identifiers.description: Other names and aliases to count as a mention, beyond the name and domain.

additional_urls.description: Other domains the competitor owns, e.g. acme.co.uk.

ai.athenahq/mcp.name: add_content
ai.athenahq/mcp.description: Add an article that is already written (for example, one drafted in this conversation) to the website's Content Hub as an editable draft. Same as pasting it into the Content Hub's blank editor: no AI model runs and no content credits are spent. Use create_content instead when Athena should research and write the piece. body is the full article in Markdown and is stored as given, except that link and image destinations with an unsafe scheme (javascript:, data:) become #. The item is created with type manual at stage generated, and the body is recorded as version 1, so get_content_draft, edit_content, revise_content and get_content_versions work on it right away. Pass title, or it is taken from the body's first heading (else its first line). sheet_id must be a tab from get_content_hub_sheets: a sheet-type tab keeps the item, a view-type tab or no sheet_id puts it in the shared pool. The item is not published. Once it is live on the site, call publish_content with its URL to start citation tracking.

ai.athenahq/mcp.name: approve_brief
ai.athenahq/mcp.description: Approve a content brief and start writing the article from it. Only valid while the piece is at status generated_brief. The article is generated from the brief exactly as it currently stands, including any revisions made with revise_brief or edits made in the app. Consumes content credits; poll get_content_status afterwards, then read the result with get_content_draft.

ai.athenahq/mcp.name: create_brand_kit
ai.athenahq/mcp.description: Create a brand kit from text the user provides: a name, guidance text per field (voice is the writing direction), voice settings and writing rules, all authored by the caller; nothing is generated. The kit starts as a draft; content generation uses it only once published, which publish: true does as version 1 (or update_brand_kit later). The website's first kit becomes its default. A name another kit uses is refused; a rule that contradicts an existing global rule is refused with the explanation and no kit is created. Kit rules need the writing rules feature on the plan. To change an existing kit, use update_brand_kit; to generate a kit from the website or uploaded documents, use the Brand Profile page.

name.description: The kit's name, unique on the website.

guidance.description: Guidance text per field, one entry per field.

field.description: voice is the writing direction; the others are audience, perspective (point of view), author (author guidance), terminology, channel (format and channel), locale (language and locale), disclosures (claims and disclosures).

text.description: The field's text. Markdown paragraphs, headings, bullets and numbered items are kept as structure.

voice_settings.description: Each 1 (formality: casual, expression: reserved, humor: serious, stance: neutral, technicality: plain) to 5 (formal, expressive, playful, opinionated, technical), or "auto" to let the writer decide. Omitted dimensions keep their value.

text.description: One writing rule, as an instruction to the writer.

category.description: A short grouping label; "" clears it.

publish.description: true publishes the new kit as version 1 so content generation can use it. Only when the user asked to publish.

ai.athenahq/mcp.name: create_content
ai.athenahq/mcp.description: Generate an article or content brief in AthenaHQ. Fetches source URLs, sends source material to external AI providers, and consumes content credits. Obtain user approval before calling. Does not publish to a website or CMS. For draft mode, auto_approve defaults to true; set false to generate only a brief and wait for approve_brief. Poll get_content_status using each returned content_ids value. Slice mode returns slice_titles and an empty content_ids array; generated items appear in list_content. To save an already-written article without generation or credit use, call add_content.

mode.description: draft: generate a brief and optionally an article from tracked prompts. snipe: draft an article using a competitor URL as input. optimize: improve an existing page for AI search. slice: turn one source URL into several articles.

title.description: Article title. Required for draft, snipe, and optimize modes.

url.description: Source page URL. Required for snipe, optimize, and slice modes. A URL without a protocol, such as example.com/article, is accepted.

prompt_ids.description: Existing tracked prompt UUIDs, up to 100. Required and nonempty for draft; omit for slice. Use IDs from the website's tracked prompt list; never invent them.

auto_approve.description: Draft mode only. Defaults to true, which continues from brief generation to article generation. Set false to pause at generated_brief until approve_brief is called.
