ai.athenahq/mcp.description: Create a location for a website

ai.athenahq/mcp.name: create_pillar
ai.athenahq/mcp.description: Create a Knowledge Base pillar (a subject area that groups brand facts) from a name and optional description. Get-or-create semantics: if a pillar with the same name already exists, it is returned with created: false instead of failing, so retries are idempotent.

ai.athenahq/mcp.name: create_prompt_tag
ai.athenahq/mcp.description: Create a prompt tag on a website, or return the existing tag when its name matches case-insensitively. Trims surrounding whitespace and rejects reserved prompt-type names. Returns the tag ID and whether it was created. Use the returned ID to assign the tag to prompts; creating a tag does not assign it to any prompts.

ai.athenahq/mcp.name: create_prompts
ai.athenahq/mcp.description: Create one or more prompts on a website

ai.athenahq/mcp.name: create_saved_view
ai.athenahq/mcp.description: Create a saved view (filter preset) for a website. Saved views appear in the dashboard filter bar for every member of the website. filters is an object keyed by filter field key, each value shaped {"id": "<unique string>", "field": "<same field key>", "operator": "is_any_of", "values": [...]}. Common field keys: "models" (slugs like "chatgpt", "perplexity", "google_ai_overview"), "competitors", "prompts", "personas", "locations", "promptTags", "attributes" (arrays of UUIDs from the matching list tools), "countries", "sourceTag". "promptTags" also accepts the builtin tokens "type:high_intent" (branded prompts) and "type:discovery" (non-branded) alongside tag UUIDs. "sourceTag" values are the builtin categories "owned", "competitor", "partner", "third_party", the states "other" (the Other badge) and "untagged" (no tag), or custom source tag UUIDs, not display labels; custom source tag ids appear on existing saved views (list the website's saved views to find them). When unsure, list the website's saved views and mirror their filter shapes. icon, when set, must be a supported Remix icon name (e.g. "RiStarLine"); invalid names are rejected with the full list. When talking to the user about a view or its filters, use the dashboard names (Branded / Non-branded prompts, Owned / Competitor / Partner / Third party / Other / No tag sources), never internal tokens, field keys, operator strings, or icon identifiers.

ai.athenahq/mcp.name: create_topic
ai.athenahq/mcp.description: Create a topic on a website (returns the existing topic when the name is already taken)

ai.athenahq/mcp.name: delete_brand_facts
ai.athenahq/mcp.description: Permanently delete 1-50 brand facts from a website's Knowledge Base. There is no undo. Ids that do not exist on the website are reported in not_found_ids rather than failing the call, so retries are idempotent. Requires an admin; on OAuth connections the signed-in user must have the admin role.

ai.athenahq/mcp.name: delete_content
ai.athenahq/mcp.description: Delete a content row. Destructive: physical row delete, no undo. Powers delete-and-retry. Bulk delete is out of scope.

ai.athenahq/mcp.name: delete_location
ai.athenahq/mcp.description: Delete a location from a website

ai.athenahq/mcp.name: delete_pillars
ai.athenahq/mcp.description: Permanently delete 1-20 Knowledge Base pillars and every fact filed under them. Facts are deleted, not unfiled; there is no undo. Ids that do not exist on the website are reported in not_found_ids rather than failing the call, so retries are idempotent; ids in failed_ids are untouched and safe to retry. Requires an admin; on OAuth connections the signed-in user must have the admin role.

ai.athenahq/mcp.name: delete_prompt
ai.athenahq/mcp.description: Delete a prompt (soft when responses exist, hard otherwise)

ai.athenahq/mcp.name: delete_topic
ai.athenahq/mcp.description: Delete a topic (soft delete; optionally also delete its prompts)

ai.athenahq/mcp.name: draft_outreach_message
ai.athenahq/mcp.description: Draft a pitch email to the author of a cited page and save it as the page's Outreach draft, replacing any previous draft. Uses the website's team-wide Outreach custom instructions, the saved author name, and the sender's name. Costs 0.1 credits per draft written (billed in whole credits every 10 drafts); free when the page cannot be read. Show the draft to the user before they send it; nothing is sent.

url.description: Cited page URL, e.g. "example.com/blog/best-tools". A contact already saved under this exact URL (for example one the Outreach page saved for a query variant its URL rules list separately) is used first. Otherwise protocol, "www." and the query string (tracking parameters) are ignored, as on the Outreach page. The page is always read at the URL given.

sender_name.description: Name to sign the email with. Defaults to the signed-in user's profile name; required for API-key sessions that should sign with a name.

ai.athenahq/mcp.name: edit_content
ai.athenahq/mcp.description: Apply exact find-and-replace edits to a content draft's article body. Deterministic, no AI model involved: your replacement text lands verbatim (use revise_content when you want an AI rewrite from an instruction). Each edit's find text must match the current body exactly once; zero or multiple matches fail the whole call and nothing is saved, so extend the find text until it is unique. Edits apply in order, later ones see earlier results, and the batch is recorded as one new version, recoverable via get_content_versions / restore_content_version. Pass expected_version_number from get_content_draft to fail with a conflict when a new version was recorded after your read (a revision, edit, or restore). An app autosave changes the body without recording a version; that drift is caught by the anchors themselves, since a moved or vanished find text fails the call.

ai.athenahq/mcp.name: find_more_prompt_discovery
ai.athenahq/mcp.description: Find more prompts for a finished Discover run: start the next round of its series with the same sources, effort level, country, language and custom instructions. The round skips every question the series already suggested and reads evidence earlier rounds did not use, so its prompts add to the same list. Invoke only after the user asks for more prompts from an existing run, and confirm with them first: each round runs the same paid research as a new run. A series takes one round at a time and at most two after the first run, and ends early after a round that found fewer than ten new prompts or nothing new to read; the tool then refuses with the reason. Returns the new round's run ID; poll the discovery history tool with it. Prompts are not added to tracking automatically. Requires prompt-management permission and the series' source entitlements.

run_id.description: A finished Discover run, or any finished round of its series, to continue.

ai.athenahq/mcp.name: find_outreach_author
ai.athenahq/mcp.description: Find who wrote a cited page and how to reach them, then save it to the page's Outreach contact. Reads the page's byline, the addresses the page publishes, and Hunter.io; when no author is found it returns the site's contact address and contact page instead. Every email comes with its source. Costs 0.1 credits when an author is found (billed in whole credits every 10 lookups); free otherwise. Overwrites the saved author fields. Obtain user confirmation before running it over many pages.

url.description: Cited page URL, e.g. "example.com/blog/best-tools". A contact already saved under this exact URL (for example one the Outreach page saved for a query variant its URL rules list separately) is used first. Otherwise protocol, "www." and the query string (tracking parameters) are ignored, as on the Outreach page. The page is always read at the URL given.

ai.athenahq/mcp.name: get_ai_insight
ai.athenahq/mcp.description: Read one stored AI insight in full, by its id from get_ai_insights: its title, headline, body, suggested action, why it happened (with reasons and their pages), its numbers (facts, each with the table it came from), its move (subject, metric, current and previous values, the direction that is good news, and a definition of what the series counts and what it is out of), its evidence (topics, competitors, prompts, URLs), and the scope its numbers were computed under (window, comparison period, Default schedule, the prompts active at the analysis, prompt-type filter, the models the citation tables leave out). The numbers are the card's as of its analysis: quote them as such, with the window and the date the analysis ran (analyzed_at). A recompute with the other tools counts today's active prompts, so it can differ. Returns a not-found error for an insight that is not this website's, and status 'no_access' when AI Insights is not part of the organization's setup.

ai.athenahq/mcp.name: get_ai_insights
ai.athenahq/mcp.description: List the website's stored AI insights: the precomputed cards on the AI Insights page, each a verified finding of one past analysis, newest analysis first and higher impact first. Each has its id, title, headline, category, impact, the days its numbers cover (window), the time the analysis ran (analyzed_at), its status (available, done, or discarded = hidden by the team), the team's rating, and its move's subject and metric. Call this first for an open-ended request for insights or for what to do ('give me some insights', 'what's interesting', 'what should I prioritize'), and answer from these cards instead of running a new analysis: highest impact first, each by its title and headline. Always state the window and the date the analysis ran, and offer a fresh look with the other analytics tools. Read one card in full with get_ai_insight. Paged: 20 by default; for more, pass limit (up to 50) and offset set to the returned next_offset until it is null. Default status is available. Returns status 'no_access' when AI Insights is not part of the organization's setup. Then, or when no insight is listed, answer from the other analytics tools.

status.description: The lifecycle to list: available (default), done, or discarded (hidden by the team).

offset.description: How many to skip: the previous read's next_offset.

ai.athenahq/mcp.name: get_brand_facts
ai.athenahq/mcp.description: List a website's brand facts from the Knowledge Base, newest first, with offset paging. By default excludes facts generated by Oracle analysis; pass include_oracle=true to include them. Filters: pillar, review status (default approved), source type, and unfiled=true for facts not under any published pillar (unfiled and pillar_id are mutually exclusive).

ai.athenahq/mcp.name: get_brand_kit
ai.athenahq/mcp.description: Read a brand kit as the Brand Profile editor shows it, to inspect or change it: the draft name, the eight guidance fields as text (voice is the writing direction), voice settings (1-5 or auto), tone traits, the kit's writing rules with ids, and the website's global writing rules with ids, plus draft and published versions. Omit kit_id for the website's default kit; available_kits lists every kit. Content generation uses a kit's published version, so has_unpublished_changes means the draft differs from it. Guidance fields longer than the clip come back shortened and listed in truncated_fields; pass fields to read those whole, which update_brand_kit's find needs. Rules are clipped too, each with its own truncated flag. Call this before update_brand_kit. To write in the brand's voice, read brandKit__get instead. Read-only.

kit_id.description: The brand kit to read. Omit it for the website's default kit; available_kits lists every kit.

fields.description: Guidance fields to return whole (up to 12,000 characters) instead of clipped at 4,000. Needed before a find edit on a clipped field.

items.description: voice is the writing direction; the others are audience, perspective (point of view), author (author guidance), terminology, channel (format and channel), locale (language and locale), disclosures (claims and disclosures).

ai.athenahq/mcp.name: get_content_draft
ai.athenahq/mcp.description: Read the current draft text of a content item — the article body as it stands right now, including every revision applied so far. Use this before revise_content to see what you are changing, and after it to confirm the result. A status of generated_brief means the brief is ready while the article is still being written, so body may still be empty. For the full record (cited urls, links, social posts) use get_content_detail instead.

ai.athenahq/mcp.name: get_content_status
ai.athenahq/mcp.description: Get the normalized pipeline status (running | succeeded | failed) for one content row, plus the raw stage behind it. Read-only. Poll once per contentId returned by create_content (content.pipeline.start). A stage of generated_brief with status running means the brief is ready and waiting — for a non-auto-approve draft it stays there until approve_brief is called, so do not treat running as always in progress. Not meaningful for tracked pages (track_content_urls / external rows): they have no generation pipeline and report running with a null stage forever — read them via get_tracked_content or get_content_detail instead.

ai.athenahq/mcp.name: get_content_version
ai.athenahq/mcp.description: Read the full text of one saved version of a content item. Use it to compare two passes (fetch both and diff them yourself) or to check what an earlier version said before restoring it.

ai.athenahq/mcp.name: get_content_versions
ai.athenahq/mcp.description: List the saved versions of a content item, newest first. Each entry carries its version number, label, how it was produced, and who made it. Use it to see how a draft evolved, then get_content_version to read a specific one, or restore_content_version to go back to it.

ai.athenahq/mcp.name: get_credit_usage
ai.athenahq/mcp.description: Read recorded organization credit consumption: total, hourly (24h) or daily trend, and charged website/group/organization pools. Use for spending trends and biggest charged pools; the credit-balance tools read current balances. For 'this month' or a specific spike, supply explicit UTC window boundaries; 30d is rolling, not a calendar month. State the returned interval. A group pool is not an originating website. The breakdown may exclude unattributed usage or be capped by the billing provider; totalCreditsUsed is authoritative, not the sum of displayed entities. Negative credits are refunds. Entities are paginated: continue with window and nextOffset while hasMore. Use credit-usage events to inspect recorded actions. Requires organization billing access on a signed-in connection, or a global organization API key. Website-scoped keys are not supported. Read-only.

window.description: Explicit UTC interval within recorded history, ending no later than now. For the current month or today, use the current UTC time as endAtUtc, not the next calendar boundary. Reuse both returned boundaries when paging.

ai.athenahq/mcp.name: get_credit_usage_events
ai.athenahq/mcp.description: Read a page of recorded credit charges/refunds and action labels for the organization, optionally filtered by originatingWebsiteId. Use to inspect a usage spike or charges behind a total. Use credit-usage totals for complete period totals. Supply explicit UTC window for calendar months. Continue with returned window, originatingWebsiteId, and nextOffset while hasMore; never compute the next offset from returned row count. Limit bounds underlying operations, each may split into several charged-pool rows. One page is not a complete action breakdown. 'Not recorded' means unknown historical action/site attribution, never infer it. Unknown raw action tags are preserved. Negative credits are refunds. Requires organization billing access on a signed-in connection, or a global organization API key. Website-scoped keys are not supported. Read-only.

window.description: Explicit UTC interval within recorded history, ending no later than now. For the current month or today, use the current UTC time as endAtUtc, not the next calendar boundary. Reuse both returned boundaries when paging.

originating_website_id.description: Optional originating website in this organization; this is different from the charged group pool.

ai.athenahq/mcp.name: get_identifiers
ai.athenahq/mcp.description: Read the identifiers of the website's brand, or of one competitor: the names, aliases and domains Athena looks for in AI responses to count a mention. default_identifiers (the name and domain) are always matched and cannot be removed; identifiers lists every other value, as the Competitors page shows them. case_sensitive tells whether matching respects letter case. Read this before update_identifiers. Read-only.

competitor_id.description: The competitor to read or edit, from get_competitors. Omit it for the website's own brand.

ai.athenahq/mcp.name: get_pillar_document
ai.athenahq/mcp.description: Fetch a pillar's synthesized markdown document from the Knowledge Base. Returns document: null when the pillar exists but has no synthesized document yet.

ai.athenahq/mcp.name: get_pillars
ai.athenahq/mcp.description: List a website's Knowledge Base pillars (excluding archived ones) with approved-fact counts, whether a synthesized document exists, and when each pillar was last researched.

ai.athenahq/mcp.name: get_prompt_discovery_runs
ai.athenahq/mcp.description: Read Discover history and progress for a website, or supply the run ID returned by discovery launch to inspect one study. Distinguishes pending, running, completed, partial, failed and cancelled. limit bounds returned runs (default 10, maximum 20); has_more means older runs remain. This is read-only: it does not start research, monitor in the background or send notifications. Candidate results can be reviewed in the application's Discover page. Requires permission to view prompts; source visibility restrictions still apply.

ai.athenahq/mcp.name: get_seo_rankings
ai.athenahq/mcp.description: Read saved Google organic rankings by explicit market and device alongside observed AI visibility. Includes recent history, missing-data reasons, freshness and committed provider budget. Does not trigger collection.

ai.athenahq/mcp.name: get_shopping_metrics
ai.athenahq/mcp.description: Get the Shopping Insights dashboard for a website over a date range: how often the brand's products appear in AI shopping answers (product carousels) versus competitors, average position and price, the top own and competitor products, the competitor leaderboard, retailer (merchant) breakdown, rank distribution, price comparison, and a daily appearances trend. Rates are percentages 0-100; positions are 1-based (lower is better). Requires a paid plan.

start_date.description: Start of the date range, YYYY-MM-DD (UTC), inclusive. Required.

end_date.description: End of the date range, YYYY-MM-DD (UTC), inclusive. Omit for today.

schedule_id.description: One schedule: "default" or a custom/archived schedule UUID. Omit for Default, which includes all pre-cutover history and ad hoc runs. Schedules cannot be combined.

models.description: Shopping-capable models to include, as an array even for one model: any of "chatgpt", "ai_mode", "gemini", "perplexity" and "copilot". Omit for all.

competitor_ids.description: Competitor UUIDs to keep in the competitor blocks, as an array even for one id. Own products are always included. Omit for all competitors.

prompt_tags.description: Prompt tag IDs to filter prompts by, as an array (list tags with get_prompt_tags). Omit for all tags.

prompt_tags_operator.description: How prompt_tags combine: "is_any_of" matches prompts with any listed tag, "has_all_of" only prompts carrying every listed tag.

target_identifiers.description: Target identifier strings to filter responses to, as an array even for one value. The literal string "no-identifier" selects responses with no target identifier. Omit for all.

top_products_limit.description: How many products to return in each of top_own_products and top_competitor_products, 1 to 50. Defaults to 10.

ai.athenahq/mcp.name: get_site_health_analytics
ai.athenahq/mcp.description: Live Google Analytics 4, Google Search Console and AI-citation figures for a website over the last 28 complete days, each beside the 28 days before (period gives both ranges; change_pct is null when the earlier period was zero). ga4: AI-referred sessions, their engagement rate and key events, organic and total sessions, AI share of sessions in percent, daily AI sessions, and the top 10 AI sources, AI landing pages and organic landing pages. gsc: clicks, impressions, CTR in percent and average position, a daily series, and the top 10 queries and pages. cited_pages: the website's pages AI answers cited most, with the Google figures for the same page. connected false means no Google property is linked for that provider; available false means it is linked but the read failed. Read live from Google, so a connection made a moment ago shows at once. Requires Site Health on the website's plan; otherwise the call fails with 403.

ai.athenahq/mcp.name: get_site_health_issue_pages
ai.athenahq/mcp.description: Page through every page one Site Health issue affects, 50 per page, open pages first and most recently seen first within a status. Give the check from the issue list; filter by status; page is 0-based and has_more says whether to continue; page 0 starts from the first affected page, so it repeats the sample pages the issue list showed inline. page_id returns that one page's row for the check. Each row carries the finding_id and task_revision an update of the page's task needs, the finding's detail, recommendation and evidence, the assignee, and the dates it was first and last seen and last checked. Requires Site Health on the website's plan; otherwise the call fails with 403.

check.description: The check id of the issue, from the issue list.

status.description: Only pages in this status.

page_id.description: Only this page's row for the check, wherever it sits.

ai.athenahq/mcp.name: get_site_health_issues
ai.athenahq/mcp.description: List a website's Site Health issues: one group per kind of problem (check) with its title, why it matters, severity (critical, warning, opportunity), priority (high, medium, low), owner (writer, developer or either; null when unknown), effort (minutes, hours, days), whether it is site-wide, counts of affected pages by status (open, in_progress, fixed, verified, dismissed), up to three sections it concentrates in, and sample affected pages with each page's detail, recommendation, evidence, assignee and task_revision. Filter by status, check, a search term, the stored URLs of specific pages (page_urls), or assignee "me" (signed-in connections only). Groups are paged: page is 0-based, page_size defaults to 25 (max 200) and total counts the groups that match; counts totals pages by status across the whole site, ignoring the status filter. A group carries at most 50 sample pages (10 when a tool calls it, which also caps page_size at 25); has_more_pages says to read the rest with the issue pages read (get_site_health_issue_pages or POST /v1/seo/issues/pages), whose page 0 repeats the sample pages. has_evidence false means the site has never been crawled or audited. Requires Site Health on the website's plan; otherwise the call fails with 403.

status.description: Only groups with at least one page in this status. Group and site counts ignore it.

check.description: One check id, as `check` names it in an earlier result.

search.description: Matches the issue title or an affected page URL.

assignee.description: Only pages assigned to the signed-in user. Not available to API keys.

page_urls.description: Only issues on these pages, up to 50, in the stored URL form: no protocol, no trailing slash, www kept.

page_size.description: Groups per page, 25 by default and 200 at most (25 at most when a tool calls it).

ai.athenahq/mcp.name: get_site_health_page
ai.athenahq/mcp.description: Read one audited page of a Site Health property: what the last audit measured (title, meta description, canonical URL, HTTP status code, word count, whether it is indexable, how the server HTML and the rendered page differ, PageSpeed with performance_score 0 to 100, largest_contentful_paint_ms and interaction_to_next_paint_ms in milliseconds and cumulative_layout_shift unitless, and the hreflang audit), the status of every audit of the page, and every finding on it with its check, detail, recommendation, evidence, severity, priority_score, when it was resolved, and verification: whether the last audit of that check passed, failed or left it unverified, with the reason. page_id comes from get_site_health_pages or from an issue's affected pages. Requires Site Health on the website's plan; otherwise the call fails with 403.

page_id.description: The page, from the inventory or an issue's affected pages.

ai.athenahq/mcp.name: get_site_health_pages
ai.athenahq/mcp.description: Browse the pages of one Site Health property, 50 per page (page is 1-based) sorted by URL, each with its last audit status and time, its count of open findings and whether it is a priority page (cited by AI answers or a top Google page, so audits read it first). Narrow by check (pages with an open finding of it), one URL, or a search term; total counts the pages that match. groups lists every check with an open finding on the property and its page count, ignoring the filters, highest priority first. Page ids feed get_site_health_page and start_site_health_audit. Requires Site Health on the website's plan; otherwise the call fails with 403.

property_id.description: The property to browse, from the properties list.

check.description: Only pages with an open finding of this check.

url.description: Only the page at this URL.

search.description: Only pages whose URL contains this text.

page.description: One-based page of 50 pages, sorted by URL.

ai.athenahq/mcp.name: get_site_health_properties
ai.athenahq/mcp.description: List a website's Site Health properties, the crawl scopes Site Health audits: root URL, included and excluded path prefixes, subdomains, sitemaps, page ceiling (max_pages), whether the property is enabled, the live page count, and the latest crawl or audit run with its status, trigger, counts and timestamps. Use it for the property_id that get_site_health_pages and start_site_health_audit take, and to see whether a run is in progress before starting another. Requires Site Health on the website's plan; otherwise the call fails with 403.

ai.athenahq/mcp.name: list_outreach_contacts
ai.athenahq/mcp.description: Read saved Outreach contacts: cited pages with their status, author, email and where the email came from, LinkedIn, contact page, and pitch draft. Only pages someone has triaged, enriched or drafted are listed; find other cited pages with the source-page analytics tools. Newest first; use offset for the next page. Read-only.

url.description: Return only this page's contact. Omit to list all.

statuses.description: Only contacts in these statuses. Omit for all.

items.description: Pipeline status. "New" means untriaged; "Rejected" removes the page from the active queue.

ai.athenahq/mcp.name: merge_pillars
ai.athenahq/mcp.description: Merge 1-20 source pillars into a published target pillar: every fact on the sources (any review status) re-files onto the target, page links carry over keeping the stronger signal, and the source pillars are then deleted. The target must be a published pillar and must not appear among the sources. Unlike the other Knowledge Base writes, retries are strict: missing source ids are rejected rather than skipped, so re-read the pillars before retrying a failed merge.

ai.athenahq/mcp.name: move_brand_facts
ai.athenahq/mcp.description: File 1-50 brand facts under a published Knowledge Base pillar — works for unfiled facts and re-files facts from other pillars. Review status never changes, and only approved facts under a published pillar feed content generation, so moving is what puts approved facts to work. Missing ids are reported in not_found_ids rather than failing the call, so retries are idempotent.

ai.athenahq/mcp.name: move_content
ai.athenahq/mcp.description: Move one or more content items to a different Content Hub sheet, or back to the shared pool. Sheet assignment is organizational metadata only: a move never changes an item's stage, brief, body, versions, URL, or metrics, and the item stays fully readable and revisable. targetSheetId must be a "sheet"-type tab from the Content Hub sheets list — view-type tabs (e.g. All content) are computed filters, not assignable; pass null to unassign back to the shared pool they display. Batch is all-or-nothing: if any contentIds entry does not belong to the website, nothing moves. Custom-column values follow each item when the target has a matching column (same name and type; missing columns are auto-created); values whose column conflicts by type are dropped, and multi-select selections whose option is missing on the matched target column are removed — both counts are reported. Each moved item is returned with its previous and new sheet id so no follow-up read is needed.

ai.athenahq/mcp.name: publish_content
ai.athenahq/mcp.description: Record an already-published article's URL in AthenaHQ for citation and mention tracking. Does not upload or publish content to a website or CMS. Call only after the article is live. Sets the first publication time and moves the pipeline stage to done. A first publish requires a finished article (stage generated), with one exception: an optimize draft is created from a page that is already live and can be marked published while it waits at stage pending, as long as no Athena review is running on it. Briefs, still-generating or failed pieces, optimize drafts with a review in flight, and items with a scheduled CMS publish are rejected with the reason. Pass the exact public URL of the live page (a bare domain path like acme.com/blog/post is fine; the protocol is stripped on store). Calling it again on an already-published item (including external and imported pages, which are live by definition) updates the tracked URL only, keeping the original publish time. This is the only way to set a content URL over MCP; rename_content is deliberately title-only.

ai.athenahq/mcp.name: remove_competitors
ai.athenahq/mcp.description: Stop tracking competitors on a website, 1 to 25 per call, by id from get_competitors, as the Competitors page's delete does. Returns one result per id, in order: removed, no_change (already removed), or not_found (not a competitor of this website). Past mentions and citations are kept, and a removed competitor can be restored on the Competitors page. Reanalyzing past responses happens only when someone runs the backfill on the Competitors page, which costs credits; this tool never starts it and costs no credits.

competitor_ids.description: The competitors to stop tracking, by id from get_competitors.

ai.athenahq/mcp.name: rename_content
ai.athenahq/mcp.description: Rename a content row's title. URL editing is not supported — URL is the content asset's stable identity and cannot be changed here.

ai.athenahq/mcp.name: restore_content_version
ai.athenahq/mcp.description: Bring an earlier version's text back as the current draft — use it when a later pass came out worse than an earlier one. Nothing is deleted: the restored text is appended as a new version on top of the history, so the passes in between remain readable and restorable.

ai.athenahq/mcp.name: revise_brief
ai.athenahq/mcp.description: Rewrite a content brief from a natural-language instruction (for example: 'add a section on pricing objections', 'cut the competitor comparison'). An AI model performs the rewrite server-side, so the result is generated text, not your literal wording. Records each pass as a version; iterate by calling it again, since each call starts from the current brief. Most useful while a piece waits at status generated_brief, where the brief still shapes what the article will say — call approve_brief once it reads right. It also works after the article exists, to correct the brief for a later regeneration; note that revising the brief does NOT rewrite an already-generated article, so use revise_content for that.

ai.athenahq/mcp.name: revise_content
ai.athenahq/mcp.description: Rewrite an existing content draft from a natural-language instruction (for example: 'tighten the intro', 'add a section on pricing', 'remove the second half'). An AI model performs the rewrite server-side, so the result is generated text, not your literal wording; when you already have the exact replacement text, use edit_content instead. Applies the change to the whole article and records it as a new version, so earlier passes stay recoverable via get_content_versions / restore_content_version. Iterate by calling it again — each call starts from the current text, so no version id is needed. Use this instead of create_content to change a draft; it edits in place rather than generating a new piece. The returned body is always the complete replacement article, never just the edited passage; compare body_word_count with previous_body_word_count to confirm nothing unexpected was lost.

ai.athenahq/mcp.name: search_brand_facts
ai.athenahq/mcp.description: Semantic search over a website's approved brand facts in the Knowledge Base. Reaches facts not filed under any pillar. Returns fact text with confidence, source URL and quote, and the published pillar it belongs to (null when unfiled).

ai.athenahq/mcp.name: set_outreach_status
ai.athenahq/mcp.description: Move cited pages to an Outreach pipeline status (New, Todo, In Progress, Done, Rejected), as the Outreach inbox and board do. Each change to an existing contact is recorded in its activity history. Pages without a contact get one at the new status, starting with no activity entries; "New" only resets existing contacts and creates none. "Rejected" removes pages from the active queue; "New" returns them to untriaged. Up to 100 pages per call. Obtain user confirmation before calling.

items.description: Cited page URL, e.g. "example.com/blog/best-tools". A contact already saved under this exact URL (for example one the Outreach page saved for a query variant its URL rules list separately) is used first. Otherwise protocol, "www." and the query string (tracking parameters) are ignored, as on the Outreach page. The page is always read at the URL given.

status.description: Pipeline status. "New" means untriaged; "Rejected" removes the page from the active queue.

ai.athenahq/mcp.name: set_prompt_tags
ai.athenahq/mcp.description: Replace all tag assignments on an existing prompt. For additions or removals, read the prompt's current tags with get_prompts, resolve tag IDs with get_prompt_tags, and pass the full resulting set. Existing assignments omitted from tag_ids are removed; an empty array clears all assignments. Tag definitions and the prompt itself are preserved.

ai.athenahq/mcp.name: set_prompts_status
ai.athenahq/mcp.description: Pause or unpause multiple prompts in one transaction

ai.athenahq/mcp.name: source_tags__create
ai.athenahq/mcp.description: Create a custom source tag with a name, URL patterns and optionally an icon and colour. Read the tag listing first: built-in tags already cover media, social, government, e-commerce, review sites, PR wires, academic and wiki sources, and a host they miss is better added to the built-in tag than given a new one. Obtain user confirmation before calling. MCP executes immediately after authorization; Athena AI chat presents an approval card. Patterns support hosts (example.com), subtrees (*.example.com), path sections (example.com/blog), exact pages (example.com/blog$) and query constraints. Up to 500 patterns. These are source tags, not prompt tags.

name.description: Custom tag name. Names of built-in tags (Media, Social, Government, …) and of Owned and Competitor are reserved.

items.description: Host (example.com), subtree (*.example.com), path section (example.com/blog), exact page (example.com/blog$) or query constraint (youtube.com/watch?v=abc).

icon.description: Optional icon key from the curated set (for example newspaper, capsule, hospital, graduation-cap, building). Omit for a letter badge.

color.description: Optional colour family: ochre, clay, brick, amber, olive, moss, teal, slate, ink, mauve or plum. Default ink.

ai.athenahq/mcp.name: source_tags__delete
ai.athenahq/mcp.description: Permanently delete a custom source tag and all its pattern assignments; retain source records. Built-in tags and Owned/Competitor cannot be deleted; remove patterns from a built-in tag instead. Read the listing first and pass the tag's revision as expected-revision. Obtain explicit user confirmation identifying the tag and its patterns before calling. MCP executes immediately after authorization; Athena AI chat presents an approval card. If the tag changed, read again. Never retry a declined proposal unless asked. A false analytics-refresh result means the tag was deleted but filtered analytics may still be cached.

tag_id.description: Custom source tag ID returned by the source-tag listing tool.

expected_revision.description: Revision returned by the source-tag listing tool for this tag.

ai.athenahq/mcp.name: source_tags__get_sources
ai.athenahq/mcp.description: List cited domains by tag coverage, most cited first with citation counts: either the domains one custom source tag matches (tag ID), or, with untagged true, the domains no tag covers at all. Built-in tags (platform) and Owned/Competitor (entity) are refused as tag IDs: their membership is automatic and not listable; add or remove patterns on them instead. Start from untagged when asked which domains still need tags or which new tags to suggest.

tag_id.description: Custom tag ID from the listing tool. Built-in tags are refused. Omit and set untagged to list sources no tag covers.

untagged.description: true lists cited domains that carry no tag at all: not Owned, not Competitor, no built-in tag, no custom tag. Use this to find what still needs tagging; then propose adding hosts to a built-in tag or a new custom tag.

ai.athenahq/mcp.name: source_tags__list
ai.athenahq/mcp.description: Read every source tag this website sees: Owned and Competitor (entity), the built-in classes AthenaHQ classifies automatically (platform: Media, Social, Government, E-Commerce, Review sites, PR Wire, Academic and research, Wiki) and the website's custom tags. Built-in tags list only what this website added or removed, never the platform's own patterns; custom tags list their patterns. Read this before proposing, creating, editing or deleting tags, and prefer adding hosts to a built-in tag over creating a near-duplicate. To find sources no tag covers, call source_tags__get_sources with untagged true. The Source Tag filter also takes two values that are not tags and are not listed here: 'other' (sources the Tags column badges Other) and 'untagged' (sources with no tag). Filter by name substring or tag ID; page tags with offset, page one tag's patterns with tag ID and pattern offset.

query.description: Optional tag-name substring. Omit to list all names.

tag_id.description: Actual UUID returned by this tool. Omit to list all tags; never use a placeholder.

limit.description: Tags per page: 1 through 50, default 20. Use offset for the next page.

ai.athenahq/mcp.name: source_tags__update
ai.athenahq/mcp.description: Edit a source tag. Custom tag: rename, add patterns, remove exact patterns from the listing. Built-in tag (platform): add patterns to this website's copy so they carry the tag here, or remove patterns so they stop carrying it here; a removal is accepted only for a pattern the tag currently applies to (by a platform rule, by automatic classification, or by your own addition), and an addition is accepted only when the pattern does not already carry the tag. Owned and Competitor cannot be edited here; their patterns live in Brand Profile and Competitors. Read the listing first and pass the tag's revision as expected-revision. Obtain explicit user confirmation of the exact changes before calling; MCP executes immediately after authorization; Athena AI chat presents an approval card. If the tag changed, read again. Never retry a declined proposal unless asked. Up to 500 additions and 500 removals. A false analytics-refresh result means the edit saved but filtered analytics may still be cached.

name.description: Custom tag name. Names of built-in tags (Media, Social, Government, …) and of Owned and Competitor are reserved.

items.description: Host (example.com), subtree (*.example.com), path section (example.com/blog), exact page (example.com/blog$) or query constraint (youtube.com/watch?v=abc).

ai.athenahq/mcp.name: start_prompt_discovery
ai.athenahq/mcp.description: Start a Discover study to find evidence-grounded, untracked prompt opportunities for a website. Invoke after explicit user intent to start research and review the sources, country, language, requested prompt count and custom instructions with the user. This launches asynchronous external research and model calls; the prompt count is a target, not a guaranteed yield. Sources: website_analysis (website), social (market discussions), search_console (connected Search Console), keyword_gaps (plan-gated keyword opportunities), competitive_landscape (plan-gated category questions and comparisons researched from the website's tracked competitors; requires at least one tracked competitor), brand_guidelines (requires custom instructions). Returns the run ID and version when startup succeeds. Prompts are not automatically added to tracking. Poll the discovery history/progress tool with the returned run ID; do not start another study to check status. Requires prompt-management permission and source entitlements. Candidate results can be reviewed in the application's Discover page.

country.description: Country name or ISO code; defaults to United States.

language.description: Supported locale, for example en-US. Defaults to en-US.

custom_instructions.description: Required when brand_guidelines (Custom instructions) is selected. Focus discovery on the customer's requested topics.

ai.athenahq/mcp.name: start_response_streaming
ai.athenahq/mcp.description: Run tracked prompts against external AI providers to collect new responses for a website. Sends prompt text to the selected providers, stores their responses in AthenaHQ, and consumes response credits. Starts immediately; use only for a user-requested run. Returns a workflow_id; poll get_response_streaming_status over MCP or GET /api/v1/response-streaming/status over the API for progress.

schedule_id.description: Schedule UUID to attribute this run to and take prompt selectors from. A nonempty prompt_ids selection overrides those selectors. Omit to attribute the run to Default and run every active prompt unless prompt_ids is supplied. Explicit model, fan-out, persona and location choices apply to this run.

prompt_ids.description: Specific tracked prompt UUIDs to run, from 1 to 1,000. Overrides schedule prompt selectors when supplied. Omit to use schedule_id selectors, or every active prompt when schedule_id is also omitted. Paused prompts are skipped.

selected_models.description: Map of model id to enabled flag, e.g. { "chatgpt": true, "ai_overview": true, "ai_mode": false }. Model ids: chatgpt, ai_overview (Google AI Overviews; google_ai_overview is also accepted), perplexity, gemini, copilot, ai_mode, grok, claude, deepseek, meta_ai, mistral. An id set to true that names no model is rejected. Omit to run all enabled models.

ai.athenahq/mcp.name: start_site_health_audit
ai.athenahq/mcp.description: Start a Site Health audit of one property. mode full (the default) crawls the property, then audits every page the crawl leaves; a crawl already running is joined and audits when it ends. mode sample audits a few pages from every section plus the priority pages; page_ids (1 to 100) re-audits only those pages, which is how a fix is checked. Refused with 400 when the property is disabled. mode full is refused with 409 when a full audit already covers the property or a sample or page_ids audit holds it (try again once that ends). mode sample and page_ids are refused with 409 while any crawl or audit of the property runs, with 400 when the property has no pages yet, and with 404 when a page id is not in the current inventory. Returns the run id (null while a crawl runs first, since its audit run is created when the crawl ends), the property name, how many pages the run reads (in mode full, the inventory before the crawl), whether it is a sample and whether a crawl runs first. Results reach the issue list as the run progresses; the properties list shows the run's status. Requires Site Health on the website's plan; otherwise the call fails with 403.

property_id.description: The property to audit, from the properties list.

page_ids.description: Re-audit only these pages (1 to 100), from the inventory or an issue's affected pages. Overrides mode.

mode.description: full crawls the property first and audits every page it leaves; sample audits a few pages per section plus the priority pages.

ai.athenahq/mcp.name: track_content_urls
ai.athenahq/mcp.description: Register existing pages or third-party URLs as tracked Content Hub items so Athena attributes citations and mentions to them. Creates external content rows from bare URLs with no generation and no credit cost. Tracking starts immediately: the normalized URL becomes the citation/metric join key, so pages cited in the website's monitored AI responses accrue metrics with no publish step (use it for guest posts, partner placements, or any page Athena did not generate). Idempotent per URL: a URL already present on the website (any content type) is not duplicated; the response lists it under skipped with the existing content_id and type. Check that type before chaining destructive calls (a skip can resolve to first-party generated content that shares the URL). Rows are created without page text, which citation tracking does not need; the body can be filled from the app later. Duplicate URLs within one call (including tracking-param variants of the same page) collapse to one row, first occurrence wins. Optional sheet_id files rows under a Content Hub tab; view-type tabs resolve to the main pool (null), echoed per row. Optional per-URL fields set the customer's own Content Hub columns on the created row, addressed by column name as shown on the destination tab (text, number, date, checkbox, link, and multi-select columns; unknown multi-select options are created). An unknown column name or a value that does not fit the column type rejects the whole call and nothing is tracked; skipped URLs keep their existing values. If the user names a destination tab, resolve its id with get_content_hub_sheets before tracking. Omitting sheet_id uses the shared pool, not the user's currently open tab. After the call, report created_count and skipped_count separately, name the returned destination_name, and share content_hub_url so the user can open each item. Skipped rows keep their existing tab: use their returned destination and never describe them as newly added or moved.

ai.athenahq/mcp.name: update_brand_fact
ai.athenahq/mcp.description: Update one brand fact's text, source URL, or confidence in the Knowledge Base. Only provided fields change; pass source_url: "" to clear the source. Changing the text creates a new fact (new id) and archives the current one; the new fact keeps the current review status and the response carries it. Source URL and confidence edits update the fact in place. Duplicates across other facts are not rejected here (Knowledge Base dedup owns those). Does not change review status.

ai.athenahq/mcp.name: update_brand_kit
ai.athenahq/mcp.description: Change one brand kit's name, guidance text, voice settings, or kit writing rules, and optionally publish it, under the same rules as the Brand Profile page. Call get_brand_kit first. Edits save to the kit's draft; content generation keeps using the published version until publish is true, which creates a new immutable version (the Brand Profile page can restore earlier ones). A guidance entry without find replaces the whole field with text (empty text clears it); with find, text replaces that passage, which must occur exactly once in the field text get_brand_kit returned (empty text deletes it). Voice settings take 1-5 or "auto"; omitted settings keep their value. Rules: add new ones, update by id (omitted fields keep their value; category "" clears it), or remove by id. Kit rules need the writing rules feature on the plan. A rule that contradicts an existing kit or global rule is refused with the explanation and nothing is saved; a rename to a name another kit uses is refused. When the result says the kit changed in another session, call get_brand_kit again and retry. outcome saved_publish_failed means the draft was saved but not published; publish_error says why. Global writing rules are changed with update_global_rules, not here.

kit_id.description: The brand kit, from get_brand_kit's available_kits.

name.description: A new name, unique on the website.

guidance.description: Guidance text changes, one entry per field. Without find, text replaces the whole field (empty text clears it). With find, text replaces that passage (empty text deletes it).

field.description: voice is the writing direction; the others are audience, perspective (point of view), author (author guidance), terminology, channel (format and channel), locale (language and locale), disclosures (claims and disclosures).

text.description: The new text. Markdown paragraphs, headings, bullets and numbered items are kept as structure.

find.description: A passage to replace with text, copied exactly from the field text get_brand_kit returned; it must occur exactly once. Omit it to replace the whole field.

voice_settings.description: Each 1 (formality: casual, expression: reserved, humor: serious, stance: neutral, technicality: plain) to 5 (formal, expressive, playful, opinionated, technical), or "auto" to let the writer decide. Omitted dimensions keep their value.

text.description: One writing rule, as an instruction to the writer.

category.description: A short grouping label; "" clears it.

update.description: By id; omitted fields keep their value.

text.description: One writing rule, as an instruction to the writer.

category.description: A short grouping label; "" clears it.

is_active.description: false keeps the rule but stops applying it.

rules.description: Writing rules to add, update by id, or remove by id. Ids come from get_brand_kit.

publish.description: true publishes the saved draft as a new version, which content generation uses from then on. Only when the user asked to publish.

ai.athenahq/mcp.name: update_global_rules
ai.athenahq/mcp.description: Add, update or remove the website's global writing rules, the ones the Global rules tab holds and every brand kit and every future piece of content follows. Call get_brand_kit first: its global_rules carry the ids. Add new rules, update by id (omitted fields keep their value; category "" clears it), or remove by id. There is no draft: the change is live for all content generation as soon as it is saved, as a new version the Global rules tab's change history can restore. A rule that contradicts an existing global or kit rule is refused with the explanation and nothing is saved; when the result says the rules changed in another session, call get_brand_kit again and retry. Needs the writing rules feature on the plan. A rule meant for one kit only belongs in update_brand_kit, not here.

text.description: One writing rule, as an instruction to the writer.

category.description: A short grouping label; "" clears it.

update.description: By id; omitted fields keep their value.

text.description: One writing rule, as an instruction to the writer.

category.description: A short grouping label; "" clears it.

is_active.description: false keeps the rule but stops applying it.

ai.athenahq/mcp.name: update_identifiers
ai.athenahq/mcp.description: Add or remove identifiers on the website's brand, or on one competitor, under the same rules as the Competitors page. Call get_identifiers first. The name and domain cannot be removed. An identifier that is already listed, or that another tracked brand or competitor on this website already uses, is refused, and nothing is saved. New AI responses use the change right away. Past responses are reanalyzed only when someone runs the backfill on the Competitors page, which costs credits; this tool never starts it. changes_awaiting_backfill counts the edits waiting for it, not responses.

competitor_id.description: The competitor to read or edit, from get_competitors. Omit it for the website's own brand.

add.description: Identifiers to add, exactly as they should match (trimmed).

remove.description: Identifiers to remove, exactly as get_identifiers lists them.

ai.athenahq/mcp.name: update_location
ai.athenahq/mcp.description: Update a location for a website

ai.athenahq/mcp.name: update_outreach_contact
ai.athenahq/mcp.description: Edit a cited page's Outreach contact: author name, email, LinkedIn, or the draft's subject and body. Creates the contact when the page has none. Supply at least one field; only the fields supplied change, and null clears a field. A changed email is labeled as entered manually. Each change is recorded in the contact's activity history. Obtain user confirmation of the new values before calling.

url.description: Cited page URL, e.g. "example.com/blog/best-tools". A contact already saved under this exact URL (for example one the Outreach page saved for a query variant its URL rules list separately) is used first. Otherwise protocol, "www." and the query string (tracking parameters) are ignored, as on the Outreach page. The page is always read at the URL given.

author_name.description: Author name. Null clears it; omit to keep it.

email.description: Email to pitch. Null clears it; omit to keep it.

linkedin.description: Author LinkedIn URL. Null clears it; omit to keep it.

subject.description: Draft subject. Null clears it; omit to keep it.

message.description: Draft body. Null clears it; omit to keep it.

ai.athenahq/mcp.name: update_pillar
ai.athenahq/mcp.description: Update a Knowledge Base pillar's name, description, or status. At least one of name, description, or status must be provided; only provided fields change, and description: "" clears the stored description. Renaming fails with a conflict when another pillar already uses the name. Status accepts published or archived: archiving hides the pillar from get_pillars and stops its facts feeding content generation, while keeping the facts stored.

ai.athenahq/mcp.name: update_prompt
ai.athenahq/mcp.description: Update a prompt's metadata (text, type, topic, geography)

ai.athenahq/mcp.name: update_site_health_issue
ai.athenahq/mcp.description: Set the work status (todo, in_progress, or dismissed for not an issue) or the assignee of a whole Site Health issue: every unresolved finding of one check across the website, in one write, as the status and assignee controls on an issue do. Omit a field to leave it as it is; unassign true (or assignee_user_id null) unassigns every page. Returns how many task rows changed; a repeated write changes none. The assignee is emailed once for the pages they now hold. Signed-in connections only: an API key has no teammate to act as, so API-key connections are not offered this tool and a direct call is refused with 403. Requires Site Health on the website's plan; otherwise the call fails with 403.

check.description: The check id of the issue, from the issue list.

work_status.description: todo, in_progress or dismissed (not an issue).

assignee_user_id.description: A teammate with analytics access on the website, as get_user_by_email or an earlier assignee.id gives it; null unassigns every page (chat tools send unassign true instead); absent leaves assignees as they are.

unassign.description: true clears the assignee. Chat tools must use this: a null assignee_user_id is dropped as unspecified. Cannot be sent with an assignee_user_id.

ai.athenahq/mcp.name: update_site_health_task
ai.athenahq/mcp.description: Assign one Site Health finding to a teammate or set its work status: todo, in_progress, ready_to_verify, or dismissed (not an issue, which stays closed even when a later audit finds it again). Pass the page's finding_id and task_revision from the issue list or the issue pages read as finding_id and revision; a revision that is no longer current, or a finding that has since recurred, is refused with 409, so re-read first. unassign true (or assignee_user_id null) clears the assignee; the teammate must have analytics access on the website. A newly assigned teammate is emailed. Returns the new revision with the before and after assignee and status. Signed-in connections only: an API key has no teammate to act as, so API-key connections are not offered this tool and a direct call is refused with 403. Requires Site Health on the website's plan; otherwise the call fails with 403.

finding_id.description: The finding, as `finding_id` names it on an affected page.

revision.description: The page's `task_revision` from the same read; a stale value is refused.

assignee_user_id.description: A teammate with analytics access on the website, as get_user_by_email or an earlier assignee.id gives it; null clears the assignee (chat tools send unassign true instead).

unassign.description: true clears the assignee. Chat tools must use this: a null assignee_user_id is dropped as unspecified. Cannot be sent with an assignee_user_id.

work_status.description: todo, in_progress, ready_to_verify or dismissed (not an issue).

ai.athenahq/mcp.name: update_topic
ai.athenahq/mcp.description: Update a topic's name or description

ai.atmy/air-quality.name: search_cities
ai.atmy/air-quality.description: Find the cities with an Atmy air-quality summary by name (any language) or country. Returns slugs to pass to the other tools.

query.description: Part of the city name in any site language.

country.description: Country name or ISO code.

lang.description: Language of city and country names and of the page link; default en.

ai.atmy/air-quality.name: get_air_quality
ai.atmy/air-quality.description: PM2.5 now in a city (mean of the latest reading of each eligible sensor, at most 60 minutes old; a government station hour up to 3 hours old, with the time it was measured) with its US EPA category and the weather now (temperature, humidity, pressure, wind, clouds, precipitation), plus the last completed day from the Atmy Data Hub with its weather. Pass city or lat/lon.

city.description: City name in any of the site languages, a slug like "russia/krasnoyarsk", or the Atmy city id.

country.description: Country name, to tell apart cities with the same name.

lat.description: Latitude; with lon, the nearest city with an Atmy summary within 50 km.

lang.description: Language of city and country names and of the page link; default en.

ai.atmy/air-quality.name: get_air_quality_history
ai.atmy/air-quality.description: Daily PM2.5 of a city from the Atmy Data Hub (UTC days, sensors after the quality check) with the day's weather from 2026-01-19 (mean, lowest and highest temperature, humidity, pressure, wind, strongest gust, clouds): the last days, or any period since 2017 with from/to, at most 400 days per call. For the whole history or records use get_air_quality_monthly first.

city.description: City name in any of the site languages, a slug like "russia/krasnoyarsk", or the Atmy city id.

country.description: Country name, to tell apart cities with the same name.

lat.description: Latitude; with lon, the nearest city with an Atmy summary within 50 km.

lang.description: Language of city and country names and of the page link; default en.

days.description: How many days back from the last completed day; ignored with from/to.

from.description: First day YYYY-MM-DD (2017-01-01 or later).

to.description: Last day YYYY-MM-DD; default the last completed day.

ai.atmy/air-quality.name: get_air_quality_monthly
ai.atmy/air-quality.description: The whole measurement history of a city from the Atmy Data Hub: PM2.5 per month with the month's weather from 2026-01, yearly means (complete years marked), the dirtiest and cleanest months and days. For questions like "how has the air changed" or "the most polluted month on record".

city.description: City name in any of the site languages, a slug like "russia/krasnoyarsk", or the Atmy city id.

country.description: Country name, to tell apart cities with the same name.

lat.description: Latitude; with lon, the nearest city with an Atmy summary within 50 km.

lang.description: Language of city and country names and of the page link; default en.

ai.atmy/air-quality.name: get_city_forecast
ai.atmy/air-quality.description: The next hours of a city: temperature, wind, humidity, precipitation and the pollution accumulation index 0–100 (how strongly the weather keeps particles near the ground). A weather estimate, not a PM2.5 forecast.

city.description: City name in any of the site languages, a slug like "russia/krasnoyarsk", or the Atmy city id.

country.description: Country name, to tell apart cities with the same name.

lat.description: Latitude; with lon, the nearest city with an Atmy summary within 50 km.

lang.description: Language of city and country names and of the page link; default en.

ai.atmy/air-quality.name: get_country_ranking
ai.atmy/air-quality.description: Cities of a country ranked by daily PM2.5 for the last completed day (Atmy Data Hub), most polluted or cleanest first.

country.description: Country name in any site language or the ISO code, e.g. "Russia", "Сербия", "DE".

settlements.description: Large cities only, or every settlement with enough sensors.

lang.description: Language of city and country names and of the page link; default en.

ai.atmy/air-quality.name: list_sensor_networks
ai.atmy/air-quality.description: The sensor networks in Atmy (Sensor.Community, AirGradient, Atmy, and government stations of official networks) with their number of sensors, how many pass the quality check, and their license.

ai.atmy/air-quality.name: find_sensors
ai.atmy/air-quality.description: Single sensors with their latest reading (PM1, PM2.5, PM10, temperature, humidity, pressure), network and quality check: status, rating 0–10 of the last checked day, the mean rating of the last 7 days and the reasons. Filter by city, country, or a point with a radius; sort=rating puts the most reliable sensors first.

ai.auteng/docs.name: auteng_docs_create
ai.auteng/docs.description:
Create a document in the agent's workspace.

Requires EIP-191 wallet signature auth. Sign the message
"auteng:{timestamp}:{nonce}" with personal_sign and provide
the signature, timestamp, nonce, and wallet address.

Args:
    wallet_address: 0x... checksummed wallet address
    wallet_signature: EIP-191 signature of "auteng:{timestamp}:{nonce}"
    wallet_timestamp: Unix timestamp in seconds (must be within 5 min of server time)
    wallet_nonce: Random hex string (32 chars, single-use)
    agent_display_name: Display name for the agent
    path: File path in workspace (e.g. "reports/q1.md"). Must end with extension.
    content: Markdown content (max 100 KB)
    title: Optional display title (derived from path if omitted)

ai.autonomad/travel.name: search_hotels
ai.autonomad/travel.description: Searches hotels and other places to stay by city or country and check-in/check-out dates, with optional filters for brand, room type, maximum nightly rate, star rating and amenities. Results come from our hotel partners and hotels contracted directly with Autonomad, and include room options, the cancellation policy, a photo and whether each result can be booked. Prices: quote all_in_usd (all_in_per_night_usd per night), the full price of the stay, and say how it is paid: paid_at_booking_usd on autonomad.ai at booking, plus due_at_hotel_usd collected by the hotel at check-in (resort or property fees, named in due_at_hotel_fees). A hotel with hotel_fees_unknown has no all-in price: say its hotel fees could not be confirmed, never that nothing is due at the hotel. max_rate_usd and cheapest-first use the all-in nightly price. brand keeps only hotels of that brand (e.g. "Kimpton"). Every star level is included, ranked best first (guest score or star rating, then price); a hotel whose star rating is unknown has `stars` null. If the person wants only higher-rated hotels, pass min_star_rating (hotels with an unknown rating are then left out and counted in meta.unrated_excluded); if they want the cheapest first, pass flexible: true. Searching does not reserve anything or charge anyone. If the traveler gave no length, assume about 7 nights abroad (6 for Mexico, 4 for Canada from the US), 3 at home, and tell them it's an assumption. After showing hotels, offer the person a booking link for the one they like; when they pick one or ask how to book, call create_booking_intent with that hotel from these results (searching again is not needed to book).

ai.autonomad/travel.name: search_flights
ai.autonomad/travel.description:
Searches flights between two airports (IATA codes such as JFK or LHR) on a departure date, with an optional return date, cabin class, travelers, maximum price and nonstop filter. Results come from our flight partner's airline inventory and include the airline, flight numbers, times, stops, duration, fare, baggage and refundability. Each result is ONE itinerary (the same flights at the same times) with its `fare_options`, cheapest first: each has its own offer_id, fare brand (e.g. Basic Economy, Main Cabin, Business), cabin, price_usd, `rule` (changes and refund in a few words), `bags` (the bags included with that fare, in words to repeat as given: a basic fare often has none, and not provided by the airline means unknown, not none), `dot_24h_refund_eligible` (true = the US DOT 24-hour rule covers that fare: the traveler can cancel within 24 hours of booking for a full refund; say so only when it is true), changeable/refundable and, when stated, change_penalty_usd and refund_penalty_usd (the AIRLINE's penalties: what the traveler loses to the airline on a change or a refund). Those are the airline's terms only: Autonomad's own change and cancellation fees come on top and are stated on the booking page and in create_booking_intent's flight_money_terms, so never call a fare free to change or free to cancel. When the cheapest fare is Basic Economy (is_basic_economy), say so plainly and repeat its terms exactly as returned (its `rule`, fare_note and fare_warning): Basic Economy fares differ by airline, so never describe one's changes or refunds in any other words. Offer the other fares and let the person choose. Searching does not reserve anything or charge anyone.

Travelers can be any age: only the account holder who books and pays must be 18 or older. For a party with children, send `adults`, `children_ages` (one age 0-17 per child who has their own seat, as of the last flight of the trip) and `infants_on_lap` (under-2s on an adult's lap, at most one per adult); at most 9 travelers in total. With any child or lap infant in the search, each offer's price_usd is the total for every traveler and there is no per-person price: quote the total, never divide it.

Booking: after showing flights, offer the person a booking link for the one they like. When they pick a flight or fare, say they want to book, or ask how to book, call create_booking_intent with that flight from these results (with the chosen fare) — searching again is not needed to book, and the website re-checks the price at checkout.

A name is flown as that place: for a town, region or island the airports near it are compared (meta.arrival_airports, with the drive from each) and each offer says which one it lands at. A code is flown to that airport only.
