ai.buildwithorbit/orbit.name: search
ai.buildwithorbit/orbit.description:
Find and evaluate public API endpoints and MCPs that match your query. Set `q` to a natural language query, keywords, an API name, or a question — results are matched by meaning and keyword; each result includes `id`, `resourceType` (`endpoint` or `mcp`), `name`, `description`, `method` (for an `endpoint`) or `transport` (for an `mcp`), `url`, and `evaluateGuide` — an evaluation of what the endpoint or MCP does, when to use it, and its limitations. Review `evaluateGuide` to pick the best fit, then pass each chosen result's `id` and `resourceType` (as `type`) to `integrate`. Paginate with `cursor` from `meta.nextCursor` (`limit` defaults to 10, max 25; pagination stops at 40 results total). No authentication required.

Best practices for querying:
- Use focused keyword queries that include the product or provider name along with the endpoint details, for example "PayPal create invoice".
- Alternatively, use natural language queries such as "PayPal API to create an invoice".
- Avoid jumbled queries that cram many unrelated keywords into a single query, for example "paypal invoice payment delivery payments ordering".
- Avoid OR-separated queries such as "paypal invoice OR paypal create invoice OR paypal OR invoice creation".
- If you need to explore multiple intents, try each as a separate call.

clientName.description: Name of the client application or agent invoking this tool (e.g. "cursor/composer-2.5", "claude/sonnet-4.6", "codex/gpt-5.6-sol"). Used for anonymous usage analytics.

cursor.description: Pagination cursor from a prior response's `meta.nextCursor`. Omit for the first page.

q.description: Free-text search: a natural language query, keywords, an API name, or a question (e.g. "weather forecast", "twilio", "Add tracking details for an existing paypal order"). Matched by meaning and keyword.

ai.buildwithorbit/orbit.name: integrate
ai.buildwithorbit/orbit.description: Get integration details for public endpoints and MCPs from `search` results. Provide a `task` describing what you want to accomplish and up to 10 `resources` — each with an `id` and `type` taken from the matching search result's `resourceType`. Returns a task brief covering authentication, base URLs, request steps, parameters, expected responses, dependencies between steps, and other important considerations.

clientName.description: Name of the client application or agent invoking this tool (e.g. "cursor/composer-2.5", "claude/sonnet-4.6", "codex/gpt-5.6-sol"). Used for anonymous usage analytics.

resources.description: Up to 10 endpoints or MCPs to integrate. Each entry needs an `id` and `type` from a search result (`type` is the result's `resourceType`).

id.description: Resource id from a search result's `id` field.

type.description: Resource type from a search result's `resourceType` field (`endpoint` or `mcp`).

task.description: What you want to accomplish with the selected resources (max 512 characters).

ai.bumblebox/mail.name: search_emails
ai.bumblebox/mail.description: Searches every connected mailbox (sender, subject, preview), newest first. Operators: from:, subject:, before:YYYY-MM-DD, after:YYYY-MM-DD, in:sent (only what the user sent, from any mailbox or alias); the rest is free text. Deleted emails are not returned.

ai.bumblebox/mail.name: get_email
ai.bumblebox/mail.description: One email in full: sender, recipients, date, subject, plain-text body, attachment names, folder and BumbleBox classification.

id.description: Email id, as returned by search_emails or list_to_answer.

ai.bumblebox/mail.name: list_to_answer
ai.bumblebox/mail.description: Received emails BumbleBox classified as needing a reply and still in the inbox, newest first.

ai.bumblebox/mail.name: search_contacts
ai.bumblebox/mail.description: Contacts BumbleBox knows from the mail history (name, address, organization domain, exchange counts, last exchanges, VIP mark, note), matched on name, address or domain.

ai.bumblebox/mail.name: list_folders
ai.bumblebox/mail.description: The folders of each connected mailbox, as last synced. Trash, spam, sent and drafts are left out.

ai.bumblebox/mail.name: list_calendar_events
ai.bumblebox/mail.description: Events of the connected Google calendars between two dates (default: the next 7 days, at most 62 days).

ai.bumblebox/mail.name: draft_reply
ai.bumblebox/mail.description: Saves the text as the reply draft of a received email, from the address the email was written to (a brand address or the mailbox). needsIdentity: that address cannot send until the user verifies it in BumbleBox. Nothing is sent: the draft waits in BumbleBox (Pilotage › prepared replies) until the user reviews it and clicks Send. Saving again replaces the previous draft of the same email.

email_id.description: Email id, as returned by search_emails or list_to_answer.

body.description: Plain-text reply body.

ai.bumblebox/mail.name: send_reply
ai.bumblebox/mail.description: Replies to the sender of one received email, and only to them (no Cc, no Bcc, no attachment), from the address the email was written to. What happens next is the level the user set in BumbleBox for this kind of reply: a draft, a reply waiting for one tap (the default), or a reply that leaves after a delay the user can cancel. Anything that commits the user (amounts, bank details, acceptance, contracts, dates, links) always waits for the user, and so does a reply from an address the user has not verified (needsIdentity). The result says which one applied.

email_id.description: Email id, as returned by search_emails or list_to_answer.

body.description: Plain-text reply body.

ai.bumblebox/mail.name: archive_email
ai.bumblebox/mail.description: Moves one inbox email to its mailbox's archive folder, on the mail server too. Undone by restore_to_inbox. Nothing is deleted.

email_id.description: Email id, as returned by search_emails or list_to_answer.

ai.bumblebox/mail.name: move_email
ai.bumblebox/mail.description: Moves one inbox email to an existing folder of the same mailbox (see list_folders), on the mail server too. No folder is created. Undone by restore_to_inbox.

email_id.description: Email id, as returned by search_emails or list_to_answer.

ai.bumblebox/mail.name: trash_email
ai.bumblebox/mail.description: Moves one email to its mailbox's trash. In the inbox: only when BumbleBox certifies it as noise (spam, newsletter, promotion, unanimous safety vote, no known contact or action word). Already filed out of the inbox (Notifications, Newsletters, archive…): when it is noise, a notification or an automated alert, with no known contact or action word. Any other email is not moved: it becomes a proposal the user confirms in one tap in BumbleBox. Never a permanent deletion; undone by restore_to_inbox.

email_id.description: Email id, as returned by search_emails or list_to_answer.

reason.description: Why, shown to the user with a proposal.

ai.bumblebox/mail.name: clean_filed_mail
ai.bumblebox/mail.description: Moves to the trash every email of one sender (an address, or @domain for a whole domain) that is already filed out of the inbox, in every connected mailbox, when it is noise, a notification or an automated alert. Because the sender is named, action words and known-contact status do not keep a mail; a protected category (a real conversation, a transaction, a legal notice) or a mail the user reclassified by hand still stays. The inbox is never touched, nor a mail the server still shows in the inbox. Returns how many were trashed, which were kept and why, how many are still in the inbox and how many were not found on the server. Never a permanent deletion; each email is undone by restore_to_inbox.

sender.description: An email address, or @domain.com for every address of that domain.

folder.description: Only the mail filed in this folder (see list_folders).

ai.bumblebox/mail.name: restore_to_inbox
ai.bumblebox/mail.description: Moves an archived, filed or trashed email back to the inbox, on the mail server too.

email_id.description: Email id, as returned by search_emails or list_to_answer.

ai.bumblebox/mail.name: list_missions

mission_id.description: Campaign id, as returned by list_missions.

ai.bumblebox/mail.name: update_campaign_draft
ai.bumblebox/mail.description: Changes the subject, body or recipient of a draft that is still a draft. Nothing is sent, and a draft the user already validated cannot be changed.

mission_id.description: Campaign id, as returned by list_missions.

ai.bumit/verify-business.name: verify_business
ai.bumit/verify-business.description: Verify a Swiss company using official commercial-register data (Zefix), SECO sanctions data, and FINMA authorisation data. Search by UID or company name (optionally narrowed by address); a UID is not required. Returns structured verification outcomes, source provenance, and data freshness. If a name matches multiple companies, returns candidates for the agent or user to disambiguate; never assume a partial match is the intended company. Unavailable evidence must not be interpreted as a failed verification.

inputSchema.description: Identify a Swiss company by uid or name; supply at least one of them. A uid is not required when a name is given. address is optional and only assists; address alone is not supported (result outcome UNSUPPORTED). If uid is given, it identifies the company and a supplied name is checked against the registered name. Only uid, name and address are accepted.

uid.description: Optional Swiss UID, canonical (CHE-123.456.789) or compact (CHE123456789); a trailing official supplement as printed on invoices and legal notices (MWST, TVA, IVA, VAT, HR, RC) is accepted and ignored. When present it identifies the company directly. Check digit validated server-side; an invalid UID is rejected before any source lookup.

name.description: Optional company legal name; use it when no UID is known. Name-only resolution needs at least 3 characters. A company is resolved only on a unique exact normalized legal-name match — never fuzzy. Otherwise candidates are returned for explicit selection: do not guess; resubmit with the chosen candidate's uid. With uid, the name is compared against the registered name instead.

address.description: Optional Swiss postal address; all four fields are required when address is supplied. It is checked against the official building-address directory (this never proves the company is at that address). With name, locality may narrow several exact legal-name matches by registered seat; it never turns a non-exact match into an identity. Address alone cannot identify a company.

locality.description: Locality (town). Also compared with the registered seat when narrowing exact name matches.

ai.bumit/verify-business.name: search_companies
ai.bumit/verify-business.description: Search the Swiss commercial register (Zefix) by company name and receive bounded, deduplicated candidate summaries (UID, legal name, legal form, register status, seat, canton) with source attribution. Use this to find a company's UID before calling get_company_profile, or to review candidates after verify_business reports an ambiguous name. Discovery only: no candidate is selected automatically, results are not ranked or scored, and a name match is not a verification result. For direct one-call verification, use verify_business.

inputSchema.description: Search the Swiss commercial register (Zefix) by company name. Discovery only: returns bounded register candidates; nothing is selected, ranked or verified.

name.description: Company name to search for. Trimmed; 3–300 characters. Do not guess spellings; use the name as claimed.

ai.bumit/verify-business.name: get_company_profile
ai.bumit/verify-business.description: Retrieve the canonical Swiss commercial-register (Zefix) profile for one company by UID: legal name, legal form, register status, seat, canton, registered address, purpose and official register links, with provenance, attribution and a freshness envelope (evidence age, freshness threshold, stale flag and source state). The UID is normalized and its check digit validated before any source request. FOUND means a register record was retrieved, not that the business passed verification. For sanctions, FINMA and full verification outcomes, use verify_business.

inputSchema.description: Retrieve the canonical Swiss commercial-register (Zefix) profile for one company by UID. Retrieval only: FOUND means a register record was retrieved, not that the business passed verification.

uid.description: Swiss UID (e.g. CHE-116.281.549). Formatting is normalized and a trailing official supplement (MWST, TVA, IVA, VAT, HR, RC) is accepted and ignored; the mod-11 check digit is validated before any source request.
